94.1: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. My mind has come to love the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and the Lord himself. By great good fortune I have meditated on the Lord's Name. Through the perfect Guru I have gained this attainment of the Lord's Name; rare is the one who walks by the Guru's teaching. I have tied (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, into the corner of my cloth as spending-money (for life's journey). It is the companion of my life-breath, and goes with me always. The perfect Guru has made the Lord's Name firm (within me); the Lord's wealth, unshakable, is (now) in my lap. The Lord, Har Har, is my friend, my beloved, my King. If only someone would bring him and unite me with him, the one who gives life to my breath. O Beloved, I cannot live without seeing you; tears stream and keep streaming (from my eyes). The True Guru is my friend, the companion of my childhood. I cannot live without seeing him, O my mother. Dear Lord, show your grace and unite me with the Guru, that servant Nanak may have the Lord's wealth in his lap. ॥4॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
94.2: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Madhusudan (the Lord) is my mind, my body and my life-breath. I know no other, none but the Lord. If only, by great good fortune, some friend, a Sant, would meet me and point me to my beloved Lord God. I search my mind and body; I seek, and have others seek, (asking) how I may meet my dear Beloved, O my mother. Joining the Sat Sangat, I ask for news of his trail; it is in the Sangat that the Lord God dwells. My dear Beloved, the True Guru, is my protector. We are (your) helpless children: cherish and sustain us. My mother and father are the Guru, the perfect True Guru; meeting the water that is the Guru, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms. Without seeing the Guru, sleep does not come to me. Separation from the Guru brings pain to my mind and body. O Lord, Har Har, be merciful and unite me with the Guru; meeting the Guru, servant Nanak blossoms with joy. ॥4॥
Madhusudan (the slayer of the demon Madhu): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God.
95.1: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Let us read of the Lord's virtues, let us reflect on the Lord's virtues; let us listen every day to the telling of the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Gathered in the Sat Sangat and singing the Lord's virtues, one crosses the world, the terrible ocean so hard to cross. Come, my companion, let us bring about our union with the Lord. Whoever brings me word of my Beloved, and shows me the way to the Lord, Narhari, is my friend, my companion, my dear one, my brother. The perfect Guru, one with the Lord, knows my pain: I cannot live without uttering the Name. O perfect Guru, give me the medicine, the mantra (of the Name); it is through the Name of the Lord, Har Har, that I can be saved. We are humble chatriks, in the refuge of the True Guru; (he) has put the drop of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, into our mouths. The Lord is the ocean, and we are the fish of its water; O servant Nanak, without the water we die. ॥4॥
Narhari (nar, man; hari, lion): Narasimha, the Man-Lion in whose form, in the Puranas, God saved Prahlad; in Gurbani, a name of God.
95.2: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O holy servants of the Lord, my brothers, come and meet me. Show me the way to my Lord God; a hunger (for him) has seized me. O Life of the world, O Giver, fulfil my longing: that, meeting the Lord, my mind may be drenched in the sight of him. May I join the Sat Sang and speak the Lord's Bani; the telling of the Lord, Har Har, has won my mind. The Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, is dear to my mind; it is in meeting the True Guru that the Amrit is drunk. The fortunate find the Lord's Sangat; the unfortunate, lost in doubt, suffer blows. Without good fortune the Sat Sang is not found; without the Sangat, (the mind) is filled with filth. Come and meet me, O beloved Life of the world. Holding mercy in your heart, (grant me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Through the Guru's teaching the Name has grown sweet and dear to the mind; O servant Nanak, the mind is drenched in the Name. ॥4॥
95.3: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). From the Guru I have received knowledge of the Lord; I have found the Lord's sweet essence, I have found the Lord. My mind is dyed in the Lord's love; (the Guru) has given me the Lord's essence to drink. With my mouth I utter the Name of the Lord, Har Har, I speak Har Har; my mind brims over and over with the Lord's essence. Come, O Sants, and take me into your embrace; tell me the story of my Beloved. O Sants of the Lord, meet me; to the one who speaks the Gurbani with his mouth, I would give my mind. By great good fortune the Lord has brought me to meet the Sant (the Guru); the perfect Guru has put the Lord's essence into my mouth. The unfortunate have not found the True Guru; the manmukh falls again and again into the womb, into birth after birth. God, the Merciful, has himself shown mercy, (and) done away with all the filth of Haumai and of Maya's poison. O Nanak, it is in the shops and the town of the body that the Gurmukhs purchase the Lord's goods. ॥4॥
95.4: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). May I meditate on the virtues of Govind, on the Name of the Lord; may I join the Sangat and enshrine the Naam in my mind. O Lord God, inaccessible Master beyond the reach of the senses: it is in meeting the True Guru that the Lord's essence is enjoyed. Blessed, blessed are the Lord's servants who have known the Lord God. May I go and ask those servants about the Lord; may I massage their feet and wash them, rubbing them clean; meeting the Lord's servants, the Lord's essence is drunk. The True Guru, the Giver, has made the Naam firm (within me); by great good fortune I have had the sight of the Guru. I utter the essence of Amrit, the true Amrit (of the Name); it is from the perfect Guru that the Amrit is received. O Lord, unite me with the Sat Sangat, with the True Being (the Guru); it is in joining the Sat Sangat that the Lord's Name is meditated on. Nanak says: may I hear the telling of the Lord and utter it with my mouth; through the Guru's teaching (the mind) is absorbed in the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
96.1: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Come, my sisters, my dear ones, and meet me. To the one who shows me my Beloved, I am a sacrifice. Joining the Sat Sangat, I have found the Lord, my friend; to the True Guru I am a sacrifice. Wherever my eyes fall, the Master is there. You pervade every heart, (O Lord), you who know what is within. The perfect Guru has shown me the Lord right beside me; I am ever a sacrifice to the True Guru. One is the air (in all), all the clay is one, and one light is in each and all. One light is at work in all, (yet in each it works) apart and distinct; no one can blend (these differences) into one. (Yet) by the Guru's grace the One has come into my sight; I am offered up to the True Guru. Servant Nanak speaks the Bani that is Amrit; it is dear to the minds of the Guru's Sikhs, it pleases them. The Guru, the perfect True Guru, gives the teaching; the Guru, the True Guru, does good to others. Seven Chaupade of the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
96.2: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My mind longs for the sight of the Guru; it cries out like the chatrik. Its thirst is not quenched, nor does peace come, without the sight of the dear Sant. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to the sight of the Guru, the dear Sant. Your face is beautiful, and your word stirs the melody of Sahaj. It is long since I saw you, O Saringpani. Blessed is the land where you dwell, O my friend, my companion, O Murari. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to the Guru, my friend, my companion, Murari. When I did not meet you for a single ghari, it was Kalyug (the dark age) for me. When now shall I meet you, my beloved, blessed Lord? My night does not pass, nor does sleep come, without seeing the Guru's court. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to that true court of the Guru. Good fortune has come to me: the Guru has brought me to meet the Sant (God, the source of peace); I have found the imperishable God within my own home (the heart). Servant Nanak says: may I serve your servants, and not be parted (from them) for a moment, not for an instant. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to your servants, says servant Nanak. ॥1॥
97.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Beautiful is the season in which I hold you in my heart; sweet is the work that I toil at for you; at peace is the heart in which you have come to dwell, O Giver of all. You are the Master and Father we all share; yours are the nine treasures, your storehouses never run out. The one to whom you give (your gift) is filled and satisfied; that one alone is your devotee. Everyone sits in hope of you; within each and every heart you alone dwell. All are called your partners; you are seen to be outside of no one. You yourself, through the Guru, bring (beings) to liberation; you yourself make (them) self-willed and send them wandering through births. Nanak, your slave, is a sacrifice to you; all this is your play, plain to see. ॥4॥
97.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The unstruck melody resounds (within me); in Sahaj (the mind) is at ease. Through the Shabad it ever delights in bliss and play. In the cave of Sahaj it has sunk into deep absorption, and set its seat on high. After roaming about, (the mind) has come back to its own home; what it sought, that it has found. It is filled and satisfied, O Sants; through inner experience the Guru has shown (me) the all-pervading Being. He himself is the king, he himself the people; he himself is free of all desire, he himself the enjoyer. He himself, the True Judge, sits on the throne; all cries of complaint have come to an end. As I have seen (him), so have I spoken. The one who has grasped the secret has come to relish it. (That one's) light has merged into the Light, and found peace; O servant Nanak, it is the One who has spread out (all this). ॥4॥
97.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the home (of the heart) where the Husband has brought the joy of wedded life, in that home, O companion, songs of joy are sung. Joy and delight grace the home of that bride whom the Husband has adorned. She is virtuous, she is fortunate, blessed with sons, gentle in nature, a happy wedded wife; beautiful, skilled and wise is the bride who is dear to her Husband. She alone is upright in conduct, she alone is foremost; through her knowing (the Husband) every adornment becomes her. She is of noble family, she is blessed with brothers, the bride made beautiful by the Husband's love. Her glory cannot be told, she whom the Husband has united with himself and held close to his side. Her wedded life is lasting, her Groom inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses; O servant Nanak, love is her support. ॥4॥
Sabhraaee (sa, with; bhraa, brother): a bride with brothers, and so held in honour in her husband's home.
98.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Searching and searching, (many) long for the sight (of God); in many ways they roam through forest after forest. My Lord, Har Har, is Nirgun (beyond all qualities) and Sargun (manifest in all qualities); is there anyone who would bring him and unite me with him? (Some) study the six Shastras and speak words of knowledge; (some do) worship, wear the frontal mark and bathe at places of pilgrimage; (some practise) the nivli cleansing and the eighty-four postures; but through these peace does not come. For many years (they) have chanted and practised austerities; they have travelled, wandering over the earth; (yet) not for a moment does peace come to the heart; the yogi gets up and runs off again and again. In his grace (God) has brought me to meet the Saadh (the holy Guru); my mind and body are cooled, and I have found steadiness. The imperishable God has come to live within (my) heart; Nanak sings the Lord's songs of joy. ॥4॥
Nivli: a hatha yoga practice in which the belly muscles are rolled to cleanse the bowels; the eighty-four postures (asanas) are the sitting postures of hatha yoga.
98.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Supreme Lord is beyond the farthest beyond, the radiant Divine One; he is inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses, unseen, and no one knows his secret. He is merciful to the meek, Gopal, Gobind: meditate through the Guru on that Lord, who grants liberation. Through the Guru, Madhusudan carries (beings) across; through the Guru, Krishna, Murari, becomes (one's) companion. The merciful Damodar is found through the Guru, and in no other way at all. Keshav needs no food and bears enmity to none; millions of his servants worship his feet. The one in whose heart, through the Guru, the Lord, Har Har, dwells is the devotee of the One alone. The sight of him never fails to bear fruit; he is endless and boundless, great in power, ever the Giver. When the Naam is repeated through the Guru, by it one crosses over (the world-ocean); O Nanak, few have come to know this state. ॥4॥
Damodar (he whose waist was bound with a cord: the child Krishna) and Keshav (of the long, beautiful hair) are names of Vishnu and Krishna in the Puranas; in Gurbani they are names of the one God.
98.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), what you command is what is done, and what you give is what is received. The poor and the helpless rely on you alone. You alone, you alone are everything, my beloved; I am a sacrifice to your power. By (your) will (one) strays into the wilds, by (your) will (one) keeps to the path; by (your) will, through the Guru, (some) sing the Lord's praises; by (your) will (one) wanders in doubt through many births: everything is in his will. No one is a fool, and no one is wise (of himself); in all things it is your will that is at work. O inaccessible (Lord), beyond the reach of the senses, endless and unfathomable, your worth cannot be told. Grant (me) the dust of the Sants' feet, O beloved; O Lord, I have come and fallen at your door. Beholding (the Sants), the mind is satisfied; O Nanak, (then) union (with the Lord) comes with ease. ॥4॥
98.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Sorrow comes only when (the Lord) is forgotten; (then) hunger (for Maya) takes hold, and (one) runs about in many ways. Remembering the Naam, that one is ever at peace to whom (the Lord), merciful to the meek, gives (it). My True Guru is mighty indeed; when I cherish (him) in my heart, all sorrow is lifted. The disease of anxiety and the pain of ego have gone; (the Lord) himself takes care of (me). Like a child, I ask (him) for everything; however much God gives, his gifts never run short. Falling at (your) feet again and again, I plead with (you) earnestly, O Gopal, merciful to the meek. I give myself in sacrifice to the perfect True Guru, who has cut away all my bonds. Placing the Naam in the heart, he has made (us) pure; in (the Lord's) love, Nanak has become a home of delight. ॥4॥
99.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O beloved, O Gopal, merciful and full of joy, deep and profound, endless Govind, lofty, unfathomable, endless Master: remembering (you) again and again, I live. O destroyer of sorrow, priceless treasure, fearless, without enmity, unfathomable, beyond all weighing, your form beyond time, unborn, self-existent: remembering (you) in my mind, I am cooled and at peace. Gopal, the Lord, is (our) companion for ever, (the giver of) all delights; he cherishes the high and the low (alike). The Naam is the home of all delights, and it satisfies the mind; through the Guru I drink (this) nectar. In sorrow and in joy, O beloved, I meditate on you; this sound understanding I have received from the Guru. You alone are Nanak's support, O Master; in the Lord's love I cross over (the world-ocean). ॥4॥
99.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Blessed is the moment in which I met the True Guru; fruitful is the sight of him: beholding (him) with my eyes, I have crossed over (the world-ocean). Blessed are those muhurats, chasas, moments and gharis; blessed are those times of meeting. Through striving, (my) mind has become pure; as I walk the Lord's path, all (my) doubt has been dispelled. The True Guru has let (me) hear the treasure of the Naam, and all (my) ailments are gone. (O Lord), within and without is your Word; you yourself have spoken it, and you yourself have expounded it. The Guru has said: everywhere is the One, the One alone; there will never be any other. From the Guru I have drunk the nectar of the Lord; the Lord has become (my) clothing, and the Naam (my) food. In the Naam are (my) joys, in the Naam (my) sport and play; Nanak has made the Naam (his) pleasures. ॥4॥
99.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). From all the Sants I ask for one thing; I make my plea and cast off (my) pride. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, lakhs of times: grant (me) the dust of the Sants' feet. (O Lord), you are the Giver, you the all-pervading Creator; you are all-powerful, ever the giver of peace. Everyone prospers by you alone: bring this opportunity of mine (the human life) to fulfilment. Those whose dwellings (their bodies) the sight of you has made holy are the ones who have conquered the hard fortress of the self. You are the Giver, you the all-pervading Creator; there is no other hero as great as you. The dust of the Sants' feet has touched my face; evil-mindedness has perished, and base understanding has fled. Settled in the true home, (I) sing (his) praises; O Nanak, falsehood has perished. ॥4॥
100.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Giver so great, never slip from (my) mind; show your grace, O (Lord) imbued with love for your devotees, that day and night I may meditate on you: grant me this gift. Into blind clay (the body) you have placed awareness; you have given everything, and good places (to dwell in). Joys, pleasures, wonders and shows: whatever pleases you comes to be. Everything we receive is his gift: the thirty-six kinds of ambrosial food we eat, the comfortable bed, the cool breeze, the play and delight we enjoy at ease. Give (me) that understanding by which you never slip from (my) mind; give (me) that wisdom by which I meditate on you. With every breath may I sing your praises; Nanak's shelter is the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
100.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). To praise you is (to accept) your Hukam, O Master of the will; that is knowledge and meditation which is pleasing to you. That alone is chanting which pleases God; (walking) in his will is perfect knowledge. Your ambrosial Naam is sung only by the one who is pleasing to your mind, O Master. You belong to the Sants, and the Sants are yours; O Master, (their) minds rest content in you. You cherish the Sants; the Sants play in your company, O Gopal. Your own Sants are most dear to you; you are the life-breath of the Sants. My mind is offered in sacrifice to those Sants who have come to know you and have found favour in your mind. In their company (I) have found peace for ever; with the Lord's nectar Nanak is filled and satisfied. ॥4॥
100.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), you are the ocean, and we are your fish; your Name is the raindrop, and we are thirsting chatriks. My hope is in you, my thirst is for you; my mind is absorbed in you alone. As a child is satisfied by drinking milk, as a pauper finds joy at the sight of wealth, (as) the thirsty one (is refreshed) drinking cool water, so is this mind drenched (in love) with the Lord. As a lamp gives light in the dark, (as a wife's) hope is fulfilled as she longs for her husband, as there is bliss in meeting the beloved, so is (my) mind dyed in the love of the Lord. The Sants have set me on the Lord's path; the merciful Saadh (the Guru) has made (me) at home with the Lord. The Lord is ours, and we are the Lord's servants; O Nanak, the Guru has given (us) the true Shabad. ॥4॥
100.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ever pure is the ambrosial Naam of the Lord, who gives peace and drives away pain. I have tasted and tried all other flavours; O mind, the Lord's essence is the sweetest of all. Whoever drinks (it) is satisfied; whoever obtains the essence of the Naam becomes immortal. The treasures of the Naam come to him alone in whose mind the Guru's Shabad has come to dwell. Whoever has found the Lord's essence is filled and satisfied; whoever has found the Lord's flavour does not waver. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, comes to him alone on whose forehead good fortune (is written). When the Lord comes into the hands of one, very many reap the benefit; clinging to that one, many are set free. The treasure of the Naam is found through the Guru; says Nanak, rare are those who have seen it. ॥4॥
101.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). For me the Lord, Har Har Har, is the treasures, the siddhis and the riches; by (the grace of) the deep and profound (Lord), this human birth is a precious gift. Whoever is attached to the Guru's feet enjoys lakhs and crores of joys and delights. Beholding (the Guru), (we) have become pure, and all (our) brothers and friends have been saved. By the Guru's grace I meditate on the True One, my own Master, inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses. The One whom all created beings seek is seen by a rare one, through great good fortune. Lofty, boundless and beyond the reach of the senses is (his) abode; that mansion the Guru reveals. O deep and profound (Lord), your Name is nectar; whoever has it dwelling in the heart is liberated. The Guru has cut away all their bonds; O servant Nanak, (they) remain absorbed in Sahaj. ॥4॥
101.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). It is by God's grace that I meditate on the Lord, Har Har; it is by God's mercy that I sing the song of (his) praise. Rising, sitting, sleeping and waking, let us meditate on the Lord all our life. The Saadh (the Guru) gave me the Naam as medicine; (my) sins are cut away, and (I) have become pure. Bliss has come, all pain has gone out, and every ache is destroyed. The one whose side my beloved takes is freed from the ocean of the world. Whoever has recognised the Guru, holding (him) true, why should he be afraid? Since I found the Saadh Sangat, on meeting the Guru, the curse of ego has gone. With every breath Nanak sings of the Lord; the True Guru has covered me and kept my honour. ॥4॥
101.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Like warp and weft, (the Lord) is woven into his servant. God, the giver of peace, protects and sustains the servant. I carry water, wave the fan and grind grain at the door of that servant whose striving is for the Master alone. Cutting away (his) noose, God has set (him) to (his) service; the Master's Hukam is dear to the servant's mind. He does only what pleases the Master; such a servant is wise, within and without. (O Lord), you are the all-knowing Master; you know every condition. The Master's servants revel in the joys of the Lord. Whatever is the Master's becomes the servant's; it is through being with the Master alone that the servant becomes known. The one whom his own Master has robed in honour is never again summoned to give account. Nanak is a sacrifice to that servant; he is a pearl, deep and profound. ॥4॥
102.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Everything is within the home (of the heart); nothing is outside. Whoever searches outside wanders astray in doubt. Those who by the Guru's grace have found (him) within are at peace, within and without. In a gentle patter the stream of Amrit rains down; the mind drinks it, hearing the Shabad and reflecting (on it). Day and night it rejoices in bliss and delight; for ever and ever it sports with the Lord. The one parted for birth after birth has met (the Lord); by the grace of the Saadh (the Guru), what was dry has turned green. Receiving good understanding, one meditates on the Naam; through the Guru the union comes about. As a wave of water merges into the water itself, so (the Lord) has merged (that one's) light with the Light. Says Nanak, the doors of doubt have been cut down; one no longer wanders away (from him). ॥4॥
102.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), I am a sacrifice to the one who has heard you (your Name); I am devoted to the one who has uttered (you) with the tongue. Over and over I give myself up to the one who worships you with mind and body. Let me wash the feet of the one who walks on your path; let me look with my own eyes on that kind person; let me give my mind to that friend of mine who has found that God by meeting the Guru. Fortunate are they who have known you; in the midst of all, they remain untouched and free of desire. In the Saadh's company such a one has crossed the fearsome world-ocean; such a one has subdued all the (inner) foes. My mind has come into their refuge, having given up pride, (reliance on its own) strength and the darkness of attachment. Grant Nanak the gift of the Name of that God, beyond reach and beyond all depth. ॥4॥
ਸੇ and ਨਿਰਬਾਣੇ are plural: those who stay untouched in the midst of all are the fortunate ones who have known God.
102.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), you are the tree, and the branch that has spread and flowered is yours. You, the subtle (unseen), have become the gross (the visible world). You are the ocean, you the foam and the bubble; apart from you, no other is found. You are the thread (of the mala), and the beads too are you; you are the knot, and you the meru, the head bead set above (them all). In the beginning, the middle and the end, it is God alone; no other is to be seen. You are nirgun (beyond Maya's three qualities) and sargun (the world made of them), the giver of peace; you are free of all desire, and you are the enjoyer, dyed in the colour (of the world's delights). You alone know your own works; you yourself take care (of all). You are the Master, and again you yourself the servant; O God, you yourself are hidden, and you yourself are manifest. Servant Nanak ever sings (your) praises; even for a moment, behold (him) with your glance of grace. ॥4॥
The meru is the head bead of a mala (a string of prayer beads), set above the others where the thread is knotted.
103.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Fruitful is that Bani through which the Naam is uttered; by the Guru's grace, only some rare one has come to know it. Blessed is the hour in which the Lord's (praise) is sung and heard; those who have come (into the world) and (sing and hear it) are accepted. Accepted are the eyes that have beheld the sight (of the Lord); good are the hands that have written the Lord's praise; beautiful are the feet that have walked on the Lord's path. I am a sacrifice to them; in their company I recognise (the Lord). Listen, my friend, my dear companion: in the Saadh Sangat one is saved in an instant. Sins are cut away, the mind becomes pure, and coming and going (birth and death) is ended. Joining both hands, let us make one prayer: (O God), in your grace, take hold of (this) sinking stone. To Nanak God has been merciful, and in Nanak's mind God has become dear. ॥4॥
103.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Lord, Har Har, your Bani is Amrit; hearing it again and again, I reach the supreme state. The burning (within) is quenched and the mind has grown cool, on receiving the sight of the True Guru. Peace has come, and pain has fled far away, since the tongue of the Sant (the Guru) has uttered the Lord's Name. Water and land are filled with water, the pools brimming; no one goes away empty. That Creator has shown mercy and cherished all beings and creatures. He is kind, gracious and compassionate; all are filled and wholly content. He has made the forests, the blades of grass and the three worlds green; the Maker did (this) within a moment. O Nanak, whoever worships him through the Guru, (God) fulfils the hope of that one's mind. ॥4॥
103.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), you are my father, you are my mother; you are my kinsman, you are my brother. In every place you are my protector; so what fear, what worry, can there be? It is by your grace that I have come to know you. You are my shelter, you alone my pride. Without you there is no other at all; all this is your play, your arena. All beings and creatures were made by you; to whatever task it pleased you, to that you have set each one. Everything that happens is your doing; nothing is of our doing. By meditating on the Naam I have obtained great peace; singing the Lord's praises, my mind has grown cool. Through the Perfect Guru the drums of rejoicing have sounded; Nanak has won the hard bout in the arena. ॥4॥
The akhara is the wrestling arena; bikhara (bikham akhara) is the hard bout. Drums of rejoicing sound for the victor.
103.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). God is the support of soul, breath and mind; singing the praises of the Infinite, the devotees live. The Lord's Name is Amrit, the treasure of virtues; meditating and meditating on the Lord, (they) have found peace. Whoever leaves home with longing in the heart (and comes to the holy company) ends birth and death in the Saadh Sangat. Hope and heart's aim are fulfilled on meeting the Guru and beholding him. No measure at all of the Unreachable, the Imperceptible, has been known, (though) seekers, Siddhas and men of knowledge meditate (on him). Self-conceit is erased and delusion is ended: the Guru has revealed (the Lord) within the mind itself. The treasures of bliss, joy and well-being, peace and Sahaj are for the one who has uttered the Lord's Name. Our own Master has become merciful, O Nanak, and the Name has come into the home (of the heart). ॥4॥
104.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O Lord), hearing and hearing of your glory, I live. You are (my) Beloved, the Master, exceedingly great. Your doings you alone know; your shelter (is mine), O Gopal. Singing (your) praises, the mind turns green; hearing (your) story, all its filth is washed away. Joining the company of the Saadhs and Sants, I ever repeat (the Name of) the Merciful One. With every breath I keep my God in mind; by the Guru's grace I hold this understanding in my mind. By your grace the light (within) dawns; in your mercy you sustain all. That God is true, true, true (ever abiding); always, always, for ever, he himself alone exists. Your wonders are plain to see, O Beloved; seeing them, Nanak is filled with joy. ॥4॥
In ਗੋੁਪਾਲਾ the letter ਗ carries two vowel signs (ੋ and ੁ); it is read gupaalaa, to keep the metre of the line.
104.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By (the Lord's) Hukam the rains have begun to fall; friends and Sants meet together and repeat the Naam. Cooling peace and the bliss of Sahaj are found; God himself has brought coolness. He has brought forth everything in great abundance; God, in his grace, has filled all to contentment. O my Giver, you bestow your gifts, and all beings and creatures are filled. True is the Master, true his glory; through the Guru's grace I meditate on him always. The fears of birth and death, and attachment, are cut away; sorrow and torment are destroyed. With every breath Nanak praises (him); remembering the Naam, all the nooses are cut. In an instant (God) has fulfilled the hope, as the praises of the Lord, Har Har Har, are repeated. ॥4॥
104.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Come, friends, Sants, dear companions: let us meet and sing the praises of the Unreachable, the Infinite. By singing and hearing (them), all are set free; let us meditate on him who made us. The sins of birth after birth depart, and (they) obtain the very fruits their minds have longed for. Remember that Master, the True Lord, who gives every one their sustenance. Repeating the Naam, every comfort is found; all fear is destroyed when the Lord, Har Har, is meditated on. Whoever has served (him) crosses to the far shore; all (that one's) tasks are accomplished. (O Lord), I have come and fallen into your refuge; as it pleases you, so unite (me with you). In your grace, O God, join (me) to your devotion, that Nanak may drink the Amrit of the True (Name). ॥4॥
105.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Govind, the Lord of the world, has become merciful; the cloud rains on every place. Kind to the lowly, ever gracious, the Creator has brought coolness. He cherishes his own beings and creatures, as a mother looks after her children. The Master, who shatters pain, the ocean of comfort, gives food to all. The Merciful One pervades water and land; let us ever be a sacrifice, an offering, to him. Night and day I meditate on him always, who saves all in an instant. God himself has saved all; all sorrow and torment are gone. Repeating the Naam, mind and body turn green; O God, look upon Nanak with your glance of grace. ॥4॥
105.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Where the Name of the beloved God is repeated, those places, (however bare), are golden mansions. Where (your) Name is not repeated, O my Govind, those very towns are a wilderness. The one who eats dry bread and (yet) keeps the Lord in (his) heart: on him the Lord looks with grace, within and without. The one who eats and eats and does evil deeds: know him as a garden of poison. The one who forms no love for the Sants and commits misdeeds in the company of the Saakats: that ignorant one has wasted the rare (human) body, and torn up his own root himself. My (Lord), merciful to the meek, I am in your refuge; O Ocean of peace, my Guru, my Gopal. Show mercy, that Nanak may sing (your) praises; keep our honour. ॥4॥
105.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Master's feet have come to rest in the heart, and all strife and suffering have gone far away. Peace, comfort and the strain of Sahaj have welled up, (as) one now dwells in the company of the Saadh (the Guru). The love that has taken hold (for the Lord) never breaks at all; the Lord fills all, within and without. Remembering, remembering, remembering (him), I sing (his) praises, and the noose of Jam has been cut. Amrit rains down through the unstruck Bani; peace has settled within mind and body. Your servants are fulfilled and wholly sated; the True Guru has given (them) comfort. From the One to whom (I) belonged, (I) have received the fruit; in his grace (the Guru) has united (me) with God. By great good fortune the comings and goings (of birth and death) have ended; O Nanak, (all) hopes are fulfilled. ॥4॥
105.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The rain has fallen: the Supreme God has sent it down; he has made all beings and creatures dwell in comfort. Distress has gone and lasting peace has come, as I cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har. He to whom they belong has himself sustained them; the Supreme Lord God has become (their) protector. My Master has heard (my) prayer, and (my) toil has come to full fruit. (God) is the Giver to all beings; by the Guru's grace, he has looked (on me) with his glance of grace. All (that lives) in water, on land and in the sky is sated; I wash the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). (He) fulfils the desire of the mind; I am a sacrifice (to him) for ever and ever. O Nanak, the Destroyer of pain has bestowed the gift (of the Name); (his servants) are dyed in the love of God, the source of all delight. ॥4॥
106.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Mind and body are yours, and wealth too is yours; you are my Master, my Lord, my God. Soul and body are all your capital; your power, O Gopal, is (my) strength. Forever and ever, you alone are the giver of peace; bowing low again and again, I fall at your feet. I would do (your) work, if by it I pleased you, when you grant it, O merciful Lord. God, all I receive is from you; you are my adornment. Whatever you give, that I bear as joy. Wherever you keep (me), there is Baikunth (heaven); you are the cherisher of all. O Nanak, (the one who) has found peace by remembering (you) again and again, and has sung your praises at all hours, has every longing fulfilled, and is never in sorrow. ॥4॥
106.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Supreme Lord God has sent the cloud; he has made it rain on water, land and sky, in all ten directions. Peace has come, all thirst is quenched, and there is joy in every place. (God) gives peace and destroys pain; of himself, in his grace, he takes care of (all) beings. He himself sustains what he has made; falling at (his) feet, I seek his favour alone. He in whose refuge the highest state is attained: on that Lord's Name let us meditate with every breath. Apart from him there is no other master; all places are his alone. You are my pride, God, and you are my strength; you are the True Master, fathomless in virtues. Servant Nanak makes this prayer: that I may meditate on you at all hours. ॥4॥
106.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). With God pleased, every comfort has come; the feet of the Perfect Guru have come to dwell in the mind. The samadhi of Sahaj has set in, and attention is fixed within; that delight only the one (in this state) knows. My Master is beyond reach, beyond the grasp of the senses; (yet) he is present, close at hand, within each and every heart. Ever untouched (by Maya), he is the Giver to all beings; rare is the one who recognises his own self. This is the sign of meeting God: in the mind one recognises the true Hukam of the One. In Sahaj and contentment (such people) stay ever fulfilled, and find bliss in the Master's will. God, the Giver, has given a palmful (of medicine), and cured all the diseases of birth and death. O Nanak, the servants God has made his own revel in the Lord's Kirtan (the singing of his praises). ॥4॥
Hathi: a palmful of medicine, as mothers place a dose of carom seed and the like on a child's palm.
107.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Gopal, the Lord of the world, has shown mercy; the Guru's feet now dwell in the mind. That Creator has accepted (me) as his own, and pulled down the camp of sorrow. In mind and body that True One himself has come to dwell; (now) no place seems hard (to pass). All foes and enemies have become friends, (since I) have longed for the one Master alone. Whatever (God) does, he does himself, of his own accord; no one's wit or cleverness is seen (to count) at all. He himself is the helper of his Sants; God has taken away (their) doubt and delusion. (God's) lotus feet are the support of his servant; at all hours the Name of Ram is (his) trade. In the bliss of Sahaj (his servants) sing Govind's praises; O Nanak, God pervades all. ॥4॥
107.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That is the true temple in which the True One is meditated on; that heart is at ease in which the Lord's praises are sung; that land is beautiful where the Lord's servants live; to the True Name I am a sacrifice. You are the True One; the worth of (your) greatness no one has found; (your) creation and (your) grace cannot be told. Your servants live by meditating (on you) again and again; the True Shabad is the mainstay of their minds. Only by great good fortune does one come to praise the True One; by the Guru's grace the Lord's praises are sung. Those steeped in your love please you; the True Name is the mark (of their approval). The True One's limit no one knows; in every place and the spaces between is that True One. O Nanak, let us ever meditate on the True One, the Knower of hearts, the All-wise. ॥4॥
107.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Lovely is the night, and the day passes in ease, (when) one repeats the nectar-like Name, in fellowship with the Sants. The gharis, muhurats and moments that pass in remembering (him): there life bears fruit. Remembering the Naam, all faults have been washed away; within and without, the Lord God is at (my) side. The Perfect Guru has driven out fear, dread and doubt; I see (him) in all places. God is all-powerful, great, lofty and infinite; the Naam is the nine treasures; (his) storehouses are full. In the beginning, the end and the middle there is God alone; I hold no other as his equal. Show mercy, my (Lord), merciful to the meek: (your) beggar begs for the dust of the feet of the Saadh (the Guru). Grant (this) gift, servant Nanak asks: that I may meditate on the Lord forever and ever. ॥4॥
107.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Here it is you alone, and hereafter you yourself; all beings and creatures are of your making. There is none other than you, O Creator; on you I lean, you are my shelter. (My) tongue lives by repeating (your Name) again and again, O Master, O Supreme Lord God, Knower of hearts. Whoever has served (you), he alone has found peace; he does not lose (his) life in a gamble. The servant of yours who has obtained the medicine of the Naam has rid (himself) of the disease of birth after birth. Sing the Lord's Kirtan day and night; this is the work that bears fruit. Casting his glance of grace, (God) has adorned his servant; (that servant) has bowed to the Supreme Lord within each and every heart. Without the One there is no other, O brother; O Nanak, this is the highest understanding. ॥4॥
108.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). For mind and body to be dyed in (the love of) the beloved Lord, let us offer up all we have as a sacrifice. At all hours let us sing Govind's praises; do not forget (him) for a single breath. He alone is a friend, a beloved companion, who reflects on the Name of Ram in the Saadh Sangat. In the company of the Saadh the (world-)ocean is crossed, and the noose of Jam is cut. The Lord's service is the four great gifts (padaarath); the Paarjat tree is the repeating (of the Name) of the Unseen, the Unfathomable. The Guru has cut away lust, anger and sins, and hope is fulfilled. The mortal whose fortune has come to fullness meets Saarangpaani, the Lord, in the Saadh Sangat. O Nanak, the one within whom the Naam has come to dwell is approved, be he householder or renunciant. ॥4॥
The four padaarath: dharam (righteousness), arth (wealth), kaam (fulfilment of desire) and mokh (liberation), held to be the four aims of life.
108.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering the Naam, peace has been found in the heart; in his grace, (God) has revealed (himself) to the devotees. Those who have joined the company of the Sants and repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, are rid of sloth and sickness. The Lord in whose house are the nine treasures, O brother, is met by the one who has the earnings of past (good deeds). (Such a one gains) knowledge of the Perfect, Supreme God and meditation on him; God is able to do all things. In an instant (God) can set up and pull down; he himself is alone, and himself the whole expanse (of the world). No stain (of Maya) clings to the Giver, the Life of the world; on seeing him, separations are lifted. Attaching it to (his) hem, he has carried the whole world across; he himself has (us) repeat his own Name. By (his) grace the ship of the Guru has been found; O Nanak, (this) union was ordained from the beginning. ॥4॥
108.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (A being) does only what (God) himself has it do. Wherever he keeps (us), that is a good place. That one alone is wise, that one is honoured, to whom (his) Hukam seems sweet. (He) has strung all (creation) on a single thread. The one he attaches (to himself) is attached to (his) feet. One whose inverted lotus (of the heart) has blossomed has seen the Immaculate (Lord) in all. You alone know your own greatness. You yourself recognise your own self. I am a sacrifice to those Sants of yours, each of whom has ground down lust, anger and greed. You are without enmity; your Sants are pure, and at the sight of them all sins are washed away. O Nanak, whoever lives by meditating on the Naam again and again: his doubt and stubborn fear are destroyed. ॥4॥
The inverted lotus: the heart turned away from God, like a lotus hanging upside down and closed; turned towards him, it opens as the lotus does.
109.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). If anyone asks only for what is false (and passing), it does not take him a moment to die. One who ever serves the Supreme Lord, having met the Guru, is to be called unshakable. One in whose mind loving devotion has taken hold, sings (God's) praises day and night, ever awake. The Master takes by the arm and unites (with himself) the one on whose forehead (this) share is written. The lotus feet (of the Lord) dwell in the devotees' minds; without the Supreme God, all are robbed. (They) ever long for the dust (of the feet) of the Sants; the Name of the True One is (their) ornament. Standing up and sitting down, let us sing (the praises of) the Lord, Har Har, remembering whom the eternal Husband is found. O God, be merciful to Nanak, (that he may) bear what you do. ॥4॥
109.2: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those who are dyed through the Shabad, all of them (living) in (your) Hukam, are called to the mansion of (your) True Court. O True One, my Master, merciful to the meek, (they) have won their minds over to the True One. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those made beautiful through the Shabad, who through the Guru's teaching enshrine in the mind the Amrit Name, ever the giver of peace. No one is mine; whose am I? The True Master, (pervading) the three worlds, is mine. Acting again and again in Haumai, multitudes pass away; having done wrong, they repent. One who recognises (his) Hukam speaks of the Lord's virtues; through the Guru's Shabad he carries the insignia (passport) of the Name. The account of all is taken at the True One's door; one made beautiful by the Name will be set free. The manmukh, gone astray, finds no place of rest; bound at Jam's door, he suffers blows. Without the Name no one is his companion or friend; those who meditate on the Naam are liberated. The Saakat, caught in falsehood, does not love the Truth; bound in duality, he comes and goes. No one erases the destiny written (by past deeds); through the Guru, liberation is won. In her parents' home (this world), she did not know her Husband; parted (from him) by falsehood, she weeps and wails aloud. Robbed by her faults, she does not reach (his) mansion; through virtue (her) faults are forgiven. She who, in her parents' home, has known the Beloved, understands through the Guru and reflects on the essence; she puts a stop to (her) coming and going, and merges in the True Name. Through the Guru one understands the One who is called the Indescribable; to the True Master only truth is pleasing. Nanak speaks the truth and prays: those who sing (his) praises meet the True One. ॥8॥

Hau vaari jeeo vaari: vaari is to be offered up in sacrifice; jeeo is the word of loving address (71.2), not the soul. In these ashtapadis the lines ending in -ania (vasaavania, suhaavania) mostly name those who do the act; in some lines the form reads as a plain verb.
109.3: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). When there is grace, (God) brings (one) to meet the True Guru; (then one) fixes the awareness on service and the mind on the Shabad. Killing Haumai, (such a one) has found lasting peace and cast off attachment to Maya. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, offered up to the True Guru, through whose teaching the light has dawned (within); day and night (I) sing the Lord's praises. When one searches one's body and mind, then one finds the Name, holds back the running (mind) and keeps it still, sings the Guru's Bani day and night, and in Sahaj performs devotion. Within this body is a wealth beyond counting; when, through the Guru, the True One is met, then I see (it). (Rising above) the nine doors, one is set free at the Tenth Gate, and makes the unstruck Shabad resound. True is the Master, true is his glory; by the Guru's grace (it) is enshrined in the mind. Day and night, ever dyed in (his) love, one gains understanding at the True One's door. (She who) did not know the worth of sin and of virtue, clinging to duality, has strayed in doubt; ignorant and blind, she does not know the way, and comes and goes again and again. Through serving the Guru, lasting peace has been found; Haumai and the sense of mine have been held in check. Through the Guru's teaching the darkness has gone, and the hard (adamantine) doors have been opened. (One who), killing Haumai, has enshrined (him) in the mind, and ever fixed the mind on the Guru's feet, by the Guru's grace is pure in mind and body, and meditates on the pure Name. Life and death are all in your hands; the one he forgives, he gives glory. O Nanak, meditate ever on the Naam; you will make birth and death worthy. ॥8॥
110.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). My God is pure, beyond reach, without limit; without scales he weighs the world. The one who becomes Gurmukh understands this; speaking (his) virtues, he merges in the Lord of virtues. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Lord's Name in the mind. Those attached to the True One stay awake day and night, and win honour at the True One's door. He himself hears and he himself sees; that person alone is accepted on whom he casts his glance of grace. The one he himself attaches is attached; through the Guru, (such ones) practise Truth. Whom he himself leads astray, where can he reach out (for support)? What is written from before cannot be erased. Those who have met the True Guru are fortunate; by perfect grace they are united (with him). In her parents' home the bride sleeps day and night; her Husband has forgotten her; for her faults she is cast off. Day and night she wanders ever wailing; without her Husband she finds no sleep. (She who) in her parents' home has known the Giver of peace, has killed Haumai and recognised (him) through the Guru's Shabad: her bed is lovely, she ever delights in her Husband, and makes Truth her adornment. He created the beings of the eighty-four lakh forms of life; on whom he casts his glance of grace, him he brings to the Guru. (His) servants, their sins cut away, are ever pure; at the True One's door the Name makes them beautiful. If he asks for the account, who can give it? Then reckoning (one's deeds) by twos and threes brings no peace. God, the True One, himself forgives; himself forgiving, he unites (them with himself). He himself does and himself has (all) done; through the perfect Guru's Shabad he unites (beings with himself). O Nanak, the one who receives the Naam receives glory; he himself unites (such a one) in union (with himself). ॥8॥
111.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The One himself moves about, hidden from sight. When, through the Guru, I see (him), then this mind is drenched (with love); giving up craving, I have found the peace of Sahaj, and enshrine the One in the mind. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who fix their minds on the One alone. Through the Guru's teaching their mind has come to (its) one home; they are dyed in the True One's colour. This world has gone astray; you yourself have led it astray. Forgetting the One, it is lured by another; day and night it wanders ever, lost in doubt; without the Name it suffers pain. Those who are dyed in the love of the Creator, the Ordainer of destinies, are known through the four ages, through service of the Guru. The one to whom he himself gives glory merges in the Lord's Name. In attachment to Maya, (the manmukh) does not remember the Lord; bound in Jam's city, he suffers pain. Blind and deaf, he sees nothing; the manmukhs are consumed in sin. Some are dyed in (your) love, whom you yourself have drawn into loving attention (to you); through loving devotion they are dear to your mind. They serve the True Guru, ever the giver of peace; (you) yourself fulfil all their wishes. O dear Lord, I am ever in your refuge; you yourself forgive and give glory. Jamkaal does not come near the one who meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Those who please the Lord are dyed (in his love) day and night; my God has joined them (to himself) and united them in union. O True One, they remain ever, ever in your refuge; you yourself give them the understanding of Truth. Those who have known the True One are merged in the True One; they sing the Lord's praises, speaking the Truth. O Nanak, those steeped in the Name are detached; they sit in deep absorption in their own home (within). ॥8॥
111.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who dies through the Shabad is known as truly dead (to self). Death does not crush him, pain does not torment him; his light, meeting the (Lord's) Light, is merged in it; hear, O mind, (such a one) merges in the True One. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who win glory through the Lord's Name, who, serving the True Guru, have fixed their minds on the True One, and through the Guru's teaching merge in Sahaj. Her body is frail, and she wears a flimsy garment; clinging to duality, she does not reach (his) mansion. Every day she wanders burning, day and night; without her Husband she suffers great pain. Neither body nor caste goes on ahead (to the world beyond); where the account is called for, there one is set free by practising Truth. Those who serve the True Guru are rich; here and hereafter they are merged in the Name. (She who) makes the fear (of God) and love her adornment, by the Guru's grace finds the mansion, (her true) home; every day, ever, day and night, she delights in (her Lord), and takes on a colour as fast as the madder's. The Husband dwells ever with all; by the Guru's grace some rare one beholds (him) with (his) eyes. My God is the highest of the high; in his mercy he himself unites (one with himself). This world sleeps in attachment to Maya; forgetting the Naam, it is ruined in the end. The One by whose will it sleeps awakens it; through the Guru's teaching understanding is won. One who drinks the Amrit sheds doubt; by the Guru's grace he attains liberation and the highest state. Steeped in devotion, ever detached, he kills his self and is united (with God). He himself creates and sets (beings) to their tasks; he himself brings sustenance to (the beings of) the eighty-four lakh forms of life. O Nanak, those who are dyed in the True One, meditating on the Naam, do the work that pleases him. ॥8॥
112.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Within (each body, God) has fashioned the diamond and the ruby (of his Name); through the Guru's Shabad, (the Gurmukh) has assayed it and had it assayed. Those who have Truth in their keeping speak Truth, and test by the touchstone of Truth alone. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Guru's Bani in the mind, who amid the black stain (anjan) of Maya have found the Immaculate (Lord), and merge (their) light in the Light. Within this body is a vast expanse (of Maya); the Name is immaculate, far beyond reach and without limit. The one who becomes Gurmukh obtains it; (God) himself forgives and unites (him with himself). (The one in whom) my Master makes the Truth firm, fixes the mind on the True One by the Guru's grace. The True One alone pervades every place; (such ones) merge in the True One alone. Carefree is my Beloved, the True One, the destroyer of sins and faults. With love and affection let us ever meditate (on him), and make devotion firm (within) in fear and love. O True One, true devotion to you (is received) if it pleases (you); he himself gives, and does not regret (giving). He is the one Giver of all beings; through the Shabad he slays (the ego) and gives life. O Lord, without you I have no one; O Lord, you alone I serve, and you I praise. Unite me with yourself, O True God; by (your) perfect grace you are found. To me there is no other like you; through your glance of grace the body finds fulfilment. Day and night, O Lord, you care for (all) and protect (them); through the Guru, (they) merge in Sahaj. To me no other is as great as you; you yourself created (the world), and you yourself take it back into yourself. You yourself make, break and adorn; O Nanak, through the Name (you) make (beings) beautiful. ॥8॥
113.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). He himself is the Enjoyer in all hearts; the Unseen pervades (all), beyond reach, without limit. Through the Guru's Shabad let us meditate on my Lord God; (those who do so) merge, in Sahaj, in the True One. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Guru's Shabad in the mind. When the Shabad is understood, then (one) wrestles with one's own mind, and, stilling desire, merges (in the Lord). The five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) are plundering the world; the blind manmukhs have no sense or awareness (of it). One who becomes Gurmukh guards his own home, and through the Shabad burns away the five enemies. Some, through the Guru, are ever dyed in the True One's love; in Sahaj they serve God, intoxicated (with love) day and night. Meeting the Beloved, they sing the praises of the True One, and win honour at the Lord's door. First, the One alone brought himself forth; second (comes) duality, (third) Maya of the three qualities; the fourth step, the high one, is the Gurmukh's: (there they) practise Truth, Truth alone. All is true if it pleases the True One; one who has known the True One merges in Sahaj. This is the Gurmukhs' way of life: they serve the True One, and go and merge in the True One. Apart from the True One there is no other at all; clinging to duality, the world wears itself out and dies. One who becomes Gurmukh knows the One alone, and serving the One finds peace. All beings and creatures are in your refuge; you yourself place the pieces (on the board of the world's chaupar) and see which are raw and which ripe. Day and night he himself has (beings) do (their) work; he himself joins (them) in union (with himself). You yourself unite (them), and, ever at hand, you watch over (all); he himself is fully present in all. O Nanak, he himself, all by himself, pervades (all); through the Guru, (this) understanding is gained. ॥8॥
The fourth step is the fourth state (turiya, 30.2).
In the game of chaupar the pieces move round the board to reach home; a piece that has reached home is ripe (pakki), one still out is raw (kachi).
113.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Guru's Amrit Bani is sweet; some rare Gurmukh has tasted (it) and seen. Light (dawns) within (him); he drinks the supreme essence, and at the True One's door makes the Shabad resound. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who fix their minds on the Guru's feet. The True Guru is a true pool of Amrit; (those whose) mind bathes (in it) wash away (their) filth. O True One, no one has found your limit; by the Guru's grace some rare one has fixed the mind (on you). Praising you, I am never sated; a hunger for the True Name stays with me. I see the One alone, no other; by the Guru's grace I have drunk Amrit. Through the Guru's Shabad I have quenched (my) thirst, and in Sahaj I am merged in peace. (The manmukh) gives up the priceless jewel for straw; the blind manmukh clings to the love of another. Whatever he sows, that fruit he reaps; not even in a dream does he find peace. The one on whom (God) shows his grace, that person finds (him), (and) enshrines the Guru's Shabad in the mind. Day and night he ever lives in the fear (of God); killing (all other) fears, he casts off doubt. He has cast off doubt and found lasting peace; by the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state. Pure is (his) heart, pure (his) speech; in Sahaj he sings the Lord's praises. (The pandit) expounds the Simritis, the Shastras and the Vedas, (but), lost in doubt, he does not know the essence. Without serving the True Guru he finds no peace, and earns pain upon pain. He (the Lord) himself does (all); to whom can anyone speak? One would go to speak (to him) only if he erred. O Nanak, he himself does and has (all) done; through the Name, (beings) merge in the Name. ॥8॥
114.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). God himself dyes (beings), in Sahaj and in love; through the Guru's Shabad he applies the colour of the Lord's (Name). (Their) mind and body are dyed, the tongue deep red with (that) colour; through fear and love (of God) this colour is applied. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Fearless (Lord) in the mind. By the Guru's grace they have meditated on the Fearless Lord, and through the Shabad (he) carries (them) across the poisonous world-ocean. The foolish manmukhs act clever; though bathed and washed, (the manmukh) is not accepted (at the Lord's door). As he came, so he will go; having done wrong, he repents. The blind manmukh understands nothing; he does not grasp that (all) have come with death written (in their lot). The manmukh performs (ritual) deeds but does not find (the Lord); without the Name he wastes (his) life. (Remembering) the Truth (alone) is the deed to do, the Shabad (alone) is the essence; through the perfect Guru the door of liberation is found. Day and night (the Guru) recites the Bani through the Shabad; (those who hear it) are steeped in the True One and dyed in (his) love. (One whose) tongue, filled with love, is steeped in the Lord's taste, (his) mind and body are enraptured, in Sahaj and in love; in Sahaj he has found the dear Beloved, and with ease he is united in Sahaj. One within whom is love sings (God's) praises; through the Guru's Shabad he merges with ease in peace. I am ever a sacrifice to those who fix their minds on the Guru's service. The True One, Truth itself, is won over by truth alone; by the Guru's grace, (those whose) heart is drenched (in love), sit in the blessed place (within) and sing the Lord's praises; (God) himself makes (them) accept (this) as true. The one on whom he casts his glance of grace finds (him); by the Guru's grace (his) Haumai departs. O Nanak, the Naam dwells in (his) mind, and he wins honour at the True One's door. ॥8॥
114.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). By serving the True Guru, great glory (is won): the dear Lord, free of care, comes and dwells in the mind. The dear Lord is a fruit-bearing tree (whose juice) is Amrit; whoever has drunk it, his thirst is quenched. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the True One, who brings (beings) into the Sangat and unites (them with himself). The Lord himself brings (beings) into the Sat Sangat; (there,) through the Guru's Shabad, they sing the Lord's praises. I serve the True Guru, who has made (my life) beautiful through the Shabad, who has enshrined the Lord's Name in (my) mind. The pure Lord takes away the filth of Haumai; (such ones) win honour at the True One's door. The Name is not found without the Guru; the Siddhas and seekers were left wailing (for it). Without serving the Guru there is no peace; the Guru is found by perfect destiny. This mind is a mirror; some Gurmukh (alone) sees (himself in it). No rust clings (to it) when he dries up Haumai. He makes the unstruck Bani, the pure Shabad, resound (within); through the Guru's Shabad he merges in the True One. Without the True Guru, (the Lord) is not to be seen at all; the Guru, in his grace, has revealed (the Lord's) own self. He himself, himself alone, is blended (in all); (one who sees this) merges with ease in Sahaj. One who becomes Gurmukh fixes loving attention on the One alone; he burns away the doubt of duality through the Guru's Shabad. Within the body he trades and deals, and finds the true treasure of the Naam. The Gurmukh's deed is the Lord's praise, the most excellent (of deeds); through the Guru, (he) finds the door of liberation. Day and night, dyed in (God's) love, he sings (his) praises, and is called into the mansion (of the Lord). The True Guru, the Giver, is met when (God himself) brings about the meeting; by perfect destiny (one) has enshrined the Shabad in the mind. O Nanak, (such a one) receives the glory that is the Naam, and sings the praises of the True Lord. ॥8॥
115.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). If one sheds the self, then one gains everything; through the Guru's Shabad one fixes true loving attention (on the Lord). (Such ones) trade in Truth, gather Truth, and deal in Truth alone. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who sing the Lord's praises day and night. I am yours, you are my Master; through the Shabad you give glory. Lovely are all the hours and moments, in which the True One is dear to my mind. Serving the True One, true glory (is won); by the Guru's grace the True One is found. When the True Guru is pleased, (one) receives the food of love; the taste for other things ends, and (one) enshrines the Lord's taste in the mind. Truth, contentment and the peace of Sahaj are received from the perfect Guru through (his) Bani. Those who do not serve the True Guru are fools, blind and ignorant; how then will they find the door of liberation? Dying again and again they are born, again and again they come; at Jam's door they suffer blows. When (people) know the taste of the Shabad, then they recognise their own selves, and through the Shabad they utter the pure Bani. Serving the True One they ever find peace, and enshrine in the mind the Naam, (which is) the nine treasures. Lovely is the place that has pleased the Lord's mind, where, sitting in the Sat Sangat, (his devotees) have sung the Lord's praises. Day and night they praise the True Lord, and make the pure melody (of his praise) resound. The manmukhs' capital is counterfeit, and counterfeit is their show; they practise falsehood and suffer heavy pain. Lost in doubt they wander day and night; dying and being born, they waste (their) life. The True Master is very dear to me; through the perfect Guru's Shabad (he is my) support. O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (such ones) know pain and pleasure as one. ॥8॥
116.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (O God,) yours are the sources of life, yours the tongues (that beings speak); without the Name, all (creation) strays in doubt. Through service of the Guru the Lord's Name has been found; without the True Guru no one finds (it). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who fix their minds on the Lord. The True Lord is found through devotion to the Guru; in Sahaj (they) enshrine (him) in the mind. If one serves the True Guru, then one obtains everything; with whatever wish one sets about (the service), such is the fruit one receives. The True Guru gives all things; by perfect fortune (God) brings (one) to meet (him). This mind is soiled; it does not meditate on the One; through love of duality much filth has stuck to it within. (This) proud (mind) roams to riverbanks, places of pilgrimage and foreign lands, and smears on still more of the filth of Haumai. If one serves the True Guru, then the filth goes; (one) dies (to self) while still alive, and fixes the mind on the Lord. The Lord is pure and true, and no filth clings to him; one who clings to the True One washes (his) filth away. Without the Guru there is pitch darkness; the ignorant one is blind, (lost in) blind darkness. Worms of dung, they deal in dung, and in dung again they rot. Serving the liberated one (the Guru), one becomes liberated; through the Shabad one sheds Haumai and the sense of mine. Day and night (such a one) serves the True Lord; by perfect fortune (he) has found the Guru. (God) himself forgives and unites (one) in union (with himself); from the perfect Guru one obtains the treasure of the Naam. Through the True Name the mind becomes true for ever; serving the True One, one sheds pain. (He) is ever present; do not think (him) far away; through the Guru's Shabad, recognise the Lord within. O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (the Name) is obtained from the perfect Guru. ॥8॥
116.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who are true here are true hereafter (too); (their) mind is true; (they) are absorbed in the true Shabad. They serve the True One and practise Truth; Truth, and Truth alone, they practise. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the True Name in the mind. They serve the True One, merge in the True One, and sing the praises of the True One. The pandits read (the scriptures) but do not taste (their) savour; in the love of another they let (their) minds wander after Maya. In attachment to Maya (they) have lost all understanding; having done wrong, they repent. If one meets the True Guru, then one finds the essence (of things), and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind. Through the Shabad one dies (to self), subdues one's own mind, and finds the door of liberation. (He) cuts away sins and drives out anger, (who) keeps the Guru's Shabad held in the heart. Those dyed in the True One are ever detached; killing Haumai, they are united (with God). The jewel is within, but it is found only when (the Guru) leads one to it; desire is of three kinds, Maya is of three kinds. Reading and reading, the pandits and the silent sages have grown weary, (yet) they do not grasp the fourth state. (God) himself dyes (them), (himself) gives (them) the colour (of love); those people stay steeped (in his love) whom (he) has dyed through the Guru's Shabad. The Lord's colour, utterly boundless, has come upon (them); steeped in the Lord's savour, with joy, (they) sing (his) praises. For the Gurmukh, that (True One) alone is wealth, miraculous power, truth and self-discipline; through the Guru (comes) divine knowledge; through the Name, liberation. Through the Guru (they) do the work of Truth, and merge in the True One alone. Through the Guru (one understands that God himself) creates, and having created, destroys; for the Gurmukh, (God) himself is caste and honour, everything. O Nanak, the Gurmukh meditates on the Name, and merges in the Name alone. ॥8॥
117.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Creation and dissolution come about through (God's) Word (his Hukam) alone; through the Word alone creation comes about again. Through the Guru (one sees that) the True One himself pervades all; through the Guru, (that) having created (the world), he is merged (in it). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the perfect Guru in the mind. From the Guru comes peace; (one) performs devotion day and night, and speaking (his) virtues, merges in the Lord of virtues. Through the Guru (one sees that) in earth and water, in air and fire, the Wondrous (Lord himself) is at play. He is without a Guru who dies and dies and is born again; those without a Guru keep coming and going. That Creator has staged a play; within the frame of the body he has placed everything. Piercing (the mind) with the Shabad, some (rare) one reaches (the Lord's) mansion; (the Lord) calls (him) into (his own) mansion. The Banker is true, and the traders (who deal with him) are true, (who) trade in Truth, in boundless love for the Guru. They purchase Truth and practise Truth; Truth, and Truth alone, they practise. Without capital, how can anyone obtain the goods? All the manmukh people have gone astray. Without capital all depart empty-handed; going empty-handed, they suffer pain. Some, (abiding) in love through the Guru's Shabad, trade in Truth; they themselves swim across and carry all their families across. Their coming (into the world) is approved; meeting the Beloved, they find peace. The treasure is within, (but) the fool searches outside; the blind manmukhs wander about out of step (with life's true rhythm). Where the treasure is, from there no (manmukh) obtains (it); the manmukhs stray in doubt. (God) himself gives (this gift), calling (one to himself) through the Shabad; in the mansion of the Master of the mansion, (such a one) finds the peace of Sahaj. O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (God) himself hears (the Name) again and again and meditates (on it). ॥8॥
Betaale: out of the beat (taal), as a singer loses the rhythm.
117.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The True Guru has imparted (this) true teaching: remember the Lord; (he) is (your) companion at the end. The Lord is beyond reach and beyond the senses, has no master over him, and is not born; (he) is found through love for the True Guru. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who rid themselves of self-conceit. If one sheds self-conceit, then one finds the Lord, and in Sahaj merges with the Lord. As was written from before, (one) has done that deed: serving the True Guru, (he) has found lasting peace. Without good fortune one does not find the Guru; through the Shabad (the Guru) unites (one) in union (with God). The Gurmukh stays untouched in the world, leaning on the Guru, with the Name as (his) support. What force can anyone use on the Gurmukh? (The one who tries) wears himself out and suffers pain. The blind manmukh has no understanding at all; he is the slayer of his own soul and a butcher of the world. Slandering again and again, he takes up a great load (of sin), and carries (others') load without wages. This world is a garden, and my God (its) gardener; he ever tends (it), and no (plant) is left out (of his care). Whatever scent he places (within), that is what comes forth; the fragrant (flower) makes itself known by its fragrance. The self-willed world is sick; (it) has forgotten the Giver of peace, the Unreachable, the Infinite. The wretched wander ever wailing; without the Guru (they) find no peace. He who made (them) alone knows the way (to heal them); if he himself acts (in grace), then (one) recognises (his) Hukam. As (the nature) he places within (a being), so (that being) acts; and he himself casts (it) out. Apart from that True One, I have no other; the one he attaches (to himself) becomes pure. O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (every) heart; the one to whom (God) gives (it) receives (it). ॥8॥
The slanderer is held to take on the sins of the one he slanders: he carries another's load and is paid nothing for it.
Vaasna is both a scent and the inclination placed within a being; vaasu is the fragrant one, the flower.
118.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (One who) enshrines the Amrit Name in the mind, sheds Haumai, the sense of mine, and all pain; through the Amrit Bani (he) ever praises (God), and through the Amrit (Bani) obtains the Amrit (Name). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Amrit Bani in the mind. Enshrining the Amrit Bani in the mind, (they) meditate on the Amrit Name. With (his) mouth, in (his) words, (he) ever speaks Amrit; with (his) eyes (he) ever sees and discerns the Amrit (Lord). Day and night (he) ever speaks the Amrit discourse, and recites it to others. Dyed in the love of the Amrit (Lord), (he) holds (him) in loving attention; by the Guru's grace (he) obtains the Amrit. With (his) tongue (he) speaks Amrit day and night, and in mind and body drinks the Amrit. (God) does what does not even enter (anyone's) thoughts; no one can erase his Hukam. By (his) Hukam alone the Amrit Bani prevails; by (his) Hukam alone (he) gives the Amrit to drink. Wondrous are the works of the Creator Lord; this mind, going astray, (he) turns back, fixes (its) attention on the Amrit Bani, and through the Amrit Shabad makes (the Name) resound (within it). The counterfeit and the genuine you yourself created; you yourself assay all people. Assaying the genuine, (you) put them in (your) treasury, and the counterfeit you lead astray in doubt. (O God,) how can I see (you)? How can I praise (you)? By the Guru's grace, through the Shabad, (I) praise (you). In your will dwells the Amrit; by (your) will you give the Amrit to drink. Amrit is the Shabad, Amrit the Lord's Bani; when the True Guru is served, (it) settles in the heart. O Nanak, the Amrit Name is ever the giver of peace; drinking the Amrit, all hunger departs. ॥8॥
119.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Amrit is raining down gently, of its own accord; through the Guru, only some rare person obtains (it). Drinking the Amrit, (they) are satisfied for ever; in (his) mercy (God) quenches (their) thirst. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who drink the Amrit through the Guru. (Their) tongue, having tasted the savour (of the Name), stays ever dyed in (God's) love, (and) in Sahaj (they) sing the Lord's praises. By the Guru's grace some (rare) one attains Sahaj; (he) kills duality and holds the One in loving attention. If (God) casts (his) glance of grace, then one sings the Lord's praises, (and) by (his) grace merges in the True One. O God, your glance of grace is upon all; on some it is little, on some it is much. Nothing happens beyond you; through the Guru (this) understanding is won. Through the Guru (this) essence has been reflected upon: your storehouses are filled with Amrit; without serving the True Guru, none obtains (it); by the Guru's grace (it) is received. The person who serves the True Guru is made beautiful; (his) inner mind is enraptured by the Amrit Name. (His) mind and body are dyed with the Amrit, with the Bani; in Sahaj (he) recites the Amrit (to others). The manmukh has gone astray; the love of another ruins (him); (he) does not take the Naam, and dies eating poison. Day and night, ever, (he) dwells in dung; without service (he) wastes (his) life. He alone drinks the Amrit whom (God) himself gives it to drink; by the Guru's grace, in Sahaj, (he) holds (God) in loving attention. The Perfect (Lord) himself pervades all; through the Guru's teaching (he) comes into view. He, the Immaculate, is himself all in all; the One who created (the world) himself destroys (it). O Nanak, cherish the Naam ever (in the mind); (so) in Sahaj you will merge in the True One. ॥8॥
119.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (O God,) those who please you are attached to the True One; they ever serve the True One, in Sahaj and in love. Through the true Shabad let (me too) praise the True One; the True One unites (those who praise him) in union (with himself). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who praise the True One. All who meditate on the True One are dyed in the True One, and merge in the True One alone. Wherever I look, the True One is in every place; by the Guru's grace I enshrine (him) in the mind. True is the body (of those) whose tongue is dyed in the True One; hearing the Truth, they speak it and tell of it. (The mind) subdued, (one) whose desire has merged in the True One has seen with this mind that all (the world) comes and goes. Such a one serves the True Guru; (his) mind is ever steady, and he finds a dwelling in his own home (within). The Guru's Shabad has shown (me the Lord) within the heart; through the Shabad (I) have burnt away attachment to Maya. Seeing only the True One (everywhere), I praise (him); through the Guru's Shabad (beings) find the True One.
