Those who are dyed in the True One have their loving attention fixed on him for good; those who keep the Lord's Name (in the heart) are fortunate. Through the true Shabad (God) himself unites (with himself) those who sing the True One's praises in the Sat Sangat. One could read (his) account, if he could be held in any account; he is beyond reach, beyond the senses; understanding (of him) comes through the Shabad. Day and night I praise (him) through the true Shabad; no one else can find his worth. (People) have read and read until they were weary, but peace did not come; burnt by craving, they have no understanding. They buy poison, they thirst for attachment to poison, and speaking falsehood they eat poison. By the Guru's grace I have known the One alone; killing (the sense of) another, the mind has merged in the True One. O Nanak, the one Name pervades within the mind; by the Guru's grace (it) is obtained. ॥8॥
120.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (O God,) all the colours and forms at play are yours; (beings) die and are born again and again, and go through many rounds (of birth and death). You alone are unshakable, beyond reach and without limit; through the Guru's teaching you give understanding (of yourself). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Name of Ram in the mind. He has no form, no mark, no colour at all; through the Guru's teaching he himself gives understanding (of himself). There is one Light in all, if anyone comes to know it; serving the True Guru, it is made manifest. Hidden and manifest, he pervades every place; he merges (the soul's) light in (his own) Light. The world is burning in the fire of craving; (in it is) greed, pride and much egotism. Dying again and again it is born, loses its honour, and wastes its life in vain. Some rare one understands the Guru's Shabad; if one kills the self, then (the Lord, pervading) the three worlds is seen. Then he does not die (again), death does not come to him; in Sahaj he merges in the True One. He does not fix his mind on Maya again; he remains ever merged in the Guru's Shabad. He praises the True One, who is within every body; the True One alone shines (in all). I praise the True One, ever present; through the Guru's Shabad (he is seen) filling all. By the Guru's grace the True One is seen; in the True One alone is peace found. The True One is pervading within the mind; the True One is ever unshakable; he does not come or go. The mind that is attached to the True One is pure; through the Guru's teaching (such ones) merge in the True One. I praise the True One; there is no other (like him), serving whom there is lasting peace. O Nanak, those dyed in the Name are discerning; Truth, and Truth alone, they practise. ॥8॥
121.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Pure is the Shabad (of his praise), pure is (his) Bani; (his) pure Light is contained in all. Through the pure Bani I praise the Lord; repeating (the Name of) the pure Lord, (beings) rid themselves of filth. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine in the mind the Giver of peace. Through the Guru's Shabad I praise the pure Lord; hearing the Shabad alone, (they) quench their craving. (One in whose) mind the pure Name has come to dwell becomes pure in mind and body, and casts off attachment to Maya. He ever sings the pure praises of the True One, and sounds the pure Naad (of praise). (One who) has received the pure Amrit from the Guru has died to self within; there is no attachment to Maya there. Pure is (his) wisdom, his meditation utterly pure; (such ones) enshrine the pure Bani in the mind. One who serves the Pure One becomes pure; through the Guru's Shabad he washes off the filth of Haumai. (Within him) the pure Bani sounds as the unstruck melody; (such ones) win glory at the True One's door. From the Pure One all become pure; pure is the mind of one who strings it on the Lord's Shabad. Fortunate are those attached to the pure Name; through the Name they are pure and beautiful. He alone is pure who is made beautiful by the Shabad; the pure Name holds (his) mind and body enraptured. In the True Name no filth ever clings; the True One makes (their) faces radiant. The mind is filthy in the love of another; filthy is (his) cooking square, filthy the place (he sits in). Eating filth, he adds yet more filth; the manmukhs, through filth, suffer pain. The filthy and the pure, all are in (his) Hukam, every one; they alone are pure who please the True Lord. O Nanak, (those within whose) mind the Naam dwells rid themselves of filth through the Guru. ॥8॥
Naad: the sound the yogis raise on their horn (singi); here the praise of the True One is that sound.
121.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Govind is radiant, and radiant are (his) swans (his devotees); (my) mind, (my) speech and my desire are made pure. Radiant within, their faces ever shine; they meditate on the Naam, radiant beyond measure. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who sing the praises of Gobind. (Such a one) says Gobind, Gobind, day and night, and through the Shabad lets (others) hear Gobind's praises. (Those who) sing of Gobind in Sahaj and in love become radiant in the fear of the Guru; the filth of Haumai departs. They remain ever in bliss and perform devotion day and night; they hear Gobind's praises and sing them. The mind dances (when one) holds devotion firm; through the Guru's Shabad he joins the mind (to the Lord) within the mind. Ending attachment to Maya is keeping the true beat; (such ones) dance in the Shabad alone. (One who) cries out aloud and dashes his body (on the ground) is (caught) in attachment to Maya; Jamkaal has him in sight. Attachment to Maya makes this mind dance; with deceit within, (such ones) suffer pain. When (the Lord) himself has devotion done through the Guru, body and mind are dyed, in Sahaj and in love. The Bani resounds (within), and he plays it through the Shabad; (the Lord) accepts devotion done through the Guru. (One who) beats out many rhythms and plays instruments, (by that) no one hears (the Name) or enshrines (it) in the mind. For Maya's sake he marks out the ring and dances; in the love of another (such ones) suffer pain. One within whom love (for the Lord) takes hold is liberated; (his) senses are under control, and he holds to the self-discipline of Truth. Through the Guru's Shabad he ever meditates on the Lord; this is the devotion that pleases the Lord. Through the Guru alone has devotion been done in all four ages; by any other way no one attains devotion. O Nanak, the Name is obtained through devotion to the Guru, by fixing the mind on the Guru's feet. ॥8॥

Dancing in a marked-out ring (pirr): troupes of the raas marked out a ring and, dancing to rhythm and instruments, enacted the life of Krishna and called it devotion; the hymn's dance, beat and instruments allude to it.
122.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). I serve the True One, I praise the True One; in the True Name there is never any pain. Those who serve the Giver of peace find peace; through the Guru's teaching they enshrine (him) in the mind. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who rest in the Samadhi of peace, in Sahaj. Those who serve the Lord ever look beautiful; they win glory, and their awareness is beautiful. (O God,) everyone calls himself your devotee; they alone are devotees who are pleasing to your mind. Through the Bani they praise you, the True One; dyed in (your) love, they perform (your) devotion. O True dear Lord, everyone is yours; when one meets (you) through the Guru, the round (of birth and death) is ended. When it pleases you, you absorb (beings) in the Name; you yourself have them repeat the Name. (One who) through the Guru's teaching has enshrined the Lord in the mind has cast off joy and sorrow and all attachment. His loving attention is fixed on the One for ever; (such ones) enshrine the Lord's Name in the mind. (O God, your) devotees are dyed in (your) love, ever in joyful eagerness for you; the Naam, the nine treasures, has come to dwell in (their) minds. By perfect fortune they have found the True Guru, (who) through the Shabad unites (them) in union (with the Lord). (O God,) you are merciful, ever the giver of peace; you yourself unite (beings with yourself); through the Guru (you) are known. You yourself give the Naam and glory; those dyed in the Naam find peace. O True One, ever, ever I praise you; through the Guru (I) have known that there is no other. The mind stays absorbed in the One; when the mind is won over, (such ones) are united (with the Lord) within the mind. One who becomes Gurmukh praises the True Master, the Carefree. O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (his) mind; through the Guru's Shabad (such ones) are united with the Lord. ॥8॥
122.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (O God,) your devotees look beautiful at the true court; through the Guru's Shabad they are adorned with the Name. Day and night they remain ever in bliss; speaking (his) virtues, they merge in the Lord of virtues. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who hear the Naam and enshrine (it) in the mind. The dear Lord is true, the highest of the high; killing Haumai, (beings) are united (with him). The dear Lord is true, and true is (his) glory; by the Guru's grace he unites some (rare one with himself). Those who meet (him) through the Guru's Shabad are not parted (again); in Sahaj they merge in the True One. (O God,) nothing happens outside you; you create and create, and watch over (it); you alone know (it all). The Creator himself does and has (all) done; through the Guru's teaching he himself unites (beings with himself). The virtuous soul-bride finds the Lord; she makes the fear (of God) and love her adornment. Serving the True Guru, she is a happy wife for ever; through the true teaching she merges (in her Husband). Those who forget the Shabad have no place and no rest; lost in doubt, (they wander) like a crow in a deserted house. They lose both this world and the next; (their lives) pass in pain upon pain. Writing and writing, (they) have used up paper and ink; (but) in the love of another no one finds peace. They write falsehood and practise falsehood; with their minds fixed on falsehood, they burn away. (Those who) through the Guru write Truth, and Truth alone, and reflection (on it), those people are true; they find the door of liberation. True are (their) paper, pen and inkpot; writing Truth, they merge in the True One. My God sits within (all) and watches; by the Guru's grace, the one who meets (him) is accepted. O Nanak, (one who) receives the Naam receives glory; (the Naam) is obtained from the perfect Guru. ॥8॥
123.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through the Guru the light of the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) dawns (within); through the Guru's Shabad one clears away the filth of Haumai that clings (to the mind). The mind becomes pure and is dyed in devotion day and night; through devotion one finds the Lord. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who themselves practise devotion and lead others to devotion. Let us ever bow to such devoted servants (of the Lord), who sing the Lord's praises day and night. The Creator himself brings about the cause (of devotion); he sets (each one) to the task that pleases him. By perfect fortune the Guru is served; through serving the Guru, peace is found. When one dies (to self) again and again and lives (anew), then one gains something; by the Guru's grace one enshrines the Lord in the mind. One who enshrines the Lord in the mind is ever free, and with natural ease merges in Sahaj. (One who) performs many rituals does not find liberation; he roams from land to land, and in the love of another goes astray. The deceitful one has wasted his life in vain; without the Shabad he suffers pain. One who guards the running (mind), checks it and keeps it still, by the Guru's grace attains the highest state. The True Guru himself brings (him) into union (with the Lord); meeting the Beloved, he finds peace. Some are attached to falsehood, and gain false fruits; in the love of another their lives are wasted in vain. They drown themselves and drown all their kin as well; speaking falsehood, they eat poison. Some rare Gurmukh sees the mind (held still) within this body, when through loving devotion he dries up Haumai. Siddhas, seekers and those under vows of silence have kept fixing their attention; they too have not seen the mind (held still) within the body. That Creator himself causes (all) to be done; what else can anyone do? What can come of what the created (being) does? O Nanak, the one to whom he gives the Naam receives it, and enshrines the Naam alone in the mind. ॥8॥
124.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Within this cave (of the body) is a treasure that never runs out; within it dwells the Lord, unseen and boundless. He himself is hidden and himself manifest; through the Guru's Shabad (one) sheds the self. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Amrit Name in the mind. The Amrit Name is of the highest savour, and sweet; through the Guru's teaching they drink this Amrit. Killing Haumai, (one who) has had the hard (adamantine) doors opened has found the priceless Naam by the Guru's grace. Without the Shabad no one finds the Naam; by the Guru's grace (it) is enshrined in the mind. One who has put the true collyrium (eye-salve) of the Guru's wisdom in the eyes has light within, and has driven off the darkness of ignorance; (his) light has merged in the Light, the mind is won over, and he wins glory at the Lord's door. One who goes outside the body to search does not find the Naam, and suffers great pain, (like one pressed into) forced labour. The blind manmukh does not understand; when, after wandering about, he comes back, he finds the thing (the Name) through the Guru. When by the Guru's grace one finds the True Lord, one sees (him) in the mind and in the body, and the filth of Haumai goes. Sitting in the sacred place (within), he ever sings the Lord's praises, and through the Shabad merges in the True One. One who has barred the nine doors and held back the running (mind) comes to dwell in the tenth (door), his own home. There the unstruck melodies of the Shabad play day and night; through the Guru's teaching he lets (others) hear the Shabad. Without the Shabad there is darkness within; (one) neither finds the thing (the Name) nor does the round (of births) end. The key is in the True Guru's hand; by no other means does the door open; the Guru is met by perfect fortune. You are hidden and manifest in all places; by the Guru's grace, meeting (you), this understanding is gained. O Nanak, ever praise the Naam; through the Guru (it) is enshrined in the mind. ॥8॥
124.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Gurmukh meets (the Lord); (the Lord) himself unites (him with himself). Death does not cast its eye on him, and pain does not torment (him). Killing Haumai, he breaks all bonds; the Gurmukh is made beautiful through the Shabad. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who are made beautiful through the Name of the Lord, Har Har. The Gurmukh sings (his praises), the Gurmukh dances (in joy), and fixes his mind on the Lord. The Gurmukh, living and dying, is approved (by the Lord); his life does not waste away; the Shabad is his familiar companion. The Gurmukh does not die, nor does death devour him; the Gurmukh merges in the True One. The Gurmukh wins glory at the Lord's door; the Gurmukh sheds the self from within. He crosses over himself and carries all his kin across; the Gurmukh makes his life worthy. Pain never touches the Gurmukh's body; the Gurmukh's pain of Haumai is ended. The Gurmukh's mind is pure, no filth clings to it again; the Gurmukh merges in Sahaj. The Gurmukh receives the Name, and glory; the Gurmukh sings (his) praises and wins honour. He stays ever in bliss, day and night; the Gurmukh makes the Shabad (of praise) his work. The Gurmukh is dyed in the Shabad day and night; through all four ages the Gurmukh has known (the Lord). The Gurmukh sings (his) praises and is ever pure; through the Shabad he performs devotion. Without the Guru there is pitch darkness; seized by Jamkaal, (people) cry out. Day and night they are diseased; they are worms of filth, and in filth they suffer pain. The Gurmukh (knows that the Lord) himself does and has (all) done; in the Gurmukh's heart he himself comes and dwells. O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (it) is obtained from the perfect Guru. ॥8॥
125.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One Light is the light in (all) bodies; the perfect True Guru shows (this) through the Shabad. He himself has made the difference within the hearts; he himself has fashioned the whole design. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who sing the praises of the True Lord. No one finds Sahaj without the Guru; through the Guru one merges in Sahaj. You yourself are beautiful, and you yourself enchant the world; you yourself, by your glance of grace, string the world (on your thread); you yourself give pain and pleasure, O Creator; through the Guru the Lord is shown. The Creator himself does and has (all) done; he himself enshrines the Guru's Shabad in the mind. From the Shabad springs the Amrit Bani; the Gurmukh speaks it and lets (others) hear it. He himself is the Creator, himself the Enjoyer; he breaks the bonds (of beings), and is ever free. The True One himself is ever free; he himself, the Unseen, makes himself known. He himself is Maya, and himself its shadow (its spell); he himself is attachment; he has created the whole world. He himself is the Giver of virtues and sings (his own) praises; he himself speaks (them) and lets (others) hear (them). He himself does and has (all) done; he himself sets up and himself pulls down; nothing happens outside you; you yourself set (all) to their tasks. He himself kills and himself gives life; he himself brings (beings) together and unites (them) in union (with himself). Through service, lasting peace has been found; through the Guru one merges in Sahaj. He himself is the highest of the high; only the rare one to whom he himself shows (himself) sees (him). O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (his) heart; (the Lord) himself watches over (all) and reveals (himself). ॥8॥
126.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). My God is fully pervading all places; by the Guru's grace, within the home (of the heart) itself, I have found (him). I serve (him) ever and meditate on (him) with a single mind; through the Guru (one) merges in the True One. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Life of the World in the mind. The Lord, the Life of the World, is fearless, the Giver; through the Guru's teaching (they) merge in Sahaj. Within the home (of the heart) are the earth, the bull Dhaul (said to bear it) and the nether worlds; within the home itself is the Beloved, ever young. The Giver of peace is ever in bliss; through the Guru's teaching (one) merges in Sahaj. (While) within the body there is Haumai and the sense of mine, the round of birth and death does not end. Whoever becomes Gurmukh kills Haumai, and meditates on the True One alone. Within the body are two brothers, sin and virtue; the two together have brought forth the world. One who kills both and goes and enters the one home merges in Sahaj through the Guru's teaching. In the home itself, through the love of another, there is darkness; when one gives up Haumai and the sense of mine, there is light; the Shabad, the Giver of peace, becomes manifest, and (one) meditates on the Naam day and night. Within is the Light whose expanse is manifest (as the world); through the Guru's teaching the darkness has gone; the lotus (of the heart) has blossomed, lasting peace has been found, and (his) light is merged in the Light. Within the mansion (of the body) are storehouses filled with jewels; the Gurmukh obtains the boundless Naam. The Gurmukh, the trader, ever deals (in it), and ever earns the profit of the Naam. He himself keeps the merchandise (of the Name), and himself gives (it); through the Guru, many a one trades (in it). O Nanak, the one on whom he casts his glance of grace obtains (it); in his mercy he enshrines (it) in the mind. ॥8॥
126.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Lord himself unites (one with himself) and has (him) serve (him); through the Guru's Shabad the love of duality goes. The Lord is pure, ever the Giver of virtues; the Lord himself merges (his servants) in (his) virtues. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the True One, ever true, in the heart. The True Name is ever pure; through the Guru's Shabad (they) enshrine (it) in the mind. He himself is the Guru and the Giver; he is the Maker (of beings) according to (their) deeds. (His) servants serve (him); through the Guru they have known the Lord. Through the Amrit Name (his) servants are ever beautiful; through the Guru's teaching they obtain the Lord's sweet essence. Within this cave (of the body) one place is made beautiful, (when) the perfect Guru has ended Haumai and doubt. Day and night (such ones), dyed in (his) love, praise the Naam; by the Guru's grace they find (him). Through the Guru's Shabad this (soul) reflects on the cave (of the body), (and) the immaculate Name of Murari dwells within (him); he sings the Lord's praises, is made beautiful by the Shabad, and meeting the Beloved, finds peace. Jam, the toll-collector, levies his tax on those in the love of another; he punishes those who have strayed from the Name. He takes account of every ghari and muhat (every moment), and has (all) weighed out, ratti by ratti, masa by masa (to the smallest weight). (The bride who) in her parents' home (this world) does not remember her Husband, robbed by duality, weeps and wails aloud; utterly of a bad home, unlovely and ill-natured, she does not find her Husband even in a dream. (She who) in her parents' home has enshrined her Husband in her mind, to her the perfect Guru has shown (him) ever present; that bride keeps her Husband clasped to her bosom; through the Shabad she delights in her Husband, and her bed is beautiful. He himself calls (beings) to himself and gives (this gift); he enshrines his own Name in the mind. O Nanak, (one who) receives the Naam receives glory, and ever, day and night, sings (his) praises. ॥8॥
Ihu (with -u, masculine) is the soul, not the cave (gufa is feminine): through the Guru's Shabad the soul reflects on the cave of the body.
127.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Exalted is the birth, and blessed the place of dwelling, of those who serve the True Guru and, living at home, remain detached (from Maya). They abide in the Lord's love, ever dyed in (that) love; their minds are sated with the Lord's sweet essence. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who read, understand and enshrine (the Name) in the mind. Through the Guru they read and praise the Lord's Name, and win honour at the True One's door. The Lord, unseen and unfathomable, is contained in all; by no means at all can he be attained. If he grants his grace, the True Guru is met, and with his glance of grace (the Lord) unites (one) in union (with himself). One who reads in the love of another does not understand; he frets and burns for the sake of Maya of the three qualities. The bonds of the three qualities are broken through the Guru's Shabad; through the Guru's Shabad one is set free. This fickle mind does not come under control; caught in duality, it runs off in the ten directions. It is a worm of poison, steeped in poison, and in poison itself it rots away. (The manmukh) keeps saying I, I, and makes a show of himself; he performs many rites, (but) none of them is accepted. (O God,) nothing happens apart from you; those (you) forgive are made beautiful through the Shabad. (One who) does not understand the Lord is born and wastes away; day and night (such people) wander in the love of another. The manmukh's life has gone in vain; in the end he departed repenting. The Husband is in a far land, and (the wife) adorns herself: such are the deeds the blind manmukh does. He has no honour in this world and no shelter in the next; he wastes his life in vain. Some rare one has known the Lord's Name, recognising (it) through the perfect Guru's Shabad. Every day, day and night, he performs devotion, and in Sahaj he finds peace. The One, he alone, is at work in all; only some rare one understands (this) through the Guru. O Nanak, the servants imbued with the Name look beautiful; in his mercy (the Lord) himself unites (them with himself). ॥9॥
128.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The manmukhs read (the scriptures) and have themselves called pandits, (but) in the love of another they suffer great pain. Drunk on the poison (of Maya), they perceive nothing; again and again they come into (new) births. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who kill Haumai and are united (with the Lord). Through serving the Guru the Lord has come to dwell in (their) minds, and in Sahaj they drink the Lord's sweet essence. (The pandits) read the Veda, (but) have not come to taste the Lord's sweet essence; enticed by Maya, they only hold forth in dispute. Those of ignorant mind are ever in darkness; those who understand through the Guru sing of the Lord. When the Indescribable One is spoken of, through the Shabad (he) is found lovely; through the Guru's teaching the True One becomes dear to the mind. Day and night they dwell on the True One, the True One alone; this mind (of theirs) is dyed in the True One. Those dyed in the True One love the True One alone; (God) himself gives (this gift), and does not regret (the giving). Through the Guru's Shabad they have ever known the True One; meeting the True One, they find peace. The filth of falsehood and deceit does not cling to them; by the Guru's grace (such a one) stays awake day and night. The pure Name dwells within (his) heart, and (his) light merges in the Light. (The manmukhs) read about the three qualities, (but) do not know the Lord, the essence (of all); strayed from the Root, they do not recognise the Guru's Shabad. Gripped by attachment, they perceive nothing; the Lord is found through the Guru's Shabad. The Veda speaks aloud of Maya of the three qualities; the manmukhs, in the love of another, do not understand. They read about the three qualities, and do not know the One Lord; without understanding, they suffer pain. When it pleases him, he himself unites (one with himself), and through the Guru's Shabad takes away anxiety and pain. O Nanak, true and lasting is the glory of the Name; by trusting in the Name alone (beings) find peace. ॥8॥
128.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). He himself is Nirgun, and he himself Sargun; one who recognises (this) essence is the true pandit. Enshrining the Lord's Name in the mind, he himself crosses over and carries all his kin across. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who taste the Lord's sweet essence and know its savour. Those who taste the Lord's sweet essence, those servants, are pure, and meditate on the pure Name. He alone is nihkarmi who reflects on the Shabad; within (him) is the essence, and through wisdom he kills Haumai. He obtains the treasure of the Name, the nine treasures, and, erasing the three qualities, merges (in the Lord). One who acts in Haumai does not become nihkarmi; by the Guru's grace (alone) does one shed Haumai. Within (him) is discernment (between good and bad); he ever examines himself, and through the Guru's Shabad sings (the Lord's) praises. The Lord (himself) is the lake, the ocean; he alone is pure. The Sants, having become Gurmukh, ever peck (the pearls of the Name) from it. They bathe (in it) ever, day and night, and wash away the filth of Haumai. (One who dwells) in loving devotion is a pure swan; having killed Haumai, he dwells in the Lord's lake. Day and night in love with the true Shabad, he gains a dwelling in the Lord's lake. The manmukh is ever a filthy crane, smeared with the filth of Haumai; he bathes, but (his) filth does not go. (One who) dies while living and reflects on the Guru's Shabad washes away the filth of Haumai. (He) found the precious jewel (of the Name) within (his own) home (the heart), (to whom) the perfect True Guru made the Shabad heard. By the Guru's grace (his) darkness was dispelled; there was light in the heart, and (he) recognised his own self. (God) himself creates, and himself watches over (all); that person is accepted who serves the True Guru. O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (his) heart; by the Guru's grace (he) attains (the Lord). ॥8॥
Nihkarmi: free of the bond of deeds; not one who does nothing, but one who acts without Haumai and desire, so that his deeds do not bind him.
The lake and the swan: in Indian poetry the swan lives on the lake Mansarovar and feeds on pearls; here the lake is the Lord and the swans are his Saints.
129.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The whole world is (caught in) attachment to Maya; (beings of) the three qualities are seen enticed by Maya. By the Guru's grace some rare one understands (this), and fixes his attention in the fourth state. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who burn away attachment to Maya through the Shabad. One who burns away attachment to Maya fixes the mind on the Lord, and wins honour at the Lord's door, in (his) mansion. Maya is the root of the goddesses and gods, (Maya,) which brought forth the Simritis and the Shastras. Lust and anger have spread through the world; coming and going, (beings) suffer pain. In it (this world) one jewel of divine wisdom has (also) been placed; (the one who), by the Guru's grace, has enshrined (it) in the mind practises continence, truthful living, self-restraint and truth, and through the perfect Guru meditates on the Naam. In her parents' home (this world) the bride has strayed, lost in doubt; clinging to another, she repents afterwards. She loses both this world and the next, and finds no peace even in a dream. The bride who, in her parents' home, cherishes her Husband (in her heart) sees (him) by the Guru's grace right beside her; in Sahaj she stays dyed in her Husband's love, and makes the Shabad her adornment. Fruitful is the life of those who have found the True Guru; through the Guru's Shabad they have burned away the love of another. The One alone pervades within (their) hearts; joining the Sat Sangat, they sing the Lord's praises. One who does not serve the True Guru: why did he come (into the world)? Cursed is his life; he has wasted his birth in vain. The Naam does not come into the manmukh's mind; without the Name he suffers great pain. He who fashioned the world alone knows (its play); he himself unites (with himself the one who) recognises (him) through the Shabad. O Nanak, the Naam has come to those servants on whose foreheads this destiny was written by the Lord from the start. ॥8॥
129.2: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). He himself is the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond; he himself establishes (the world), and having established it, (himself) pulls it down. The One, he alone, is at work in all; through the Guru (beings) win honour. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who meditate on the Name of the Formless One. No form or feature is his, (yet) he is seen in each and every heart; through the Guru the Unseen is perceived. (O God,) you are merciful and kind; you alone are that God. Without you there is no other at all. (On whom) the Guru bestows his grace, (to him) he gives the Naam; (such a one) stays merged in the Naam, in the Naam alone. You yourself are the True Creator; your storehouses are full of devotion. One who receives the Name through the Guru has the mind drenched (in it), and enters Samadhi in Sahaj. Day and night I sing your praises, O God; I praise you, my Beloved. I beg of no other than you; by the Guru's grace (alone) are you found. (You are) inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses; no one has found your measure. You show your mercy, and unite (one with yourself). Through the perfect Guru's Shabad let (God) be meditated on; serving the Shabad, (people) find peace. Virtuous is the tongue that sings (God's) praises; (one who) praises the Naam is pleasing to the True One. Through the Guru (that tongue) stays ever dyed in (his) love; meeting the True One, (such people) win honour. The manmukh does his deeds in pride; at the gamble he loses (his) life, the whole game. Within (him) is greed, pitch darkness; again and again he comes and goes. The Creator himself gives glory to those for whom he himself set down this writ from the start. O Nanak, (they) receive the Naam, the destroyer of fear, and through the Guru's Shabad find peace. ॥8॥
130.1: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Unseen (Lord) is within (all), (yet) cannot be perceived; (he) has taken the jewel of the Naam and kept it hidden (within). Inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses, higher than all, (he) is perceived through the Guru's Shabad. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who make the Naam heard in Kalyug. The True One upholds (his) beloved Sants; by great good fortune is the sight (of them) obtained. He for whom seekers and Siddhas wander about, (on whom) the Brahmas and Indras meditate in their hearts, whom the thirty-three crore (gods) search for: (the fortunate,) meeting the Guru, sing of him in their hearts. (O God,) at all hours the wind repeats (your Name); the earth is (your) servant, a maid who waits at (your) feet. You dwell in (beings of) all the sources of life and all tongues; you are pleasing to the minds of all. The True Master becomes known through the Guru; through the perfect Guru's Shabad (he) is recognised. Those who have drunk (the nectar of the Name) are the ones satisfied; in the Truest of the True they are fulfilled. In his home (the heart) is Sahaj; he alone is at ease; he ever enjoys bliss, delight and joyful play. He is the wealthy one, he the great banker, who fixes his mind on the Guru's feet. (O God,) first you provided the sustenance, and afterwards you created the being. O Lord, there is no other giver as great as you; no one can be set beside you as your equal. One with whom you are pleased meditates on you, and lives by the mantra (teaching) of the holy. He himself crosses over and carries all his kin across; at (your) court he meets no hindrance. You are great, the highest of the high; you are without end, the very greatest of the great. I go as a sacrifice to you; Nanak is a slave of (your) slaves. ॥8॥
131.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Who is the one set free? Who is the one joined (to God)? Who is the one who truly knows (God)? Who is the one who speaks (of him)? Who is the householder, who the detached one? Who is the one who knows (the Lord's) worth? In what way is one bound, and in what way set free? In what way does the coming and going (of birth and death) end? Who does (good) deeds, who is nihkarmi? Who is the one who speaks (God's praise) and has (others) speak it? Who is the one at peace, who the one in pain? Who is the one who faces (the Guru), who the one turned away? In what way is (God) met, in what way is one parted (from him)? Who makes this way known? What Word is it that holds the wandering (mind) still? What is the teaching by which one bears pain and pleasure as one? What way of life lets one meditate on the Supreme Lord? In what way may one sing (his) Kirtan? The Gurmukh is the one set free; the Gurmukh is the one joined (to God). The Gurmukh is the one who truly knows; the Gurmukh is the one who speaks (of God). Blessed is the Gurmukh, householder or detached; the Gurmukh knows (the Lord's) worth. Through Haumai one is bound; through the Guru one is set free. Through the Guru the coming and going ends. The Gurmukh does (good) deeds, the Gurmukh is nihkarmi; whatever the Gurmukh does, he does in (God's) love. The Gurmukh is at peace, the manmukh in pain. The Gurmukh faces (the Guru); the manmukh is turned away. Through the Guru (God) is met; the manmukh is parted (from him); the Gurmukh makes the way known. The Guru's Word is what holds the wandering (mind) still. Through the Guru's teaching one bears pain and pleasure as one. The way of life the Guru gives is what lets one meditate on the Supreme Lord; through the Guru one sings (his) Kirtan. (God) himself has made this whole creation; he himself does, has (all) done, and establishes (all). From the One he has become countless (forms); O Nanak, (all) merges again in the One. ॥9॥
131.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). God is imperishable: then what is there (for his servant) to fret about? The Lord is the Master of all good fortune: then his servant lives in great ease. (O God,) you give peace to the soul, the breath of life and the mind; in what you do, (your servants) find peace. I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those to whose mind and body you are dear through the Guru. You are my mountain, you are my shelter; no one can be set beside you as your equal. The one to whom what you do seems sweet, that servant has seen the Supreme Lord in each and every heart. In every place and in the spaces between, it is you, you alone; you, the One and only, are at work (everywhere). You are the giver of every wish; (your) storehouses are full of devotion and love. Those whom you have kept safe in your mercy, they alone, by your full grace, stay merged (in you). (You) have drawn (them) up out of the blind well (of Maya) onto the bank; in your mercy (you) have looked on (your) servants with a glance of grace. They sing the praises of the Perfect, Imperishable (Lord); by telling and hearing, (his praises) never run short. Here and in the world beyond, you alone are the protector; in the mother's womb it was you who nourished (us). The fire of Maya cannot touch those who, dyed in (your) love, sing (your) praises. Which of your virtues can I tell and keep in mind? Within my mind and body I see you, and you alone. You are my friend, my companion, my Master; I know no other but you. O God, the one whose helper you have become is not touched by even a hot wind. You are the Master, the shelter, the giver of peace; repeating (your Name) in the Sat Sangat, (your servants) make you manifest (within them). You are lofty, fathomless, boundless, beyond price; you are the True Master; (I am) your servant, your slave. You are the sovereign Lord, and your rule stands for ever; Nanak goes as a sacrifice to you, again and again. ॥8॥
132.1: Raag Majh, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Day after day let the Beloved Lord be cherished (in the heart); let him never at all be put out of the mind. Let the company of the Sants be found, through which one does not go on the path of Jam. Take the Lord's Name as provisions (for the road), and no stain falls on your family. Those who remember the Master are not cast into hell. Not even a hot wind touches those in whose mind (the Lord) has come to dwell. They alone are fair and handsome who sit in the Saadh Sangat. Those who have gathered the Lord's wealth (the Name), they alone are deep and boundless (of heart). Let the Lord's nectar, the home of all delights, be drunk; seeing the face of (the Lord's) servant, one lives (in spirit). Set all your affairs right: worship the Guru's feet each day. One whom the Lord has made his own is the one who will repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world. He is the hero, he is the chief, on whose forehead (such) fortune is (written). Diving deep within the mind, let God be sought out; this is the enjoyment of (all) pleasures, this is sovereignty. (In those who did so) nothing evil has ever arisen; attached to the true work, they have crossed over. One who has enshrined the Creator in the mind has obtained the fruit of (human) birth. (O soul-bride,) the Lord, your Husband, pleases your mind: your wedded bliss has become lasting. (He) has obtained the imperishable treasure (the Name), (who has come) to the shelter of the Destroyer of fear. O Nanak, attaching (him) to his hem, (the Lord) has carried (him) across; (he) has won (the game of) this priceless life. ॥8॥
132.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Majh, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeating the Lord's Name again and again, the mind grows steady. Remembering, remembering the divine Guru, (all) fears are erased and gone far away. If one comes to the shelter of the Supreme Lord, why then should he pine in grief? Serving the feet of the Sants and the holy, every wish is fulfilled. In each and every heart the One is at work; he fills the water, the land and the sky. One who has served the Destroyer of sins has been made pure by the dust of the Sants' feet. The Master himself has set all (the world) free; repeating the Lord's Name, it has grown cool and calm. The Creator has done justice: the wicked have died, become like stuffed calves (lifeless within). Nanak is dyed in the True Name, and sees the Lord ever present (with him). ॥8॥
Tapavas (Arabic): judgement, justice. A moora is the hide of a dead calf stuffed with straw and set before a cow or buffalo so that she gives milk: alive to look at, dead within.
133.1: Barah Maha: Raag Majh, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Parted (from you) by the deeds we have done, O Lord (Ram), unite (us with you) in your mercy. Having roamed the four quarters and the ten directions, worn out, we have come to God's shelter. A cow that gives no milk is of no use at all; without water the crop wilts and yields no money; (so too,) if the Lord, the Husband, the Friend, is not met, where can rest be found? Where the Lord, the Husband, is not made manifest in the home (of the heart), those towns and villages are a (blazing) furnace. All adornments, betel and (other) pleasures, the body along with them, are all worthless; for the bride bereft of God, her Master and Husband, all friends and companions are as Jam. Nanak's prayer is this: in your mercy, grant (me your) Name. O Lord, unite (me) with the Master, God, whose abode stands for ever. ॥1॥

Barah Maha (the twelve months): a song of the year in which each month's season voices the soul-bride's longing for her Husband Lord. This one opens with a prayer, and its months run from Chet (mid-March to mid-April).
133.2: In Chet, let Govind be worshipped in remembrance, and great bliss wells up. Meeting the Sants, (this gift) is found: the tongue utters the Naam. Only one who has found his God is to be counted as having truly come (into the world). To live even a moment without him: know that life to be wasted. (He) fills the water, the land and the sky, and pervades the forests too; if such a God does not come to mind, how much of (that) pain can I count? Those who have enjoyed (union with) that God: their fortune is beyond measure. (My) mind longs for the sight of the Lord; in Nanak's mind is a thirst (for it). Whoever unites (me) with that God in Chet, at his feet I would fall. ॥2॥
133.3: In Vaisakh, how can they keep heart, the brides cut off (from the Husband), who are parted from (his) love? Forgetting the Lord, the Friend, the (all-pervading) Being, they are held fast by deceitful Maya. Son, wife and wealth go along with no one; he, the Lord, alone is the imperishable (companion). Tangled again and again in attachment to false pursuits, the whole (world) has perished. Without the Name of the One Lord, (their deeds) are snatched away from them on the road ahead. Forgetting the Beloved Lord, one comes to ruin; without God there is no other (to stand by one). Those who hold to the feet of the Beloved: spotless is their good name. O God, Nanak's prayer (to you) is this: come and meet (me), O God, that I may attain you. Vaisakh seems lovely only when the Sant (the Guru) is met, and (through him) that Lord. ॥3॥
134.1: In Jeth one should be joined to the Lord, before whom all bow down. Once one holds to the hem of the Lord, the Friend, he lets no one bind (that one). The Name of God is rubies and pearls; no thief can tunnel through to them. All the delights that please the mind are Narayan's. Whatever the Lord wills, he does; and that alone his creatures do. Those God has made his own are the ones hailed as blessed. If (he) could be had by one's own taking, why would (people) weep in separation? O Nanak, those who find the company of the holy (Guru) enjoy the delights (of union). Jeth is full of joy for one who has the Lord as Master, on whose forehead (such) fortune is (written). ॥4॥
134.2: Asarh burns for those beside whom the Lord, the Husband, is not; forsaking the Being who is the Life of the world, (they put their) hope in mortal men. In the love of another one is ruined; the noose of Jam falls on (her) neck. As one sows, so one reaps: (one meets) what is written on one's forehead. The night (of life) passed; she repented, and rose and went, her hope broken. Those who meet the holy one (the Guru) are released in the Lord's court. O God, show your mercy, that thirst for the sight of you may stay (in me). O God, I have no other but you; this is Nanak's supplication. Asarh is pleasant to the one in whose mind the Lord's feet dwell. ॥5॥
134.3: In Sawan, the bride who loves (the Lord's) lotus feet is green and in bloom. Body and mind dyed in the True One's love, she has the one Name as her support. The false delights of Maya's poison all look (to her) like ashes. Lovely is the drop of the Lord's nectar; meeting the holy (Guru), one is able to drink it. Forest and grass have burst into bloom at the touch of God, the all-powerful, boundless Being. (My) mind longs to meet the Lord; (he alone) unites (one with himself) by his grace. The companions who have found God: I am ever a sacrifice to them. Says Nanak, O dear Lord, show mercy; you are the one who adorns (the soul) through the Shabad. Sawan belongs to those happy soul-brides on whose heart the Name of Ram is a necklace. ॥6॥
134.4: In Bhadon, (the soul-bride) whose love is fixed on another has strayed, lost in doubt. She has put on a hundred thousand adornments, (but) they are of no use at all. On the day the body perishes, at that hour (her own people) will call it a pret (the dead). Jam's messengers seize (the soul) and drive it on, and tell no one their secret (where they take it). Those she was bound to in love leave her in an instant and stand aside. She wrings her hands, the body trembles, (its colour) turns from black to white. As one sows, so one reaps: (the body) is the field of deeds. O Nanak, to those who come to God's refuge, God gives the ship of his feet. In Bhadon they are not cast into hell whose protector and loving friend is the Guru. ॥7॥
Pret: one who has died; as soon as the life leaves it, the body is called pret, held unclean and carried out of the house in haste.
134.5: In Assu love wells up (within me): how may I go and meet the Lord? In mind and body there is a great thirst for (his) sight; O mother, if only someone would bring (him) and unite (us). The Sants are helpers (on the way) of love; I have fallen at their feet. Without God, how can peace be found? There is no other place (for it). Those who have tasted the delight of love stay satisfied and fulfilled. Giving up self-conceit, they pray: O God, attach (us) to the hem of your robe. She whom the Lord, the Husband, has united (with himself) does not part (from him) and go anywhere else. Apart from God there is no other; Nanak has come to the Lord's refuge. In Assu they dwell in peace on whom the Lord, the King, has mercy. ॥8॥
135.1: In Katak, (what one meets is) the deeds one has done; no one else can be blamed. Strayed from the Supreme God, one is gripped by every disease. Those who turn their faces away from the Lord suffer separation through births. In a moment, all the pleasures of Maya, as many as they were, have turned bitter. No one can stand between (as a go-between); before whom can they weep day after day? Nothing comes of (one's own) doing; the lot written from the start (is what comes). By great good fortune, if my God is met, then all the pains of separation are lifted. O God, my Master, you who free (beings) from bondage, save Nanak. In Katak, if the Saadh Sangat is found, all anxieties vanish. ॥9॥
135.2: In the month of Maghar they look lovely who sit beside the Lord, their Husband. How can I count the glory of those whom the Master has united (with himself)? With the Lord, in the company of their holy friends, their body and mind have blossomed. Those cut off from the holy remain all alone. Their pain never leaves them; they have fallen into Jam's power. Those who have enjoyed (union with) their God are seen ever standing alert (in his service). The Lord's jewels, gems and rubies (his Name and praises) are set at their throats. Nanak longs for the dust (of the feet) of those who have fallen at God's door, in his refuge. In Maghar God is to be worshipped: (those who do so) are not born again. ॥10॥
135.3: In Poh the frost does not trouble (the bride) whom the Lord, her Husband, has met in close embrace. Her mind is pierced through by (his) lotus feet; her every breath clings to his sight. (She has) the shelter of Govind, Gopal, the King; service of the Master is (her) gain. The poison (of Maya) cannot touch her; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), she is immersed in (God's) virtues. She has met the One from whom she sprang, and is absorbed in true love. The Supreme Lord has taken her by the hand; she will not be parted again. I am a sacrifice a hundred thousand times to the Lord, the Friend, inaccessible, unfathomable. O Nanak, it falls to Narayan to keep the honour of those who have fallen at his door. Poh is lovely, and every comfort is (hers), whom the Carefree (Lord) forgives. ॥11॥
In ਸੋੁਹੰਦਾ the letter ਸ carries two vowel signs (ੋ and ੁ); it is read suhanda, to keep the metre of the line.
135.4: In Magh, let your holy dip be in the company of the holy: bathe in the dust (of their feet). Meditate on the Lord's Name and listen to it, and give it to all. (Then) the filth of the deeds of (many) births is washed off, and pride leaves the mind. One is not lured by lust or anger, and the dog of greed is destroyed. As one walks on the true path, the whole world sings one's praise. Compassion for (all) beings is accepted as (bathing at) the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage and (doing) every deed of merit. The one to whom (God) gives (this) in his mercy is the one who is truly wise. Nanak is a sacrifice to those who have met their God. In Magh they alone are counted pure on whom the perfect Guru is merciful. ॥12॥
On the first day of Magh (Maghi) a bath at a tirath such as Prayag was held to bring great merit.
136.1: In Phagun bliss springs up (in those) to whom the Lord, the Friend, has come and been revealed. The Sants, helpers (on the way) to the Lord, have in their mercy united (them with him). The bed (of the heart) is lovely, all comforts are there; now there is no room for sorrows. The desire of the fortunate bride is fulfilled: she has found the Lord, the King, as her Husband. Gathering together, (her) companions sing songs of joy, raising the songs of Govind. No other is seen like the Lord; no second can be set beside him as his equal. He has set right this world and the next, and given (them) a place that does not shake. He has kept (them) safe from the world-ocean; (such a one) does not run again into birth. The tongue is one, (his) virtues countless; O Nanak, falling at (his) feet, (beings) cross over. In Phagun let him be praised ever, who has not a grain of greed. ॥13॥
136.2: Each and every one who has meditated on the Naam has had (their) affairs fulfilled. Those who have worshipped the Lord, the perfect Guru, are found genuine in the court of the True One. The Lord's feet are a treasury of every comfort; (they) have crossed the terrifying world-ocean, hard (to cross). They have obtained loving devotion; they do not burn in the poison (of Maya). Their falsehoods are gone, duality has fled; they are filled to the full with the True One. They serve the Supreme Lord God, keeping the One in their minds. Every month, day and hour is good for the one on whom he casts his glance of grace. Nanak begs for the gift of your sight: O Lord, show mercy. ॥14॥
136.3: Din Raini: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Let me serve my own True Guru, and remember the Lord through all the days and nights. Giving up self-conceit, let me fall into (his) refuge and speak sweet words with my mouth: (I am) parted birth after birth; unite (me with) the Lord, (my) friend and beloved. O sister, the beings who are parted from the Lord do not dwell in peace. Without the Lord, the Husband, no rest is found; I have searched through all the skies and seen. I am parted by what I myself have done; no one else is to be blamed. O God, show mercy and save (me); there is no other who can do and cause (anything) to be done. O Lord, without you (one must) roll in the dust; to whom shall (we) tell (our) laments? This is Nanak's prayer: that I may see the Lord, the noble One, with my eyes. He hears the anguish of the soul: the Lord, the all-powerful, infinite Being. In death and in life he is to be worshipped, the support of all. In her in-laws' home and in her parents' home (alike, the bride) belongs to that Husband, whose family is vast. He is lofty, inaccessible, of fathomless wisdom; he has no end, no near shore and no far shore. He is pleased by the service (in which one) becomes the dust of the Sants' feet. He is the Master of the meek, the merciful Lord, the uplifter of the fallen. From the beginning, through the ages, the Creator, whose Name is true, has kept (all). No one knows his worth; there is no one who can weigh him. He dwells within mind and body; O Nanak, there is no reckoning (of him). To those who serve God day and night, I am ever a sacrifice. The Sants worship him for ever and ever, the forgiver of all, who fashioned soul and body, and in his mercy gave life. Through the Guru's Shabad let him be worshipped; let his pure mantra be repeated. His worth cannot be told; the Supreme God is without end. The one in whose mind Narayan dwells is called fortunate. The longing of the soul is fulfilled when the Master, the Husband, is met. Nanak lives by repeating (the Name of) the Lord; all faults are destroyed. The being who does not forget (him) day or night turns green (with life). O God, you are full of every power; (you are) the refuge of me, the humble one. O Lord, I have taken hold of your shelter in my mind; I live by repeating (your) Name again and again. O God, show your mercy, that I may stay merged in the dust (of the feet) of your servants. As you keep me, so I live; what you give, I wear and eat. O God, have me make that effort (by which), meeting the Saadh (the Guru), I may sing (your) praises. No other place comes to mind: where am I to go and cry out? O destroyer of ignorance, dispeller of darkness, lofty, inaccessible, immeasurable (Lord), unite with yourself, O Lord, the mind that is parted; this is Nanak's (one) aim. All blessings come on that day, O Lord, when I touch the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
Din Raini (day and night) is the title of this bani of four stanzas; the words recur in its lines.
Manj: my, of me (a Lahndi form); manj nimani thaau, the refuge of me, the humble one.
137.1: Vaar Majh ki: by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji), with saloks; to be sung to the tune of Malak Murid and Chandrahara Sohia. There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace. Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Guru is the Giver; the Guru is the home of snow (the source of coolness); the Guru is the lamp in the three worlds. O Nanak, (from him comes) the imperishable treasure; when the mind trusts (him), there is peace. ॥1॥
Malak Murid and Chandrahara Sohia: by tradition, two chiefs of Akbar's time (of the Malak and Sohi clans) whose fight the bards sang as a vaar; this vaar is to be sung to its tune (dhuni).
137.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In the first (stage of life, the child) is lovingly drawn to the milk of the breast; in the second, (it) comes to know its mother and father; in the third, (it knows its) brother, brother's wife and sister; in the fourth, the love of play springs up; in the fifth, the running after food and drink; in the sixth, lust, which does not ask about caste; in the seventh, gathering (things), he makes his dwelling in a house; in the eighth, anger (rises), and the body wears away; in the ninth, (the hair turns) white and the breath comes in gasps; in the tenth, he is burned and turns to ashes. The companions who went (with him to the pyre) cried out in loud wails; the swan (the soul) has flown, and asks the way. He came and he went; even his name has died. Afterwards, (they say:) call the crows to the leaf-plate. O Nanak, the manmukh's love is blind; without the Guru, the world has drowned. ॥2॥
Patal: a plate of leaves. In the shraadh rites for the dead, food is set out on leaf-plates and the crows are called to it, in the belief that it reaches the departed.
138.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). At ten (one is) in childhood, at twenty in the age of desire; at thirty, one is called handsome; at forty, one is in full bloom; at fifty, the foot starts to slip; at sixty, old age comes; at seventy, one loses one's wits; at eighty, one cannot attend to one's affairs; at ninety, one keeps to the bed, and knows no strength of one's own at all. I have sought, I have searched, I have seen; says Nanak, the world is a white mansion made of smoke. ॥3॥
138.2: You are the Creator, the all-pervading Being, the Inaccessible; you yourself brought forth the creation. You made it of colour upon colour, in many, many ways and kinds. You know (it), you who made (it); the whole play is yours. Some come, some rise up and go; without the Name (all) die and depart. The Gurmukhs are dyed deep red, dyed in the colour of the Lord's love. Serve him, the True One, the Stainless, the Lord, the all-pervading Being, the Maker. You yourself alone are all-wise, the great Being, great indeed. O my True One, I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who meditate on you with mind and heart. ॥1॥
138.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Placing the soul (in it), (God) fashioned the body, and kept it, shaping its form. With the eyes it sees, with the tongue it speaks; in the ears the power of hearing dwells. With the feet it walks, with the hands it works; what is given (to it) it wears and eats. Him who made and fashioned it, it does not know; the blind one does blind deeds. When (the vessel) breaks, it becomes a potsherd; that shape cannot be fashioned again. O Nanak, without the Guru there is no honour; without honour (God's grace) no one gets across. ॥1॥
138.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). To hold what is given dearer than the One who gives it: know the manmukh to be such. His understanding, his wisdom, his cleverness: in what words can they be told? What one does sitting hidden within becomes known in all four directions. Whoever practises dharma gets the name of the righteous; by committing sin one is known as a sinner. O Creator, you yourself play out all these plays; what other can we name and speak of? As long as your light is (in the body), so long it is you who speak in that light; without the light, let anyone do anything at all, and I will see and acknowledge it. O Nanak, through the Guru the one Lord, skilful and all-knowing, has come into sight. ॥2॥
138.5: You yourself created the world, and you yourself set it to its worldly business. Giving it the drugging herb of attachment, you have led the world astray from yourself. Within (it) is the fire of craving; hungry and thirsty, (the world) is never sated. This world is nothing but anxiety; (in it, beings) die and are born, come and go. Without the True Guru attachment does not break; all have grown weary performing (ritual) deeds. Through the Guru's teaching the Naam is meditated on; when it pleased you, (the soul) was sated in peace. (Such a one) saves his whole family line; blessed is the mother who bore him. Lovely are the glory and the understanding of one who has joined his mind to the Lord. ॥2॥
139.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Seeing without eyes, hearing without ears, walking without feet, working without hands, speaking without a tongue: so one dies while living. O Nanak, it is by recognising (the Lord's) Hukam that one then meets the Master. ॥1॥
Seeing without eyes and the rest: the senses held back from their pull to vice, so that one lives in the world dead to it.
139.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). (The Lord) is seen, is heard of, is known (in his creation), yet the taste (of meeting him) is not had. How can one who is lame, handless and blind run and fall upon (his) neck? If one makes the fear (of God) one's feet, love one's hands, and attention (held on him) one's eyes, says Nanak: O wise (soul-bride), in this way union with the Husband comes about. ॥2॥
139.3: For ever and ever you are the One; you yourself have staged the play of duality. Creating Haumai and pride, you placed greed within beings. Keep (them) as it pleases you; all do only what you make them do. Some you forgive and unite with yourself; it is you who have set them in the Guru's teaching. Some stand ready, doing your service; without the Name nothing else pleases them. To them any other work is worthless; some you have set to the true work. Son, wife and family are there, yet some, who are pleasing to you, stay untouched (by them). They are pure within and without, merged in the True Name. ॥3॥
139.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Should I make a cave in the mountain of gold, or (dwell) in the waters of the netherworld; whether on the earth or in the sky, should I stay upside down, on my head; should I cover my body wholly in clothes, and make washing my constant work; should I cry aloud the Vedas, white, red, yellow and black; should I live filthy and grimy: (all this is) the vice of an evil understanding. Nanak, reflecting on the Shabad, asks only this: may there be no I-ness and no me-and-mine, and may I not be (a self apart) at all. ॥1॥

The mountain of gold: Sumer (Meru), the golden mountain at the centre of the world in the Puranas. In old tradition each of the four Vedas has its colour: the Sama white, the Rig red, the Yajur yellow, the Atharva black.
139.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Washing his clothes, he washes his body, and thinks himself (a man of) self-restraint. The filth stuck within he does not know; he scrubs and scrubs, washing (himself) from outside. The blind one has strayed and fallen into the net of Jam. He takes what belongs to another for his own, and in Haumai he suffers pain. O Nanak, when through the Guru Haumai is broken, then one meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har; he repeats the Naam, worships the Naam alone, and through the Naam is merged in peace. ॥2॥
139.6: Ordaining their union, (the Lord) has joined the body and the swan (the soul). The very One who created (them) has also ordained (their) parting. The fool goes on enjoying pleasures, (the root of) every pain. From pleasure diseases arise, through the sins committed. From joy spring sorrow and parting; so (beings) are brought forth and wasted away. Keeping the reckonings of fools, (man) has taken on a wrangle (of birth and death). The settlement lies in the True Guru's hands; he has put an end to the wrangle. What the Creator does, that alone will be; (no one's) driving can drive it otherwise. ॥4॥
139.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One who tells lies and eats carrion (what is another's by right) and goes to instruct others is robbed himself, and has his companions robbed as well. O Nanak, such a leader is found out. ॥1॥
140.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The one within whom the True One dwells utters the True Name with his mouth, and speaks the truth. He himself walks on the Lord's path, and puts others on the Lord's path. If what lies ahead is a place of pilgrimage (of clean, open water), the filth comes off; bathing in a stagnant pond, one gathers still more filth. The True Guru is the perfect place of pilgrimage, who meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, night and day. He is set free himself, with his family, and, giving the Name of the Lord, Har Har, he frees the whole world. Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to the one who repeats (the Naam) himself and has others repeat the Naam. ॥2॥
140.2: Some gather roots and tubers to eat, and make their dwelling in some corner of the forest. Some put on saffron robes and wander about as Yogis and Sannyasis. (Yet) within them is great craving, the longing for clothes and food. Wasting their life in vain, they are neither householders nor renunciants. Jamkaal does not lift from their heads, (for in them is) desire of the three kinds. Through the Guru's teaching death does not come near, when one becomes the servant of (the Lord's) servants. With the true Shabad and the True One in the mind, one is detached while living at home. O Nanak, those who serve their True Guru become free of (worldly) hopes. ॥5॥
140.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If blood stains the clothes, the garment becomes unclean; those who drink the blood of men, how can their mind be pure? Says Nanak: take the name of God on your lips with a clean heart; all else is the world's show, and (by it) you do false deeds. ॥1॥
Paleet (Persian palid): unclean; a garment stained with blood is held unfit for the namaz.
140.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). When I am nothing (within), what can I tell (others)? With no virtue in me, what can I make myself out to be? Through what I do and what I say, I am full (of filth); again and again I am soiled, and I wash. I do not understand myself, yet I make the people understand: such is the leader I become. O Nanak, one who, being blind himself, shows (others) the way has all his companions robbed. Going on ahead (to the world beyond), he is struck again and again on the face: then such a leader is found out. ॥2॥
140.5: In all the months and seasons, in every ghari and muhurat, you are to be contemplated. By calculations (of lucky days) no one has found you, O True One, unseen and infinite. The learned man in whom are greed, avarice and pride is to be called a fool. It is the Name that should be read, the Name that should be understood, reflecting through the Guru's teaching. Those who through the Guru's teaching have earned the wealth of the Naam have their storehouses filled with devotion. Those who have accepted the pure Naam are found true at the door of the True One. The One whose are the soul and the breath of life: his infinite light is within (every being). You alone are the true banker; the rest of the world are pedlars. ॥6॥
140.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Make compassion your mosque, faith your prayer mat, and honest, lawful earning your Quran; modesty your circumcision, a gentle nature your fast: in this way become a Muslim. (Make) good conduct your Kaaba, truth your Pir, and good deeds your kalma and namaz; (let) what pleases him be your rosary: (then), O Nanak, he keeps your honour. ॥1॥
Musalla: the prayer mat; sunnat: circumcision; roza: the fast; the Kaaba: the shrine at Mecca towards which Muslims pray; Pir: a spiritual guide; kalma: the declaration of faith; tasbi: the rosary.
141.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, what is another's by right is (as) the pig to the one (the Muslim) and the cow to the other (the Hindu). The Guru, the Pir, will vouch (for one) only if one does not eat carrion. No one goes to paradise by talk; one is saved by practising truth. Put spices into what is forbidden, and it still does not become lawful. O Nanak, by false talk only falsehood is gained. ॥2॥
Halal and haram: what Islamic law allows and what it forbids. Pork is forbidden to the Muslim, and the cow is sacred to the Hindu.
141.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The prayers are five, their times are five, and the five have five names. (Let) the first be truth, the second lawful earning, the third (asking) God for the good of all; the fourth a clean intention and mind, the fifth the praise and glory (of God). Reciting the kalma of good conduct, one may then call oneself a Muslim. O Nanak, as many as are false (to these), the honour of the false is false. ॥3॥
141.3: Some trade in jewels and precious things, some deal in glass. When the True Guru is pleased, the stores of jewels within are found. Without the Guru no one has found them; the blind, the false, have died barking (from door to door). The manmukhs have rotted away in duality and died; they do not understand (true) reflection. Apart from the One there is no other; before whom can they cry out? Some, without wealth, are ever barking (from door to door); the coffers of some are full. Without the Name there is no other wealth; all the rest is poison (of Maya), mere ashes. O Nanak, (the Lord) himself causes (all) to be done and himself does (all); by his Hukam he sets (all) right. ॥7॥
141.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). To be called a Muslim is hard; if one truly is one, then let one be called a Muslim. First of all, let him hold the faith dear, and, as a burnisher scrapes off rust, let his possessions go from him. Becoming a Muslim under the guidance of the faith, let him put away the delusion of death and life. Let him accept the Lord's will upon his head, hold the Creator (as the doer of all), and lose his self. Then, O Nanak, if he is merciful to all beings, let him be called a Muslim. ॥1॥
Maskal (miskala): the burnisher that scrapes the rust off a blade; so, giving his possessions away, he scrapes off the rust of pride in them.
141.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). If one forsakes lust, anger, falsehood and slander, gives up Maya and does away with pride; if, giving up lust, he gives up attachment to woman, then amid the black stain (anjan) of Maya he finds the Immaculate (Lord); if, giving up vanity and pride and the love of son and wife, giving up thirst and hope, he fixes his attention on the Lord (Ram), (then,) O Nanak, the True One comes to dwell in the mind, and through the true Shabad he merges in the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
141.6: Kings, subjects, chiefs: none will remain. Shops, cities and bazaars will fall by (his) Hukam. The strong and handsome gateways the fool thinks his own. Storehouses full of riches are emptied in an instant. Arab horses, chariots, camels, elephants with their trappings, gardens, lands, houses and homes: where are they, that (he thought) his own? (Where are) the tents, the beds of woven tape, the screens of red satin? O Nanak, the Giver alone is true, ever-abiding; he is recognised through his creation. ॥8॥

Sikdar: a chief; taji: a horse of Arab breed; tukhar: a camel; pakhar: the howdah and trappings of an elephant; saraiche: the screens round a tent; lalti: of red satin; sinakhat (Persian): recognition.
141.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Should the rivers become cows, and the springs turn to milk and ghee; should the whole earth become sugar, and (my) soul rejoice every day; should the mountain turn to gold and silver, set with diamonds and rubies: even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥1॥
142.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If the eighteen loads (all plant life) became fruit, rich and melting in taste, if the moon and the sun, both ever circling, were held still, and my seat became unshakeable, even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥2॥
The eighteen loads: all plant life; an old belief holds that one leaf of every kind of tree and plant, weighed together, comes to eighteen bhaar (an old measure of weight).
142.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If pain were to strike my body, and the two ill-omened planets, Rahu (and Ketu, were set upon me), if bloodthirsty kings were set over my head, and (your) love were shown (to me) in this form, even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥3॥
Rahu and Ketu: two ill-omened planets of astrology; in the Puranic story they are the demons who eclipse the sun and the moon.
142.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If fire and frost were my clothing, and wind my food, if the enchanting women of heaven were (mine) — O Nanak, all of it must pass away — even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥4॥
142.4: One who does evil in secret does not know the Master (to be present); he is called mad, (for) he does not know his own self. Strife is an evil thing in the world; in quarrelling one wastes away. Without the Name, one is consumed in evil and in wandering doubt. There are two paths; the one who knows the One will come through. The speaker of kufr (falsehood) will burn, sunk in his kufr. The whole world is glorious and wondrous if one is merged in the True One; one comes through at (the Lord's) door, in (his) court, if one sheds the self. ॥9॥
This pauri uses Persian and Arabic words: badfaili (evil deed), gaibaana (in secret), devaana (mad), kufr (falsehood, denial of God), subhaan (glorious, wondrous), deevaan (court).
142.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). He alone has lived in whose mind that (Lord) dwells; O Nanak, no one else (truly) lives. If (one empty of the Name) lives at all, he goes with his honour stripped from him; all that he eats is forbidden. His delight is in power, his delight in wealth; steeped in that delight, he dances without shame. O Nanak, he is cheated and plundered; without the Name, he has lost his honour and gone. ॥1॥
142.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). What comes of eating (rich food), what of wearing (fine clothes), when that True One is not in the mind? What are dried fruits, what is ghee and sweet gur, what fine flour, what meat? What are clothes, what a soft bed, and the pleasures and delights enjoyed (on it)? What are armies, what mace-bearers and attendants, and coming to dwell in palaces? O Nanak, without the True Name, all this array is perishable. ॥2॥
142.7: What lies in the hands of caste? It is truth that is assayed. If poison is in the hand, one dies on tasting it (whatever one's caste). The rule of the True One is known (to be so) in every age. One who obeys (his) Hukam is a chief at (his) door, in (his) court. Obeying the command is the task for which the Master has sent (us into the world). The drummer (the Guru) has sounded this thought through the Shabad. Some have mounted, some have saddled (their horses); some have tied up their loads, some have galloped away. ॥10॥
Tabalbaaj: an army's drummer, who beats out the order to march; saakhti (Persian): saddling and harnessing a horse; taakhti: a gallop.
142.8: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). When (the crop) ripened, it was cut; only the stubble and the hedge were left standing. Bearded ears and all, it was threshed, and the grain was taken out by winnowing away the straw. Setting together the two stones of the mill, (people) came and sat down to grind. Those (grains) that stayed at the door (of the mill) were saved; O Nanak, a marvel has been seen. ॥1॥
At the door: at the mill's central opening, by the pivot; grains that stay there are not ground between the stones.
142.9: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). See how the sweet (cane) is cut down; cut and stripped, it is bound with ropes into bundles. Laying it between the press's wooden rollers, strong men deal out (as it were) its punishment. The juice pressed out is poured into the cauldron; it heats and (as it were) wails. Even the crushed pulp is gathered up and burnt in the fire (beneath the cauldron). Says Nanak, for sweetness one is brought to ruin (like this); come, people, and see. ॥2॥
Patreeai is a verb, one is brought to ruin; mithai: because of sweetness (not the sweet-leaved cane).
143.1: Some do not keep death in mind; their hopes are many. Day after day they die and are born again, and belong to no one. In their own mind and heart they call themselves good; (but) the King of Death keeps those manmukhs in his sight, day after day. The manmukhs are false to the salt they eat; they have not known what (the Lord has done for them). They bow only under constraint, and so do not please the Master. The one who meets the True One, with the Name on his lips, will please the Master; (all) will salute him on his throne; he will receive what was written (for him). ॥11॥
143.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). What harm can water too deep to stand in do a fish? What harm can the sky do a bird? What harm can frost do a stone? What does married home life mean to a eunuch? Smear a dog with sandalwood, and its nature is still a dog's. If a deaf man is instructed, and the Simritis are recited (to him), if a blind man is kept in the light, with fifty lamps burning, if gold is laid before a grazing herd, it still picks out the grass and eats it, if iron is put (in the fire) to be reduced to calx, it melts, but it does not turn into cotton: O Nanak, such are the ways of a fool; whenever he speaks, it is ever to (someone's) harm. ॥1॥
Taaroo: water so deep it can only be crossed by swimming; maaran: reducing a metal to calx (kushta) by fire.
143.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If bronze or gold or iron cracks, the smith joins it again with fire. If a husband breaks with his wife, in the world the bond is formed again through sons. The king makes his demand; when it is given, the bond is formed. For the hungry, the bond (with life) is formed when they eat. Famines are mended by rivers in spate and pouring rain. The bond of love is formed by sweet words. One is bound to the Vedas (the scriptures) when one speaks the truth. The dead stay bound (to the world) by the good and the charity (they did). By such bonds the world goes on. For a fool, the bond is formed by blows to his face. Nanak speaks this considered thought: through praise (of the Lord), the bond is formed at his court. ॥2॥
143.4: God himself fashions the creation, and himself takes thought (for it). Some are counterfeit, some genuine; he himself is the one who assays. The genuine go into (his) treasury; the counterfeit are cast outside. The counterfeit are flung out of the True Court; to whom can they cry out? If they run and fall in behind the True Guru, that is the excellent course. The True Guru makes the counterfeit genuine; through the Shabad he sets (them) right. Through love and devotion for the Guru, (they) are accepted in the True Court. What reckoning can anyone make of those whom the Creator himself has forgiven? ॥12॥
143.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The whole world, pirs, sheikhs and rajas, (all go) beneath the earth; emperors pass away; God alone abides, ever greater. You alone are, you alone. ॥1॥
