This salok is in Persian: ham (hama, all), jer jimi (beneath the earth), masaaik (sheikhs), me ravad (goes, passes away), afjoo (afzun, ever increasing).
143.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Neither gods nor demons nor men, nor Siddhas nor seekers (stay) on the earth. The One alone is; who else is there? You alone are, you alone. ॥2॥
Asti ek digar kui (Persian): One alone is; who is the other? Ek tui: you alone.
144.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Neither men who dispense justice, nor the seven (nether worlds) under the earth (endure). The One alone is; who else is there? You alone are, you alone. ॥3॥
Daade dihand (Persian daad dihand): givers of justice.
144.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the sphere of the heavens, nor the seven continents, nor the waters, nor food nor wind: none of them is lasting. You alone are, you alone. ॥4॥
144.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Sustenance lies in no one's hand (but yours); for all, hope in the One is enough. The One alone is; who else is there? You alone are, you alone. ॥5॥
Persian words: dast (hand), aa kase (of anyone), hamaa raa (for all), vase (bas, enough).
144.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Birds have no gold tied in a knot of cloth; they look in hope to the trees and the water; the Giver is he (alone). You alone are, you alone. ॥6॥
Persian words: parandae (birds), giraah (knot), jar (gold, wealth), darakhat (trees), aab (water).
144.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, what is inscribed on the brow none can wipe away. He alone puts power (into beings), and he alone takes it away. You alone are, you alone. ॥7॥
144.6: (O Lord,) your Hukam is true and abiding; it is known through the Guru. By the Guru's teaching, shedding the self, the True One is recognised. True is your court; the Shabad is the pass (that admits one there). Reflecting on the true Shabad, (the Gurmukhs) merge in the True One. The manmukhs ever deal in falsehood, gone astray in doubt. Their dwelling is in filth; they have never known the relish (of the Name). Without the Name, they come and go in pain. O Nanak, the Assayer is (the Lord) himself, who has told the counterfeit from the genuine. ॥13॥
144.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Lions, hawks, falcons and kuhi hawks: these (God, if he wills,) feeds on grass; those who eat grass he feeds on meat: such are the ways he sets going. He brings sandbanks into view in the midst of rivers, and turns dry plains into bottomless waters. He sets a worm upon a throne, and turns armies to ashes. All the beings that live, live by drawing breath; (but if) he keeps (one) alive, what (need is there) of breath? O Nanak, just as it pleases the True One, so he gives (each) its morsel. ॥1॥
Charg and kuhi: hunting birds of the hawk kind; giraah: a morsel, daily bread.
144.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Some feed on flesh, some eat grass; some receive the thirty-six (kinds of) nectar-sweet foods; some, dwelling in the earth, eat earth; some, the counters of breath (who practise pranayama), are bent on counting their breaths; some, devoted to the Formless One, rest on the support of the Name. The Giver lives on; no one dies (for want of food). O Nanak, they are robbed in whose mind he does not dwell. ॥2॥
144.9: The work the Perfect Guru sets is done only through (God's) grace. Through the Guru's teaching one sheds self-conceit and meditates on the Naam. Taken up with any other work, one wastes one's life. Without the Name, whatever one wears and eats is all poison. Praising the True Shabad, one merges in the True One. Without serving the True Guru there is no dwelling in peace; one comes (into birth) again and again. The world is counterfeit capital; (trading with it) one earns falsehood alone. O Nanak, praising the True One, the genuine, one departs with honour. ॥14॥
144.10: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord,) if it pleases you, (beings) play music and sing; if it pleases you, they bathe in (holy) waters. When it pleases you, they smear (their bodies with) ashes and sound the call of the horn (singi). When it pleases you, they read the Kateb and are called mullahs and sheikhs. When it pleases you, they become kings and enjoy flavours of every kind in plenty. When it pleases you, they wield the sword, and heads are severed from necks. When it pleases you, they go to foreign lands, and hearing (their) news, come back home. When it pleases you, they are absorbed in the Name; those who walk in your will are dear to you. Nanak offers one prayer: all the others practise only falsehood. ॥1॥
145.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord,) since you are great, all greatness is (yours); from the good, only good comes. Since you are true, everyone is true; no one at all is false. Speaking, seeing, talking, walking, living and dying: (all this is the spread of) Maya. Having fashioned his Hukam, he keeps (all) within the Hukam; O Nanak, (it is) the True One himself (who does so). ॥2॥
145.2: Serving the True Guru without reserve, one dispels doubt. The work the True Guru bids is the work to be done. When the True Guru is merciful, the Naam is meditated on. The profit of devotion is the highest (profit), and it is found through the Guru. As a manmukh, one lives in falsehood and darkness, and earns falsehood alone. Going to the door of the True One, one utters the Truth (the True Name). (Then,) through the Truth, one is called within the mansion of the True One. O Nanak, one who ever holds fast to the Truth is truthful, and merges in the True One. ॥15॥
145.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Kalyug is a knife, kings are butchers; dharma has grown wings and flown away. Falsehood is the dark night of the new moon; the moon of truth is not seen to have risen anywhere. I have searched (for it) until I am bewildered; in the darkness no path is (to be seen). Caught in Haumai, (the world) weeps over its pain. Says Nanak, by what means can (it) be set free? ॥1॥
145.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Kalyug, (the Lord's) praise is the light shining forth in the world. (But) only some rare one crosses over (the darkness) through the Guru. The one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace, to him he gives (this light); O Nanak, through the Guru that one receives the jewel (of the Name). ॥2॥
145.5: Between the devotees and the worldly there has never been a match. The Creator himself makes no mistake; no one can lead him into error. The devotees he has himself united (with him), who have practised truth and truth alone. The worldly he has himself led astray, who, speaking falsehood again and again, have eaten poison. They do not grasp that they must depart; they have let the poison of lust and anger grow. The devotees serve the Lord, who have meditated on the Naam night and day. Those who, becoming the servants of (his) servants, have rid themselves of self from within, at the Master's door their faces are bright; the True Shabad has made them beautiful. ॥16॥
145.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those who in the early morning praised (the Lord) and meditated on (him) with a single mind: they alone are the perfect shahs (the truly rich), who at the proper hour fought (their own mind) unto death. In the second (watch) many paths (open), and the mind's thoughts are scattered. Many fall into the fathomless (sea of the world); they go under and cannot get out. In the third (watch) morsels go into mouths; hunger and thirst both bark (for more). What is eaten turns to ash, yet the friendship with eating (remains). In the fourth (watch) drowsiness comes; shutting his eyes, (man) passes as if into the other world (of deep sleep). Rising again, he starts up the strife, (as though) he had marked out an arena for a hundred years (of life). Every hour and every moment (is blessed), if through all eight watches there is the fear (of God). O Nanak, (if) the Master dwells in the mind, (that) is the true bathing. ॥1॥
146.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). They alone are the perfect shahs who have found the Perfect One. Through all eight watches they stay free of care, (dyed) in the love of the One. Rare are those found (absorbed) in the sight and the form of the Unfathomable. By perfect grace (one meets) the Perfect Guru, whose word is perfect. O Nanak, if the Perfect One makes (someone) perfect, (that one's) weight does not fall short. ॥2॥
146.2: (O Lord,) when you are (mine), what need have I of anyone else? I tell the truth. (But the soul-bride) robbed by the thief of worldly affairs does not find (the Lord's) mansion. Because of this hard heart, (her) service is wasted. The body in which the Truth is not found is broken and shaped (again and again). How can (it) weigh true in the balance against the full weight? No one calls (it) short, if Haumai is gone (from within). The genuine, once assayed, are taken in at the door of the All-seeing One. This merchandise is had at one shop alone: from the Perfect Guru. ॥17॥
146.3: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The eight watches are eight parts (of time); the ninth part is the body. In it is the one Naam, the nine treasures; (the fortunate) seek (there) the Lord, deep in virtues. The fortunate have praised (him), O Nanak, taking the Guru as their pir. In the fourth watch, as morning nears, a longing wells up in those whose awareness is awake. Their friendship is with the rivers (of the holy company), and the True Name is in their mind and on their lips. There the Amrit (of the Name) is shared out; by (his) grace the gift is received. The body, (like) gold, is tried on the touchstone, and takes on a fine lustre. If the Assayer's glance of grace is on it, it is not put to the fire again. In the (other) seven watches, truthful living is good, and one should sit with the learned. There (in their company) sin and virtue are weighed, and the capital of falsehood runs down. There the counterfeit are thrown out, and the genuine are praised. To speak (of one's woes) is idle, O Nanak; pain and pleasure are in the Master's hands. ॥1॥
146.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Air is the Guru, water the father, and the earth the great mother. Day and night are the two nurses, the female and the male; the whole world plays (in their care). In (God's) presence, Dharam (Raj) reads out the good deeds and the bad. By their own deeds, some are near (God) and some far. Those who meditated on the Naam have gone, their toil accomplished. O Nanak, their faces are bright, and many others have been set free along with them. ॥2॥
146.5: The True Guru has shown that love (for the Lord) is the true food. (One who takes this food) is content in the True One alone, and blossoms in the True One. In the true fortress, the true village, in his own home, he dwells. Through the True Guru's favour (comes) the Name, and one rejoices in (the Lord's) love. No one reaches the court of the True One by falsehood. Uttering lie upon lie, one loses that mansion. With the True Shabad as one's pass, no barrier is met (on the way). Hearing, understanding and uttering the Truth, one is called into (the Lord's) mansion. ॥18॥
147.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If I were to wear fire, build my house in snow, and make iron my food; if I drank down all sorrows like water, and moved the earth at my call; if I set the sky on a balance and weighed it, with a tank (a tiny weight) on the other pan; if I grew so vast that I could not be contained, and led everyone by a nose-string; if there were such power in my mind that I could do (anything) myself and have it done at my word: as great as the Master is, so great are his gifts; (were) the Lord of the Will to give and give (me all this, it would still be little). O Nanak, the one on whom he casts his glance of grace has glory through the True Name. ॥1॥
147.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The mouth has never had its fill of speaking, nor the ears of hearing. The eyes have never had their fill of seeing; (each sense) is a buyer of one kind of quality alone. The hunger of the hungry does not leave them; hunger is not ended by talk. O Nanak, the hungry one is sated only when, uttering (the Lord's) virtues, he merges in the Virtuous One. ॥2॥
147.3: Without the True One, all is false; only falsehood is earned. Without the True One, the dealer in falsehood is tied up and led away. Without the True One, the body is ash, and to ash it returns. Without the True One, all that one wears and eats only (feeds) hunger. Without the True One, through falsehood, (his) court is not reached. Clinging to false greed, one loses (the Lord's) mansion. The whole world has been cheated by the cheat (falsehood); (so) one comes and goes. The fire of craving in the body is put out through the Shabad. ॥19॥
147.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, the Guru is the tree of contentment; dharma is its blossom, and divine knowledge its fruit. Full of the sap (of love), it stays ever green; through (God's) grace and meditation (its fruit) ripens. One who eats (it) tastes the delights of (union with) the Husband (Lord); (this) is the gift above all gifts. ॥1॥
147.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (The Guru is) a golden tree: its leaves are coral, its flowers jewels and rubies; on it grow fruits of gems, the words spoken by (his) mouth; in his heart of hearts he is in bliss. O Nanak, (the one) on whom there is (God's) grace, and on whose face and forehead (such) destiny is written: (for that one) the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are in the Guru's feet, and he worships them ever as the highest. Cruelty, attachment, greed and anger: all four are streams of fire. (Those who) fall in burn, O Nanak; by (God's) grace, clinging (to the Guru's feet), one crosses over. ॥2॥
Hansu here is hinsa, cruelty, not the swan.
147.6: Die while you are alive; killing (craving) so, one has no regrets (at the end). False is this world; only a rare one has grasped (it). (Man) does not set his love on the True One, and runs after worldly affairs. (Yet) cruel death, death the destroyer, hangs over the head of the world. By (the Lord's) Hukam, Jandar (the brute, Death's messenger) stands over (each) head, and strikes when his chance comes. (God) himself gives (his) love, and (then) it is enshrined in the mind. Not a moment, not an instant's delay (is allowed) when (life's) measure is full. By the Guru's grace, understanding (this), one merges in the True One. ॥20॥
147.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The bitter gourd and the colocynth, poison, the swallow-wort, the thorn-apple and the neem fruit: (O Lord,) these (bitter things) dwell in the mind and in the mouth of the one into whose thoughts you do not come. O Nanak, to whom can (their state) be told? Bereft of (God's) grace, they wander about. ॥1॥
147.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The intellect is a bird; with its past deeds (kirat) beside it, it is now high, now low. Now it perches on the sandalwood tree, now on a branch of the swallow-wort, and now (there is in it) a lofty love (for God). O Nanak, (all) are made to move by (his) Hukam; this has been the Master's way (from the first). ॥2॥
148.1: Countless people give their accounts (of God), and having told and told, they depart. The Vedas give their expositions, (yet) his limit cannot be found. By reading, his secret is not found; it is found when understanding dawns. Through the garb of the six orders (khat darshan), who has merged in the True One? The True Being is beyond seeing; through the Shabad he becomes lovely (to the mind). The one who has faith in the Name of the Countless One reaches (his) court. He bows to the Creator, and as a minstrel he sings (his praise). O Nanak, he enshrines in his mind the One who is in every age. ॥21॥
148.2: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). One who knows only the charm for scorpions, yet goes and lays hold of snakes, sets a firebrand to himself with his own hands. The Master's Hukam has gone forth from the very first: through overreaching, one is struck down. The manmukh who sets himself against the Gurmukh drowns by (the Lord's) true justice. Over both sides the Master himself (stands); he watches and judges between them. O Nanak, know it so: everything is (done) in his Will. ॥1॥
148.3: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). O Nanak, if one assays oneself, then know (that one) to be an assayer. One who knows both the illness and its remedy is a wise physician. Such a one starts no quarrels on the road (of life), knowing himself a guest (here). He speaks knowing the Root (of all), and brings harm upon what harms (him, the vices). One who does not walk by greed and abides in the Truth: that go-between is accepted. (If someone) aims an arrow at the sky, how can the shaft reach (it)? It lies beyond, out of reach; know that (the arrow falls back on) the archer. ॥2॥
148.4: The soul-brides who love their Husband are adorned with love. They worship day and night, and do not stop, though held back. Made beautiful by the Shabad, they dwell in the (Lord's) mansion. Thoughtful, they offer a true prayer. Having come by his Hukam, they look beautiful beside the Master. As his companions they make their prayer, loving (him) with all their heart. Without the Name, cursed is the dwelling (in the world), and shame on such a life. She whom he has adorned through the Shabad has drunk the Amrit (of the Name). ॥22॥
Savaareeaas: the ending -aas marks the doer as he (God): she whom he has adorned.
148.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The desert is never sated by rain, and the hunger of fire never leaves it. No king was ever sated by his kingdom; and who has ever filled up the oceans? O Nanak, what need to ask how great the longing for the True Name is? (It never ends.) ॥1॥
148.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Fruitless is the birth of that one, so long as he does not know Brahm (God). By the Guru's grace many cross over the ocean of the world. (God) is the Cause of creation, all-powerful: says Nanak, after reflection, the cause (of all) is in the power of the Creator, who has established his power (in all creation). ॥2॥
The first two lines are in Sahaskriti, a Sanskrit-coloured idiom: tasi (tasya), of him; janamasi, (his) birth is; jaavatu (yaavat), so long as. Ke means many, for the verb tarahi is plural.
148.7: The minstrel has come to dwell at the Master's court. Praising the True Master, the lotus (of his heart) has blossomed. Receiving the full (station) from the Master, he is glad at heart. He has struck down and driven out his foes (the vices), and his friends rejoice. Those who serve the True Guru: (he) has shown them the true path. Reflecting on the true Shabad, they have destroyed (the fear of) death. Made beautiful by the Shabad, the minstrel tells of the One beyond telling. O Nanak, gathering the capital of virtues, he has met the beloved Lord. ॥23॥
149.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Born of wrongs, they commit wrongs, and so they sink (ever deeper) into wrongs. These do not come off at all with washing, though they try a hundred washings. O Nanak, if (God) pardons, they are pardoned; otherwise they are beaten with shoes. ॥1॥
Paahee (Sanskrit upaanah): shoes; to be beaten with shoes is the punishment of disgrace.
149.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, it is idle prattle to ask for comforts and leave out pains. Comfort and pain are both robes (given) at (the Lord's) door, which human beings come (into the world) and wear. Where speaking only ends in defeat, there silence is best. ॥2॥
149.3: Having looked in all four directions, I searched my own self within, (and saw that) the True Being, the Unseen, has created (the world) and watches over it. To one lost in the wilderness, the Guru showed the way. Wonderful is the True Guru, the true one, (through whom) the True One is cherished (in the heart). The jewel (of the Name) was found within the house itself, (when the Guru) lit the lamp (of wisdom). Those who hold to the Truth praise (God) through the true Shabad and are at peace. Those without fear (of God) are seized by fear; they waste away in their pride. Strayed from the Name, the world wanders about out of step. ॥24॥
149.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (The world) is born in fear and dies in fear, and fear stays ever in its mind. O Nanak, whoever dies in the fear (of God): that one's coming (into the world) is blessed. ॥1॥
149.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One may live long, very long, without the fear (of God), and enjoy pleasure upon pleasure; (yet) O Nanak, if one dies without the fear (of God), one rises and departs with a blackened face. ॥2॥
149.6: When the True Guru is merciful, faith is made whole. When the True Guru is merciful, one never grieves. When the True Guru is merciful, pain is not known at all. When the True Guru is merciful, the Lord's love is enjoyed. When the True Guru is merciful, what fear of Jam can there be? When the True Guru is merciful, the body is at peace for ever. When the True Guru is merciful, one finds the nine treasures. When the True Guru is merciful, one merges in the True One. ॥25॥
149.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). They have the hair of their heads plucked out, drink dirty water, and beg and eat others' leavings. They stir their excrement and breathe its stench, and shrink at the sight of water. Like sheep, they have their heads plucked, and the hands (that pluck them) are filled with ash. They throw away the work of their mothers and fathers (earning a living), and their families wail aloud. For them there is no pind, no pattal, no kiria, no lamp; once dead, who knows where they are cast? The sixty-eight tiraths give them no shelter, and Brahmins do not eat their food. Day and night they stay ever unclean, with no tikka on the brow. They sit with heads ever bowed, as if mourning a death, and go to no gathering or assembly. Bowls hang at their waists and whisks are in their hands, and they walk in single file. They are neither yogis nor jangams, neither qazis nor mullas. Ruined by God, they wander in disgrace, and the whole flock roams accursed. He alone kills living beings and brings them to life; no one else can protect (them). They are cut off from giving and from bathing; ashes fall on their plucked heads. It was from water that the jewels came forth, when Meru was made the churning stick. The gods set up the sixty-eight tiraths (by the waters), where the holy days draw crowds and the sacred word is recited. Having bathed, one says the namaz; having bathed, one worships; the wise bathe always. In death and in life, one is made clean when water is poured over the head. O Nanak, these hair-plucked ones are perverse (shaitani); the matter (of bathing) does not please them. When the rain falls there is gladness; the very life of all beings rests in it. When the rain falls, grain, sugarcane and cotton (grow), and cotton covers everyone. When the rain falls, the cows graze on grass every day, and the woman (of the house) churns the curd. With that ghee the hom, the yagya and worship are ever performed; with it added, every rite is graced. The Guru is the ocean, and his teaching all the rivers: bathing in it, one gains glory. O Nanak, if the hair-plucked ones do not bathe (in it), then seven handfuls of ash (fall) on their heads. ॥1॥

This salok is about the Jain monks of the time (sarevre), who, for fear of harming the smallest living being, had their hair plucked out, neither bathed nor drank fresh water, and walked in single file sweeping the path with a whisk.

Pind, pattal, kiria and deeva are Hindu rites for the dead: balls of rice offered to the departed, food on leaf-plates, the rites after death, and the lamp lit in their name. Jangams are Shaiva mendicants who go about ringing bells.
150.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). What can cold do to fire? What can night do to the sun? What can darkness do to the moon? What can caste do to air and water? What can things do to the earth, in which everything comes to be? O Nanak, honour is known (as true) only when he himself keeps (one's) honour. ॥2॥
150.2: O True One, I have ever praised you as Subhan (the Wondrous). You are the true Ruler (Diwan); all others come and go. Those who ask (of you) the gift of Truth become like you. True is your command; through the Shabad it is beautiful (to them). By obeying (your command), wisdom and meditation are received from you. By (your) grace the mark (of approval) is set, which no one can remove. You are the true Giver; you give every day, and ever more and more. Nanak begs for the gift that pleases you. ॥26॥
150.3: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Those whom (the Guru) has given understanding by imparting his teaching, and merged in the True One through praise: what (further) teaching can be given to those whose Guru is Nanak Dev? ॥1॥
150.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Only the one whom he himself gives understanding understands. The one to whom he himself gives sight sees everything. One who talks and talks in discourse only wrangles over Maya. By his Hukam he makes all forms. He himself knows what is in the thoughts of all. O Nanak, the Word is his own utterance. The doubt of the one who receives (this) gift is removed. ॥2॥
150.5: I was a minstrel with no work; (the Lord) set me to (his) work. From the very first he commanded: Night or day, sing (my) vaar (of praise). The Master called the minstrel into his true mansion. He robed (me) in the robe of honour of his true praise. The true, ambrosial Name came to (me) as food. Whoever, by the Guru's teaching, has eaten (of it) to the full has found peace. The minstrel shares (this) blessing (with all), and has made the Shabad resound. Praising the True One, Nanak has found the Perfect (Lord).

94.1: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
My mind has come to love the Name of the Lord, Har Har, and the Lord himself.
By great good fortune I have meditated on the Lord's Name.
Through the perfect Guru I have gained this attainment of the Lord's Name; rare is the one who walks by the Guru's teaching.
I have tied (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, into the corner of my cloth as spending-money (for life's journey).
It is the companion of my life-breath, and goes with me always.
The perfect Guru has made the Lord's Name firm (within me); the Lord's wealth, unshakable, is (now) in my lap.
The Lord, Har Har, is my friend, my beloved, my King.
If only someone would bring him and unite me with him, the one who gives life to my breath.
O Beloved, I cannot live without seeing you; tears stream and keep streaming (from my eyes).
The True Guru is my friend, the companion of my childhood.
I cannot live without seeing him, O my mother.
Dear Lord, show your grace and unite me with the Guru, that servant Nanak may have the Lord's wealth in his lap. ॥4॥
94.2: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Madhusudan (the Lord) is my mind, my body and my life-breath.
I know no other, none but the Lord.
If only, by great good fortune, some friend, a Sant, would meet me and point me to my beloved Lord God.
I search my mind and body; I seek, and have others seek,
(asking) how I may meet my dear Beloved, O my mother.
Joining the Sat Sangat, I ask for news of his trail; it is in the Sangat that the Lord God dwells.
My dear Beloved, the True Guru, is my protector.
We are (your) helpless children: cherish and sustain us.
My mother and father are the Guru, the perfect True Guru; meeting the water that is the Guru, the lotus (of the heart) blossoms.
Without seeing the Guru, sleep does not come to me.
Separation from the Guru brings pain to my mind and body.
O Lord, Har Har, be merciful and unite me with the Guru; meeting the Guru, servant Nanak blossoms with joy. ॥4॥
95.1: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Let us read of the Lord's virtues, let us reflect on the Lord's virtues;
let us listen every day to the telling of the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Gathered in the Sat Sangat and singing the Lord's virtues, one crosses the world, the terrible ocean so hard to cross.
Come, my companion, let us bring about our union with the Lord.
Whoever brings me word of my Beloved,
and shows me the way to the Lord, Narhari, is my friend, my companion, my dear one, my brother.
The perfect Guru, one with the Lord, knows my pain:
I cannot live without uttering the Name.
O perfect Guru, give me the medicine, the mantra (of the Name); it is through the Name of the Lord, Har Har, that I can be saved.
We are humble chatriks, in the refuge of the True Guru;
(he) has put the drop of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, into our mouths.
The Lord is the ocean, and we are the fish of its water; O servant Nanak, without the water we die. ॥4॥
95.2: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O holy servants of the Lord, my brothers, come and meet me.
Show me the way to my Lord God; a hunger (for him) has seized me.
O Life of the world, O Giver, fulfil my longing: that, meeting the Lord, my mind may be drenched in the sight of him.
May I join the Sat Sang and speak the Lord's Bani;
the telling of the Lord, Har Har, has won my mind.
The Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, is dear to my mind; it is in meeting the True Guru that the Amrit is drunk.
The fortunate find the Lord's Sangat;
the unfortunate, lost in doubt, suffer blows.
Without good fortune the Sat Sang is not found; without the Sangat, (the mind) is filled with filth.
Come and meet me, O beloved Life of the world.
Holding mercy in your heart, (grant me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Through the Guru's teaching the Name has grown sweet and dear to the mind; O servant Nanak, the mind is drenched in the Name. ॥4॥
95.3: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
From the Guru I have received knowledge of the Lord; I have found the Lord's sweet essence, I have found the Lord.
My mind is dyed in the Lord's love; (the Guru) has given me the Lord's essence to drink.
With my mouth I utter the Name of the Lord, Har Har, I speak Har Har; my mind brims over and over with the Lord's essence.
Come, O Sants, and take me into your embrace;
tell me the story of my Beloved.
O Sants of the Lord, meet me; to the one who speaks the Gurbani with his mouth, I would give my mind.
By great good fortune the Lord has brought me to meet the Sant (the Guru);
the perfect Guru has put the Lord's essence into my mouth.
The unfortunate have not found the True Guru; the manmukh falls again and again into the womb, into birth after birth.
God, the Merciful, has himself shown mercy,
(and) done away with all the filth of Haumai and of Maya's poison.
O Nanak, it is in the shops and the town of the body that the Gurmukhs purchase the Lord's goods. ॥4॥
95.4: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
May I meditate on the virtues of Govind, on the Name of the Lord;
may I join the Sangat and enshrine the Naam in my mind.
O Lord God, inaccessible Master beyond the reach of the senses: it is in meeting the True Guru that the Lord's essence is enjoyed.
Blessed, blessed are the Lord's servants who have known the Lord God.
May I go and ask those servants about the Lord;
may I massage their feet and wash them, rubbing them clean; meeting the Lord's servants, the Lord's essence is drunk.
The True Guru, the Giver, has made the Naam firm (within me);
by great good fortune I have had the sight of the Guru.
I utter the essence of Amrit, the true Amrit (of the Name); it is from the perfect Guru that the Amrit is received.
O Lord, unite me with the Sat Sangat, with the True Being (the Guru);
it is in joining the Sat Sangat that the Lord's Name is meditated on.
Nanak says: may I hear the telling of the Lord and utter it with my mouth; through the Guru's teaching (the mind) is absorbed in the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
96.1: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Come, my sisters, my dear ones, and meet me.
To the one who shows me my Beloved, I am a sacrifice.
Joining the Sat Sangat, I have found the Lord, my friend; to the True Guru I am a sacrifice.
Wherever my eyes fall, the Master is there.
You pervade every heart, (O Lord), you who know what is within.
The perfect Guru has shown me the Lord right beside me; I am ever a sacrifice to the True Guru.
One is the air (in all), all the clay is one, and one light is in each and all.
One light is at work in all, (yet in each it works) apart and distinct; no one can blend (these differences) into one.
(Yet) by the Guru's grace the One has come into my sight; I am offered up to the True Guru.
Servant Nanak speaks the Bani that is Amrit;
it is dear to the minds of the Guru's Sikhs, it pleases them.
The Guru, the perfect True Guru, gives the teaching; the Guru, the True Guru, does good to others.
Seven Chaupade of the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
96.2: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My mind longs for the sight of the Guru;
it cries out like the chatrik.
Its thirst is not quenched, nor does peace come, without the sight of the dear Sant.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to the sight of the Guru, the dear Sant.
Your face is beautiful, and your word stirs the melody of Sahaj.
It is long since I saw you, O Saringpani.
Blessed is the land where you dwell, O my friend, my companion, O Murari.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to the Guru, my friend, my companion, Murari.
When I did not meet you for a single ghari, it was Kalyug (the dark age) for me.
When now shall I meet you, my beloved, blessed Lord?
My night does not pass, nor does sleep come, without seeing the Guru's court.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to that true court of the Guru.
Good fortune has come to me: the Guru has brought me to meet the Sant (God, the source of peace);
I have found the imperishable God within my own home (the heart).
Servant Nanak says: may I serve your servants, and not be parted (from them) for a moment, not for an instant.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice through and through, to your servants, says servant Nanak. ॥1॥
97.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Beautiful is the season in which I hold you in my heart;
sweet is the work that I toil at for you;
at peace is the heart in which you have come to dwell, O Giver of all.
You are the Master and Father we all share;
yours are the nine treasures, your storehouses never run out.
The one to whom you give (your gift) is filled and satisfied; that one alone is your devotee.
Everyone sits in hope of you;
within each and every heart you alone dwell.
All are called your partners; you are seen to be outside of no one.
You yourself, through the Guru, bring (beings) to liberation;
you yourself make (them) self-willed and send them wandering through births.
Nanak, your slave, is a sacrifice to you; all this is your play, plain to see. ॥4॥
97.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The unstruck melody resounds (within me); in Sahaj (the mind) is at ease.
Through the Shabad it ever delights in bliss and play.
In the cave of Sahaj it has sunk into deep absorption, and set its seat on high.
After roaming about, (the mind) has come back to its own home;
what it sought, that it has found.
It is filled and satisfied, O Sants; through inner experience the Guru has shown (me) the all-pervading Being.
He himself is the king, he himself the people;
he himself is free of all desire, he himself the enjoyer.
He himself, the True Judge, sits on the throne; all cries of complaint have come to an end.
As I have seen (him), so have I spoken.
The one who has grasped the secret has come to relish it.
(That one's) light has merged into the Light, and found peace; O servant Nanak, it is the One who has spread out (all this). ॥4॥
97.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the home (of the heart) where the Husband has brought the joy of wedded life,
in that home, O companion, songs of joy are sung.
Joy and delight grace the home of that bride whom the Husband has adorned.
She is virtuous, she is fortunate,
blessed with sons, gentle in nature, a happy wedded wife;
beautiful, skilled and wise is the bride who is dear to her Husband.
She alone is upright in conduct, she alone is foremost;
through her knowing (the Husband) every adornment becomes her.
She is of noble family, she is blessed with brothers, the bride made beautiful by the Husband's love.
she whom the Husband has united with himself and held close to his side.
Her wedded life is lasting, her Groom inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses; O servant Nanak, love is her support. ॥4॥
98.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Searching and searching, (many) long for the sight (of God);
in many ways they roam through forest after forest.
My Lord, Har Har, is Nirgun (beyond all qualities) and Sargun (manifest in all qualities); is there anyone who would bring him and unite me with him?
(Some) study the six Shastras and speak words of knowledge;
(some do) worship, wear the frontal mark and bathe at places of pilgrimage;
(some practise) the nivli cleansing and the eighty-four postures; but through these peace does not come.
For many years (they) have chanted and practised austerities;
they have travelled, wandering over the earth;
(yet) not for a moment does peace come to the heart; the yogi gets up and runs off again and again.
In his grace (God) has brought me to meet the Saadh (the holy Guru);
my mind and body are cooled, and I have found steadiness.
The imperishable God has come to live within (my) heart; Nanak sings the Lord's songs of joy. ॥4॥
98.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord is beyond the farthest beyond, the radiant Divine One;
he is inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses, unseen, and no one knows his secret.
He is merciful to the meek, Gopal, Gobind: meditate through the Guru on that Lord, who grants liberation.
Through the Guru, Madhusudan carries (beings) across;
through the Guru, Krishna, Murari, becomes (one's) companion.
The merciful Damodar is found through the Guru, and in no other way at all.
Keshav needs no food and bears enmity to none;
millions of his servants worship his feet.
The one in whose heart, through the Guru, the Lord, Har Har, dwells is the devotee of the One alone.
The sight of him never fails to bear fruit; he is endless and boundless,
great in power, ever the Giver.
When the Naam is repeated through the Guru, by it one crosses over (the world-ocean); O Nanak, few have come to know this state. ॥4॥
98.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), what you command is what is done, and what you give is what is received.
The poor and the helpless rely on you alone.
You alone, you alone are everything, my beloved; I am a sacrifice to your power.
By (your) will (one) strays into the wilds, by (your) will (one) keeps to the path;
by (your) will, through the Guru, (some) sing the Lord's praises;
by (your) will (one) wanders in doubt through many births: everything is in his will.
No one is a fool, and no one is wise (of himself);
in all things it is your will that is at work.
O inaccessible (Lord), beyond the reach of the senses, endless and unfathomable, your worth cannot be told.
Grant (me) the dust of the Sants' feet, O beloved;
O Lord, I have come and fallen at your door.
Beholding (the Sants), the mind is satisfied; O Nanak, (then) union (with the Lord) comes with ease. ॥4॥
98.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sorrow comes only when (the Lord) is forgotten;
(then) hunger (for Maya) takes hold, and (one) runs about in many ways.
Remembering the Naam, that one is ever at peace to whom (the Lord), merciful to the meek, gives (it).
My True Guru is mighty indeed;
when I cherish (him) in my heart, all sorrow is lifted.
The disease of anxiety and the pain of ego have gone; (the Lord) himself takes care of (me).
Like a child, I ask (him) for everything;
however much God gives, his gifts never run short.
Falling at (your) feet again and again, I plead with (you) earnestly, O Gopal, merciful to the meek.
I give myself in sacrifice to the perfect True Guru,
who has cut away all my bonds.
Placing the Naam in the heart, he has made (us) pure; in (the Lord's) love, Nanak has become a home of delight. ॥4॥
99.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O beloved, O Gopal, merciful and full of joy,
lofty, unfathomable, endless Master: remembering (you) again and again, I live.
O destroyer of sorrow, priceless treasure,
fearless, without enmity, unfathomable, beyond all weighing,
your form beyond time, unborn, self-existent: remembering (you) in my mind, I am cooled and at peace.
Gopal, the Lord, is (our) companion for ever, (the giver of) all delights;
he cherishes the high and the low (alike).
The Naam is the home of all delights, and it satisfies the mind; through the Guru I drink (this) nectar.
In sorrow and in joy, O beloved, I meditate on you;
this sound understanding I have received from the Guru.
You alone are Nanak's support, O Master; in the Lord's love I cross over (the world-ocean). ॥4॥
99.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Blessed is the moment in which I met the True Guru;
fruitful is the sight of him: beholding (him) with my eyes, I have crossed over (the world-ocean).
Blessed are those muhurats, chasas, moments and gharis; blessed are those times of meeting.
Through striving, (my) mind has become pure;
as I walk the Lord's path, all (my) doubt has been dispelled.
The True Guru has let (me) hear the treasure of the Naam, and all (my) ailments are gone.
(O Lord), within and without is your Word;
you yourself have spoken it, and you yourself have expounded it.
The Guru has said: everywhere is the One, the One alone; there will never be any other.
From the Guru I have drunk the nectar of the Lord;
the Lord has become (my) clothing, and the Naam (my) food.
In the Naam are (my) joys, in the Naam (my) sport and play; Nanak has made the Naam (his) pleasures. ॥4॥
99.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
From all the Sants I ask for one thing;
I make my plea and cast off (my) pride.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, lakhs of times: grant (me) the dust of the Sants' feet.
(O Lord), you are the Giver, you the all-pervading Creator;
you are all-powerful, ever the giver of peace.
Everyone prospers by you alone: bring this opportunity of mine (the human life) to fulfilment.
Those whose dwellings (their bodies) the sight of you has made holy
are the ones who have conquered the hard fortress of the self.
You are the Giver, you the all-pervading Creator; there is no other hero as great as you.
The dust of the Sants' feet has touched my face;
evil-mindedness has perished, and base understanding has fled.
Settled in the true home, (I) sing (his) praises; O Nanak, falsehood has perished. ॥4॥
100.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Giver so great, never slip from (my) mind;
show your grace, O (Lord) imbued with love for your devotees,
that day and night I may meditate on you: grant me this gift.
Into blind clay (the body) you have placed awareness;
you have given everything, and good places (to dwell in).
Joys, pleasures, wonders and shows: whatever pleases you comes to be.
Everything we receive is his gift:
the thirty-six kinds of ambrosial food we eat,
the comfortable bed, the cool breeze, the play and delight we enjoy at ease.
Give (me) that understanding by which you never slip from (my) mind;
give (me) that wisdom by which I meditate on you.
With every breath may I sing your praises; Nanak's shelter is the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
100.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
To praise you is (to accept) your Hukam, O Master of the will;
that is knowledge and meditation which is pleasing to you.
That alone is chanting which pleases God; (walking) in his will is perfect knowledge.
Your ambrosial Naam is sung only by the one
who is pleasing to your mind, O Master.
You belong to the Sants, and the Sants are yours; O Master, (their) minds rest content in you.
the Sants play in your company, O Gopal.
Your own Sants are most dear to you; you are the life-breath of the Sants.
My mind is offered in sacrifice to those Sants
who have come to know you and have found favour in your mind.
In their company (I) have found peace for ever; with the Lord's nectar Nanak is filled and satisfied. ॥4॥
100.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), you are the ocean, and we are your fish;
your Name is the raindrop, and we are thirsting chatriks.
My hope is in you, my thirst is for you; my mind is absorbed in you alone.
As a child is satisfied by drinking milk,
as a pauper finds joy at the sight of wealth,
(as) the thirsty one (is refreshed) drinking cool water, so is this mind drenched (in love) with the Lord.
As a lamp gives light in the dark,
(as a wife's) hope is fulfilled as she longs for her husband,
as there is bliss in meeting the beloved, so is (my) mind dyed in the love of the Lord.
The Sants have set me on the Lord's path;
the merciful Saadh (the Guru) has made (me) at home with the Lord.
The Lord is ours, and we are the Lord's servants; O Nanak, the Guru has given (us) the true Shabad. ॥4॥
100.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ever pure is the ambrosial Naam
of the Lord, who gives peace and drives away pain.
I have tasted and tried all other flavours; O mind, the Lord's essence is the sweetest of all.
whoever obtains the essence of the Naam becomes immortal.
The treasures of the Naam come to him alone in whose mind the Guru's Shabad has come to dwell.
Whoever has found the Lord's essence is filled and satisfied;
whoever has found the Lord's flavour does not waver.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, comes to him alone on whose forehead good fortune (is written).
When the Lord comes into the hands of one, very many reap the benefit;
clinging to that one, many are set free.
The treasure of the Naam is found through the Guru; says Nanak, rare are those who have seen it. ॥4॥
101.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
For me the Lord, Har Har Har, is the treasures, the siddhis and the riches;
by (the grace of) the deep and profound (Lord), this human birth is a precious gift.
Whoever is attached to the Guru's feet enjoys lakhs and crores of joys and delights.
and all (our) brothers and friends have been saved.
By the Guru's grace I meditate on the True One, my own Master, inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses.
The One whom all created beings seek
is seen by a rare one, through great good fortune.
Lofty, boundless and beyond the reach of the senses is (his) abode; that mansion the Guru reveals.
O deep and profound (Lord), your Name is nectar;
whoever has it dwelling in the heart is liberated.
The Guru has cut away all their bonds; O servant Nanak, (they) remain absorbed in Sahaj. ॥4॥
101.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
It is by God's grace that I meditate on the Lord, Har Har;
it is by God's mercy that I sing the song of (his) praise.
Rising, sitting, sleeping and waking, let us meditate on the Lord all our life.
The Saadh (the Guru) gave me the Naam as medicine;
(my) sins are cut away, and (I) have become pure.
Bliss has come, all pain has gone out, and every ache is destroyed.
The one whose side my beloved takes
is freed from the ocean of the world.
Whoever has recognised the Guru, holding (him) true, why should he be afraid?
Since I found the Saadh Sangat,
on meeting the Guru, the curse of ego has gone.
With every breath Nanak sings of the Lord; the True Guru has covered me and kept my honour. ॥4॥
101.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Like warp and weft, (the Lord) is woven into his servant.
God, the giver of peace, protects and sustains the servant.
I carry water, wave the fan and grind grain at the door of that servant whose striving is for the Master alone.
Cutting away (his) noose, God has set (him) to (his) service;
the Master's Hukam is dear to the servant's mind.
He does only what pleases the Master; such a servant is wise, within and without.
(O Lord), you are the all-knowing Master; you know every condition.
The Master's servants revel in the joys of the Lord.
Whatever is the Master's becomes the servant's; it is through being with the Master alone that the servant becomes known.
The one whom his own Master has robed in honour
is never again summoned to give account.
Nanak is a sacrifice to that servant; he is a pearl, deep and profound. ॥4॥
102.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Everything is within the home (of the heart); nothing is outside.
Whoever searches outside wanders astray in doubt.
Those who by the Guru's grace have found (him) within are at peace, within and without.
In a gentle patter the stream of Amrit rains down;
the mind drinks it, hearing the Shabad and reflecting (on it).
Day and night it rejoices in bliss and delight; for ever and ever it sports with the Lord.
The one parted for birth after birth has met (the Lord);
by the grace of the Saadh (the Guru), what was dry has turned green.
Receiving good understanding, one meditates on the Naam; through the Guru the union comes about.
As a wave of water merges into the water itself,
so (the Lord) has merged (that one's) light with the Light.
Says Nanak, the doors of doubt have been cut down; one no longer wanders away (from him). ॥4॥
102.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), I am a sacrifice to the one who has heard you (your Name);
I am devoted to the one who has uttered (you) with the tongue.
Over and over I give myself up to the one who worships you with mind and body.
Let me wash the feet of the one who walks on your path;
let me look with my own eyes on that kind person;
let me give my mind to that friend of mine who has found that God by meeting the Guru.
Fortunate are they who have known you;
in the midst of all, they remain untouched and free of desire.
In the Saadh's company such a one has crossed the fearsome world-ocean; such a one has subdued all the (inner) foes.
My mind has come into their refuge,
having given up pride, (reliance on its own) strength and the darkness of attachment.
Grant Nanak the gift of the Name of that God, beyond reach and beyond all depth. ॥4॥
102.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), you are the tree, and the branch that has spread and flowered is yours.
You, the subtle (unseen), have become the gross (the visible world).
You are the ocean, you the foam and the bubble; apart from you, no other is found.
You are the thread (of the mala), and the beads too are you;
you are the knot, and you the meru, the head bead set above (them all).
In the beginning, the middle and the end, it is God alone; no other is to be seen.
You are nirgun (beyond Maya's three qualities) and sargun (the world made of them), the giver of peace;
you are free of all desire, and you are the enjoyer, dyed in the colour (of the world's delights).
You alone know your own works; you yourself take care (of all).
You are the Master, and again you yourself the servant;
O God, you yourself are hidden, and you yourself are manifest.
Servant Nanak ever sings (your) praises; even for a moment, behold (him) with your glance of grace. ॥4॥
103.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Fruitful is that Bani through which the Naam is uttered;
by the Guru's grace, only some rare one has come to know it.
Blessed is the hour in which the Lord's (praise) is sung and heard; those who have come (into the world) and (sing and hear it) are accepted.
Accepted are the eyes that have beheld the sight (of the Lord);
good are the hands that have written the Lord's praise;
beautiful are the feet that have walked on the Lord's path. I am a sacrifice to them; in their company I recognise (the Lord).
Listen, my friend, my dear companion:
in the Saadh Sangat one is saved in an instant.
Sins are cut away, the mind becomes pure, and coming and going (birth and death) is ended.
Joining both hands, let us make one prayer:
(O God), in your grace, take hold of (this) sinking stone.
To Nanak God has been merciful, and in Nanak's mind God has become dear. ॥4॥
103.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Lord, Har Har, your Bani is Amrit;
hearing it again and again, I reach the supreme state.
The burning (within) is quenched and the mind has grown cool, on receiving the sight of the True Guru.
Peace has come, and pain has fled far away,
since the tongue of the Sant (the Guru) has uttered the Lord's Name.
Water and land are filled with water, the pools brimming; no one goes away empty.
and cherished all beings and creatures.
He is kind, gracious and compassionate; all are filled and wholly content.
He has made the forests, the blades of grass and the three worlds green;
the Maker did (this) within a moment.
O Nanak, whoever worships him through the Guru, (God) fulfils the hope of that one's mind. ॥4॥
103.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), you are my father, you are my mother;
you are my kinsman, you are my brother.
In every place you are my protector; so what fear, what worry, can there be?
It is by your grace that I have come to know you.
You are my shelter, you alone my pride.
Without you there is no other at all; all this is your play, your arena.
All beings and creatures were made by you;
to whatever task it pleased you, to that you have set each one.
Everything that happens is your doing; nothing is of our doing.
By meditating on the Naam I have obtained great peace;
singing the Lord's praises, my mind has grown cool.
Through the Perfect Guru the drums of rejoicing have sounded; Nanak has won the hard bout in the arena. ॥4॥
103.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
God is the support of soul, breath and mind;
singing the praises of the Infinite, the devotees live.
The Lord's Name is Amrit, the treasure of virtues; meditating and meditating on the Lord, (they) have found peace.
Whoever leaves home with longing in the heart (and comes to the holy company)
ends birth and death in the Saadh Sangat.
Hope and heart's aim are fulfilled on meeting the Guru and beholding him.
No measure at all of the Unreachable, the Imperceptible, has been known,
(though) seekers, Siddhas and men of knowledge meditate (on him).
Self-conceit is erased and delusion is ended: the Guru has revealed (the Lord) within the mind itself.
The treasures of bliss, joy and well-being,
peace and Sahaj are for the one who has uttered the Lord's Name.
Our own Master has become merciful, O Nanak, and the Name has come into the home (of the heart). ॥4॥
104.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord), hearing and hearing of your glory, I live.
You are (my) Beloved, the Master, exceedingly great.
Your doings you alone know; your shelter (is mine), O Gopal.
Singing (your) praises, the mind turns green;
hearing (your) story, all its filth is washed away.
Joining the company of the Saadhs and Sants, I ever repeat (the Name of) the Merciful One.
With every breath I keep my God in mind;
by the Guru's grace I hold this understanding in my mind.
By your grace the light (within) dawns; in your mercy you sustain all.
That God is true, true, true (ever abiding);
always, always, for ever, he himself alone exists.
Your wonders are plain to see, O Beloved; seeing them, Nanak is filled with joy. ॥4॥
104.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By (the Lord's) Hukam the rains have begun to fall;
friends and Sants meet together and repeat the Naam.
Cooling peace and the bliss of Sahaj are found; God himself has brought coolness.
He has brought forth everything in great abundance;
God, in his grace, has filled all to contentment.
O my Giver, you bestow your gifts, and all beings and creatures are filled.
True is the Master, true his glory;
through the Guru's grace I meditate on him always.
The fears of birth and death, and attachment, are cut away; sorrow and torment are destroyed.
remembering the Naam, all the nooses are cut.
In an instant (God) has fulfilled the hope, as the praises of the Lord, Har Har Har, are repeated. ॥4॥
104.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
let us meet and sing the praises of the Unreachable, the Infinite.
By singing and hearing (them), all are set free; let us meditate on him who made us.
The sins of birth after birth depart,
and (they) obtain the very fruits their minds have longed for.
Remember that Master, the True Lord, who gives every one their sustenance.
Repeating the Naam, every comfort is found;
all fear is destroyed when the Lord, Har Har, is meditated on.
Whoever has served (him) crosses to the far shore; all (that one's) tasks are accomplished.
(O Lord), I have come and fallen into your refuge;
as it pleases you, so unite (me with you).
In your grace, O God, join (me) to your devotion, that Nanak may drink the Amrit of the True (Name). ॥4॥
105.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Govind, the Lord of the world, has become merciful;
the cloud rains on every place.
Kind to the lowly, ever gracious, the Creator has brought coolness.
He cherishes his own beings and creatures,
as a mother looks after her children.
The Master, who shatters pain, the ocean of comfort, gives food to all.
The Merciful One pervades water and land;
let us ever be a sacrifice, an offering, to him.
Night and day I meditate on him always, who saves all in an instant.
all sorrow and torment are gone.
Repeating the Naam, mind and body turn green; O God, look upon Nanak with your glance of grace. ॥4॥
105.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Where the Name of the beloved God is repeated,
those places, (however bare), are golden mansions.
Where (your) Name is not repeated, O my Govind, those very towns are a wilderness.
The one who eats dry bread and (yet) keeps the Lord in (his) heart:
on him the Lord looks with grace, within and without.
The one who eats and eats and does evil deeds: know him as a garden of poison.
The one who forms no love for the Sants
and commits misdeeds in the company of the Saakats:
that ignorant one has wasted the rare (human) body, and torn up his own root himself.
My (Lord), merciful to the meek, I am in your refuge;
O Ocean of peace, my Guru, my Gopal.
Show mercy, that Nanak may sing (your) praises; keep our honour. ॥4॥
105.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Master's feet have come to rest in the heart,
and all strife and suffering have gone far away.
Peace, comfort and the strain of Sahaj have welled up, (as) one now dwells in the company of the Saadh (the Guru).
The love that has taken hold (for the Lord) never breaks at all;
the Lord fills all, within and without.
Remembering, remembering, remembering (him), I sing (his) praises, and the noose of Jam has been cut.
Amrit rains down through the unstruck Bani;
peace has settled within mind and body.
Your servants are fulfilled and wholly sated; the True Guru has given (them) comfort.
From the One to whom (I) belonged, (I) have received the fruit;
in his grace (the Guru) has united (me) with God.
By great good fortune the comings and goings (of birth and death) have ended; O Nanak, (all) hopes are fulfilled. ॥4॥
105.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The rain has fallen: the Supreme God has sent it down;
he has made all beings and creatures dwell in comfort.
Distress has gone and lasting peace has come, as I cherish the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
He to whom they belong has himself sustained them;
the Supreme Lord God has become (their) protector.
My Master has heard (my) prayer, and (my) toil has come to full fruit.
(God) is the Giver to all beings;
by the Guru's grace, he has looked (on me) with his glance of grace.
All (that lives) in water, on land and in the sky is sated; I wash the feet of the Saadh (the Guru).
(He) fulfils the desire of the mind;
I am a sacrifice (to him) for ever and ever.
O Nanak, the Destroyer of pain has bestowed the gift (of the Name); (his servants) are dyed in the love of God, the source of all delight. ॥4॥
106.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Mind and body are yours, and wealth too is yours;
you are my Master, my Lord, my God.
Soul and body are all your capital; your power, O Gopal, is (my) strength.
Forever and ever, you alone are the giver of peace;
bowing low again and again, I fall at your feet.
I would do (your) work, if by it I pleased you, when you grant it, O merciful Lord.
God, all I receive is from you; you are my adornment.
Whatever you give, that I bear as joy.
Wherever you keep (me), there is Baikunth (heaven); you are the cherisher of all.
O Nanak, (the one who) has found peace by remembering (you) again and again,
and has sung your praises at all hours,
has every longing fulfilled, and is never in sorrow. ॥4॥
106.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Supreme Lord God has sent the cloud;
he has made it rain on water, land and sky, in all ten directions.
Peace has come, all thirst is quenched, and there is joy in every place.
of himself, in his grace, he takes care of (all) beings.
He himself sustains what he has made; falling at (his) feet, I seek his favour alone.
He in whose refuge the highest state is attained:
on that Lord's Name let us meditate with every breath.
Apart from him there is no other master; all places are his alone.
You are my pride, God, and you are my strength;
you are the True Master, fathomless in virtues.
Servant Nanak makes this prayer: that I may meditate on you at all hours. ॥4॥
106.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With God pleased, every comfort has come;
the feet of the Perfect Guru have come to dwell in the mind.
The samadhi of Sahaj has set in, and attention is fixed within; that delight only the one (in this state) knows.
My Master is beyond reach, beyond the grasp of the senses;
(yet) he is present, close at hand, within each and every heart.
Ever untouched (by Maya), he is the Giver to all beings; rare is the one who recognises his own self.
This is the sign of meeting God:
in the mind one recognises the true Hukam of the One.
In Sahaj and contentment (such people) stay ever fulfilled, and find bliss in the Master's will.
God, the Giver, has given a palmful (of medicine),
and cured all the diseases of birth and death.
O Nanak, the servants God has made his own revel in the Lord's Kirtan (the singing of his praises). ॥4॥
107.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Gopal, the Lord of the world, has shown mercy;
the Guru's feet now dwell in the mind.
That Creator has accepted (me) as his own, and pulled down the camp of sorrow.
In mind and body that True One himself has come to dwell;
All foes and enemies have become friends, (since I) have longed for the one Master alone.
Whatever (God) does, he does himself, of his own accord;
no one's wit or cleverness is seen (to count) at all.
He himself is the helper of his Sants; God has taken away (their) doubt and delusion.
(God's) lotus feet are the support of his servant;
at all hours the Name of Ram is (his) trade.
In the bliss of Sahaj (his servants) sing Govind's praises; O Nanak, God pervades all. ॥4॥
107.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That is the true temple in which the True One is meditated on;
that heart is at ease in which the Lord's praises are sung;
that land is beautiful where the Lord's servants live; to the True Name I am a sacrifice.
You are the True One; the worth of (your) greatness no one has found;
(your) creation and (your) grace cannot be told.
Your servants live by meditating (on you) again and again; the True Shabad is the mainstay of their minds.
Only by great good fortune does one come to praise the True One;
by the Guru's grace the Lord's praises are sung.
Those steeped in your love please you; the True Name is the mark (of their approval).
The True One's limit no one knows;
in every place and the spaces between is that True One.
O Nanak, let us ever meditate on the True One, the Knower of hearts, the All-wise. ॥4॥
107.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lovely is the night, and the day passes in ease,
(when) one repeats the nectar-like Name, in fellowship with the Sants.
The gharis, muhurats and moments that pass in remembering (him): there life bears fruit.
Remembering the Naam, all faults have been washed away;
within and without, the Lord God is at (my) side.
The Perfect Guru has driven out fear, dread and doubt; I see (him) in all places.
God is all-powerful, great, lofty and infinite;
the Naam is the nine treasures; (his) storehouses are full.
In the beginning, the end and the middle there is God alone; I hold no other as his equal.
Show mercy, my (Lord), merciful to the meek:
(your) beggar begs for the dust of the feet of the Saadh (the Guru).
Grant (this) gift, servant Nanak asks: that I may meditate on the Lord forever and ever. ॥4॥
107.4: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Here it is you alone, and hereafter you yourself;
all beings and creatures are of your making.
There is none other than you, O Creator; on you I lean, you are my shelter.
(My) tongue lives by repeating (your Name) again and again, O Master,
O Supreme Lord God, Knower of hearts.
Whoever has served (you), he alone has found peace; he does not lose (his) life in a gamble.
The servant of yours who has obtained the medicine of the Naam
has rid (himself) of the disease of birth after birth.
Sing the Lord's Kirtan day and night; this is the work that bears fruit.
Casting his glance of grace, (God) has adorned his servant;
(that servant) has bowed to the Supreme Lord within each and every heart.
Without the One there is no other, O brother; O Nanak, this is the highest understanding. ॥4॥
108.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
For mind and body to be dyed in (the love of) the beloved Lord,
let us offer up all we have as a sacrifice.
At all hours let us sing Govind's praises; do not forget (him) for a single breath.
He alone is a friend, a beloved companion,
who reflects on the Name of Ram in the Saadh Sangat.
In the company of the Saadh the (world-)ocean is crossed, and the noose of Jam is cut.
The Lord's service is the four great gifts (padaarath);
the Paarjat tree is the repeating (of the Name) of the Unseen, the Unfathomable.
The Guru has cut away lust, anger and sins, and hope is fulfilled.
The mortal whose fortune has come to fullness
meets Saarangpaani, the Lord, in the Saadh Sangat.
O Nanak, the one within whom the Naam has come to dwell is approved, be he householder or renunciant. ॥4॥
108.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remembering the Naam, peace has been found in the heart;
in his grace, (God) has revealed (himself) to the devotees.
Those who have joined the company of the Sants and repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, are rid of sloth and sickness.
The Lord in whose house are the nine treasures, O brother,
is met by the one who has the earnings of past (good deeds).
(Such a one gains) knowledge of the Perfect, Supreme God and meditation on him; God is able to do all things.
In an instant (God) can set up and pull down;
he himself is alone, and himself the whole expanse (of the world).
No stain (of Maya) clings to the Giver, the Life of the world; on seeing him, separations are lifted.
Attaching it to (his) hem, he has carried the whole world across;
he himself has (us) repeat his own Name.
By (his) grace the ship of the Guru has been found; O Nanak, (this) union was ordained from the beginning. ॥4॥
108.3: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(A being) does only what (God) himself has it do.
Wherever he keeps (us), that is a good place.
That one alone is wise, that one is honoured, to whom (his) Hukam seems sweet.
(He) has strung all (creation) on a single thread.
The one he attaches (to himself) is attached to (his) feet.
One whose inverted lotus (of the heart) has blossomed has seen the Immaculate (Lord) in all.
You alone know your own greatness.
You yourself recognise your own self.
I am a sacrifice to those Sants of yours, each of whom has ground down lust, anger and greed.
You are without enmity; your Sants are pure,
and at the sight of them all sins are washed away.
O Nanak, whoever lives by meditating on the Naam again and again: his doubt and stubborn fear are destroyed. ॥4॥
109.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If anyone asks only for what is false (and passing),
it does not take him a moment to die.
One who ever serves the Supreme Lord, having met the Guru, is to be called unshakable.
One in whose mind loving devotion has taken hold,
sings (God's) praises day and night, ever awake.
The Master takes by the arm and unites (with himself) the one on whose forehead (this) share is written.
The lotus feet (of the Lord) dwell in the devotees' minds;
without the Supreme God, all are robbed.
(They) ever long for the dust (of the feet) of the Sants; the Name of the True One is (their) ornament.
Standing up and sitting down, let us sing (the praises of) the Lord, Har Har,
remembering whom the eternal Husband is found.
O God, be merciful to Nanak, (that he may) bear what you do. ॥4॥
109.2: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those who are dyed through the Shabad, all of them (living) in (your) Hukam,
are called to the mansion of (your) True Court.
O True One, my Master, merciful to the meek, (they) have won their minds over to the True One.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those made beautiful through the Shabad,
who through the Guru's teaching enshrine in the mind the Amrit Name, ever the giver of peace.
No one is mine; whose am I?
The True Master, (pervading) the three worlds, is mine.
Acting again and again in Haumai, multitudes pass away; having done wrong, they repent.
One who recognises (his) Hukam speaks of the Lord's virtues;
through the Guru's Shabad he carries the insignia (passport) of the Name.
The account of all is taken at the True One's door; one made beautiful by the Name will be set free.
The manmukh, gone astray, finds no place of rest;
bound at Jam's door, he suffers blows.
Without the Name no one is his companion or friend; those who meditate on the Naam are liberated.
The Saakat, caught in falsehood, does not love the Truth;
bound in duality, he comes and goes.
No one erases the destiny written (by past deeds); through the Guru, liberation is won.
In her parents' home (this world), she did not know her Husband;
parted (from him) by falsehood, she weeps and wails aloud.
Robbed by her faults, she does not reach (his) mansion; through virtue (her) faults are forgiven.
She who, in her parents' home, has known the Beloved,
understands through the Guru and reflects on the essence;
she puts a stop to (her) coming and going, and merges in the True Name.
Through the Guru one understands the One who is called the Indescribable;
to the True Master only truth is pleasing.
Nanak speaks the truth and prays: those who sing (his) praises meet the True One. ॥8॥
109.3: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
When there is grace, (God) brings (one) to meet the True Guru;
(then one) fixes the awareness on service and the mind on the Shabad.
Killing Haumai, (such a one) has found lasting peace and cast off attachment to Maya.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, offered up to the True Guru,
through whose teaching the light has dawned (within); day and night (I) sing the Lord's praises.
When one searches one's body and mind, then one finds the Name,
holds back the running (mind) and keeps it still,
sings the Guru's Bani day and night, and in Sahaj performs devotion.
Within this body is a wealth beyond counting;
when, through the Guru, the True One is met, then I see (it).
(Rising above) the nine doors, one is set free at the Tenth Gate, and makes the unstruck Shabad resound.
True is the Master, true is his glory;
by the Guru's grace (it) is enshrined in the mind.
Day and night, ever dyed in (his) love, one gains understanding at the True One's door.
(She who) did not know the worth of sin and of virtue,
clinging to duality, has strayed in doubt;
ignorant and blind, she does not know the way, and comes and goes again and again.
Through serving the Guru, lasting peace has been found;
Haumai and the sense of mine have been held in check.
Through the Guru's teaching the darkness has gone, and the hard (adamantine) doors have been opened.
(One who), killing Haumai, has enshrined (him) in the mind,
and ever fixed the mind on the Guru's feet,
by the Guru's grace is pure in mind and body, and meditates on the pure Name.
Life and death are all in your hands;
the one he forgives, he gives glory.
O Nanak, meditate ever on the Naam; you will make birth and death worthy. ॥8॥
110.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My God is pure, beyond reach, without limit;
without scales he weighs the world.
The one who becomes Gurmukh understands this; speaking (his) virtues, he merges in the Lord of virtues.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Lord's Name in the mind.
Those attached to the True One stay awake day and night, and win honour at the True One's door.
He himself hears and he himself sees;
that person alone is accepted on whom he casts his glance of grace.
The one he himself attaches is attached; through the Guru, (such ones) practise Truth.
Whom he himself leads astray, where can he reach out (for support)?
What is written from before cannot be erased.
Those who have met the True Guru are fortunate; by perfect grace they are united (with him).
In her parents' home the bride sleeps day and night;
her Husband has forgotten her; for her faults she is cast off.
Day and night she wanders ever wailing; without her Husband she finds no sleep.
(She who) in her parents' home has known the Giver of peace,
has killed Haumai and recognised (him) through the Guru's Shabad:
her bed is lovely, she ever delights in her Husband, and makes Truth her adornment.
He created the beings of the eighty-four lakh forms of life;
on whom he casts his glance of grace, him he brings to the Guru.
(His) servants, their sins cut away, are ever pure; at the True One's door the Name makes them beautiful.
If he asks for the account, who can give it?
Then reckoning (one's deeds) by twos and threes brings no peace.
God, the True One, himself forgives; himself forgiving, he unites (them with himself).
He himself does and himself has (all) done;
through the perfect Guru's Shabad he unites (beings with himself).
O Nanak, the one who receives the Naam receives glory; he himself unites (such a one) in union (with himself). ॥8॥
111.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The One himself moves about, hidden from sight.
When, through the Guru, I see (him), then this mind is drenched (with love);
giving up craving, I have found the peace of Sahaj, and enshrine the One in the mind.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who fix their minds on the One alone.
Through the Guru's teaching their mind has come to (its) one home; they are dyed in the True One's colour.
This world has gone astray; you yourself have led it astray.
Forgetting the One, it is lured by another;
day and night it wanders ever, lost in doubt; without the Name it suffers pain.
Those who are dyed in the love of the Creator, the Ordainer of destinies,
are known through the four ages, through service of the Guru.
The one to whom he himself gives glory merges in the Lord's Name.
In attachment to Maya, (the manmukh) does not remember the Lord;
bound in Jam's city, he suffers pain.
Blind and deaf, he sees nothing; the manmukhs are consumed in sin.
Some are dyed in (your) love, whom you yourself have drawn into loving attention (to you);
through loving devotion they are dear to your mind.
They serve the True Guru, ever the giver of peace; (you) yourself fulfil all their wishes.
O dear Lord, I am ever in your refuge;
you yourself forgive and give glory.
Jamkaal does not come near the one who meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who please the Lord are dyed (in his love) day and night;
my God has joined them (to himself) and united them in union.
O True One, they remain ever, ever in your refuge; you yourself give them the understanding of Truth.
Those who have known the True One are merged in the True One;
they sing the Lord's praises, speaking the Truth.
O Nanak, those steeped in the Name are detached; they sit in deep absorption in their own home (within). ॥8॥
111.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who dies through the Shabad is known as truly dead (to self).
Death does not crush him, pain does not torment him;
his light, meeting the (Lord's) Light, is merged in it; hear, O mind, (such a one) merges in the True One.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who win glory through the Lord's Name,
who, serving the True Guru, have fixed their minds on the True One, and through the Guru's teaching merge in Sahaj.
Her body is frail, and she wears a flimsy garment;
clinging to duality, she does not reach (his) mansion.
Every day she wanders burning, day and night; without her Husband she suffers great pain.
Neither body nor caste goes on ahead (to the world beyond);
where the account is called for, there one is set free by practising Truth.
Those who serve the True Guru are rich; here and hereafter they are merged in the Name.
(She who) makes the fear (of God) and love her adornment,
by the Guru's grace finds the mansion, (her true) home;
every day, ever, day and night, she delights in (her Lord), and takes on a colour as fast as the madder's.
The Husband dwells ever with all;
by the Guru's grace some rare one beholds (him) with (his) eyes.
My God is the highest of the high; in his mercy he himself unites (one with himself).
This world sleeps in attachment to Maya;
forgetting the Naam, it is ruined in the end.
The One by whose will it sleeps awakens it; through the Guru's teaching understanding is won.
One who drinks the Amrit sheds doubt;
by the Guru's grace he attains liberation and the highest state.
Steeped in devotion, ever detached, he kills his self and is united (with God).
He himself creates and sets (beings) to their tasks;
he himself brings sustenance to (the beings of) the eighty-four lakh forms of life.
O Nanak, those who are dyed in the True One, meditating on the Naam, do the work that pleases him. ॥8॥
112.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Within (each body, God) has fashioned the diamond and the ruby (of his Name);
through the Guru's Shabad, (the Gurmukh) has assayed it and had it assayed.
Those who have Truth in their keeping speak Truth, and test by the touchstone of Truth alone.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Guru's Bani in the mind,
who amid the black stain (anjan) of Maya have found the Immaculate (Lord), and merge (their) light in the Light.
Within this body is a vast expanse (of Maya);
the Name is immaculate, far beyond reach and without limit.
The one who becomes Gurmukh obtains it; (God) himself forgives and unites (him with himself).
(The one in whom) my Master makes the Truth firm,
fixes the mind on the True One by the Guru's grace.
