The True One alone pervades every place; (such ones) merge in the True One alone.
Carefree is my Beloved, the True One,
the destroyer of sins and faults.
With love and affection let us ever meditate (on him), and make devotion firm (within) in fear and love.
O True One, true devotion to you (is received) if it pleases (you);
he himself gives, and does not regret (giving).
He is the one Giver of all beings; through the Shabad he slays (the ego) and gives life.
O Lord, without you I have no one;
O Lord, you alone I serve, and you I praise.
Unite me with yourself, O True God; by (your) perfect grace you are found.
To me there is no other like you;
through your glance of grace the body finds fulfilment.
Day and night, O Lord, you care for (all) and protect (them); through the Guru, (they) merge in Sahaj.
To me no other is as great as you;
you yourself created (the world), and you yourself take it back into yourself.
You yourself make, break and adorn; O Nanak, through the Name (you) make (beings) beautiful. ॥8॥
113.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
He himself is the Enjoyer in all hearts;
the Unseen pervades (all), beyond reach, without limit.
Through the Guru's Shabad let us meditate on my Lord God; (those who do so) merge, in Sahaj, in the True One.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Guru's Shabad in the mind.
When the Shabad is understood, then (one) wrestles with one's own mind, and, stilling desire, merges (in the Lord).
The five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) are plundering the world;
the blind manmukhs have no sense or awareness (of it).
One who becomes Gurmukh guards his own home, and through the Shabad burns away the five enemies.
Some, through the Guru, are ever dyed in the True One's love;
in Sahaj they serve God, intoxicated (with love) day and night.
Meeting the Beloved, they sing the praises of the True One, and win honour at the Lord's door.
First, the One alone brought himself forth;
second (comes) duality, (third) Maya of the three qualities;
the fourth step, the high one, is the Gurmukh's: (there they) practise Truth, Truth alone.
All is true if it pleases the True One;
one who has known the True One merges in Sahaj.
This is the Gurmukhs' way of life: they serve the True One, and go and merge in the True One.
Apart from the True One there is no other at all;
clinging to duality, the world wears itself out and dies.
One who becomes Gurmukh knows the One alone, and serving the One finds peace.
All beings and creatures are in your refuge;
you yourself place the pieces (on the board of the world's chaupar) and see which are raw and which ripe.
Day and night he himself has (beings) do (their) work; he himself joins (them) in union (with himself).
You yourself unite (them), and, ever at hand, you watch over (all);
he himself is fully present in all.
O Nanak, he himself, all by himself, pervades (all); through the Guru, (this) understanding is gained. ॥8॥
113.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Guru's Amrit Bani is sweet;
some rare Gurmukh has tasted (it) and seen.
Light (dawns) within (him); he drinks the supreme essence, and at the True One's door makes the Shabad resound.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who fix their minds on the Guru's feet.
The True Guru is a true pool of Amrit; (those whose) mind bathes (in it) wash away (their) filth.
O True One, no one has found your limit;
by the Guru's grace some rare one has fixed the mind (on you).
Praising you, I am never sated; a hunger for the True Name stays with me.
I see the One alone, no other;
by the Guru's grace I have drunk Amrit.
Through the Guru's Shabad I have quenched (my) thirst, and in Sahaj I am merged in peace.
(The manmukh) gives up the priceless jewel for straw;
the blind manmukh clings to the love of another.
Whatever he sows, that fruit he reaps; not even in a dream does he find peace.
The one on whom (God) shows his grace, that person finds (him),
(and) enshrines the Guru's Shabad in the mind.
Day and night he ever lives in the fear (of God); killing (all other) fears, he casts off doubt.
He has cast off doubt and found lasting peace;
by the Guru's grace he has attained the supreme state.
Pure is (his) heart, pure (his) speech; in Sahaj he sings the Lord's praises.
(The pandit) expounds the Simritis, the Shastras and the Vedas,
(but), lost in doubt, he does not know the essence.
Without serving the True Guru he finds no peace, and earns pain upon pain.
He (the Lord) himself does (all); to whom can anyone speak?
One would go to speak (to him) only if he erred.
O Nanak, he himself does and has (all) done; through the Name, (beings) merge in the Name. ॥8॥
114.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
God himself dyes (beings), in Sahaj and in love;
through the Guru's Shabad he applies the colour of the Lord's (Name).
(Their) mind and body are dyed, the tongue deep red with (that) colour; through fear and love (of God) this colour is applied.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Fearless (Lord) in the mind.
By the Guru's grace they have meditated on the Fearless Lord, and through the Shabad (he) carries (them) across the poisonous world-ocean.
The foolish manmukhs act clever;
though bathed and washed, (the manmukh) is not accepted (at the Lord's door).
As he came, so he will go; having done wrong, he repents.
The blind manmukh understands nothing;
he does not grasp that (all) have come with death written (in their lot).
The manmukh performs (ritual) deeds but does not find (the Lord); without the Name he wastes (his) life.
(Remembering) the Truth (alone) is the deed to do, the Shabad (alone) is the essence;
through the perfect Guru the door of liberation is found.
Day and night (the Guru) recites the Bani through the Shabad; (those who hear it) are steeped in the True One and dyed in (his) love.
(One whose) tongue, filled with love, is steeped in the Lord's taste,
(his) mind and body are enraptured, in Sahaj and in love;
in Sahaj he has found the dear Beloved, and with ease he is united in Sahaj.
One within whom is love sings (God's) praises;
through the Guru's Shabad he merges with ease in peace.
I am ever a sacrifice to those who fix their minds on the Guru's service.
The True One, Truth itself, is won over by truth alone;
by the Guru's grace, (those whose) heart is drenched (in love),
sit in the blessed place (within) and sing the Lord's praises; (God) himself makes (them) accept (this) as true.
The one on whom he casts his glance of grace finds (him);
by the Guru's grace (his) Haumai departs.
O Nanak, the Naam dwells in (his) mind, and he wins honour at the True One's door. ॥8॥
114.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
By serving the True Guru, great glory (is won):
the dear Lord, free of care, comes and dwells in the mind.
The dear Lord is a fruit-bearing tree (whose juice) is Amrit; whoever has drunk it, his thirst is quenched.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the True One, who brings (beings) into the Sangat and unites (them with himself).
The Lord himself brings (beings) into the Sat Sangat; (there,) through the Guru's Shabad, they sing the Lord's praises.
I serve the True Guru, who has made (my life) beautiful through the Shabad,
who has enshrined the Lord's Name in (my) mind.
The pure Lord takes away the filth of Haumai; (such ones) win honour at the True One's door.
The Name is not found without the Guru;
the Siddhas and seekers were left wailing (for it).
Without serving the Guru there is no peace; the Guru is found by perfect destiny.
This mind is a mirror; some Gurmukh (alone) sees (himself in it).
No rust clings (to it) when he dries up Haumai.
He makes the unstruck Bani, the pure Shabad, resound (within); through the Guru's Shabad he merges in the True One.
Without the True Guru, (the Lord) is not to be seen at all;
the Guru, in his grace, has revealed (the Lord's) own self.
He himself, himself alone, is blended (in all); (one who sees this) merges with ease in Sahaj.
One who becomes Gurmukh fixes loving attention on the One alone;
he burns away the doubt of duality through the Guru's Shabad.
Within the body he trades and deals, and finds the true treasure of the Naam.
The Gurmukh's deed is the Lord's praise, the most excellent (of deeds);
through the Guru, (he) finds the door of liberation.
Day and night, dyed in (God's) love, he sings (his) praises, and is called into the mansion (of the Lord).
The True Guru, the Giver, is met when (God himself) brings about the meeting;
by perfect destiny (one) has enshrined the Shabad in the mind.
O Nanak, (such a one) receives the glory that is the Naam, and sings the praises of the True Lord. ॥8॥
115.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
If one sheds the self, then one gains everything;
through the Guru's Shabad one fixes true loving attention (on the Lord).
(Such ones) trade in Truth, gather Truth, and deal in Truth alone.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who sing the Lord's praises day and night.
I am yours, you are my Master; through the Shabad you give glory.
Lovely are all the hours and moments,
in which the True One is dear to my mind.
Serving the True One, true glory (is won); by the Guru's grace the True One is found.
When the True Guru is pleased, (one) receives the food of love;
the taste for other things ends, and (one) enshrines the Lord's taste in the mind.
Truth, contentment and the peace of Sahaj are received from the perfect Guru through (his) Bani.
Those who do not serve the True Guru are fools, blind and ignorant;
how then will they find the door of liberation?
Dying again and again they are born, again and again they come; at Jam's door they suffer blows.
When (people) know the taste of the Shabad, then they recognise their own selves,
and through the Shabad they utter the pure Bani.
Serving the True One they ever find peace, and enshrine in the mind the Naam, (which is) the nine treasures.
Lovely is the place that has pleased the Lord's mind,
where, sitting in the Sat Sangat, (his devotees) have sung the Lord's praises.
Day and night they praise the True Lord, and make the pure melody (of his praise) resound.
The manmukhs' capital is counterfeit, and counterfeit is their show;
they practise falsehood and suffer heavy pain.
Lost in doubt they wander day and night; dying and being born, they waste (their) life.
The True Master is very dear to me;
through the perfect Guru's Shabad (he is my) support.
O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (such ones) know pain and pleasure as one. ॥8॥
116.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(O God,) yours are the sources of life, yours the tongues (that beings speak);
without the Name, all (creation) strays in doubt.
Through service of the Guru the Lord's Name has been found; without the True Guru no one finds (it).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who fix their minds on the Lord.
The True Lord is found through devotion to the Guru; in Sahaj (they) enshrine (him) in the mind.
If one serves the True Guru, then one obtains everything;
with whatever wish one sets about (the service), such is the fruit one receives.
The True Guru gives all things; by perfect fortune (God) brings (one) to meet (him).
This mind is soiled; it does not meditate on the One;
through love of duality much filth has stuck to it within.
(This) proud (mind) roams to riverbanks, places of pilgrimage and foreign lands, and smears on still more of the filth of Haumai.
If one serves the True Guru, then the filth goes;
(one) dies (to self) while still alive, and fixes the mind on the Lord.
The Lord is pure and true, and no filth clings to him; one who clings to the True One washes (his) filth away.
Without the Guru there is pitch darkness;
the ignorant one is blind, (lost in) blind darkness.
Worms of dung, they deal in dung, and in dung again they rot.
Serving the liberated one (the Guru), one becomes liberated;
through the Shabad one sheds Haumai and the sense of mine.
Day and night (such a one) serves the True Lord; by perfect fortune (he) has found the Guru.
(God) himself forgives and unites (one) in union (with himself);
from the perfect Guru one obtains the treasure of the Naam.
Through the True Name the mind becomes true for ever; serving the True One, one sheds pain.
(He) is ever present; do not think (him) far away;
through the Guru's Shabad, recognise the Lord within.
O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (the Name) is obtained from the perfect Guru. ॥8॥
116.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who are true here are true hereafter (too);
(their) mind is true; (they) are absorbed in the true Shabad.
They serve the True One and practise Truth; Truth, and Truth alone, they practise.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the True Name in the mind.
They serve the True One, merge in the True One, and sing the praises of the True One.
The pandits read (the scriptures) but do not taste (their) savour;
in the love of another they let (their) minds wander after Maya.
In attachment to Maya (they) have lost all understanding; having done wrong, they repent.
If one meets the True Guru, then one finds the essence (of things),
and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind.
Through the Shabad one dies (to self), subdues one's own mind, and finds the door of liberation.
(He) cuts away sins and drives out anger,
(who) keeps the Guru's Shabad held in the heart.
Those dyed in the True One are ever detached; killing Haumai, they are united (with God).
The jewel is within, but it is found only when (the Guru) leads one to it;
desire is of three kinds, Maya is of three kinds.
Reading and reading, the pandits and the silent sages have grown weary, (yet) they do not grasp the fourth state.
(God) himself dyes (them), (himself) gives (them) the colour (of love);
those people stay steeped (in his love) whom (he) has dyed through the Guru's Shabad.
The Lord's colour, utterly boundless, has come upon (them); steeped in the Lord's savour, with joy, (they) sing (his) praises.
For the Gurmukh, that (True One) alone is wealth, miraculous power, truth and self-discipline;
through the Guru (comes) divine knowledge; through the Name, liberation.
Through the Guru (they) do the work of Truth, and merge in the True One alone.
Through the Guru (one understands that God himself) creates, and having created, destroys;
for the Gurmukh, (God) himself is caste and honour, everything.
O Nanak, the Gurmukh meditates on the Name, and merges in the Name alone. ॥8॥
117.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Creation and dissolution come about through (God's) Word (his Hukam) alone;
through the Word alone creation comes about again.
Through the Guru (one sees that) the True One himself pervades all; through the Guru, (that) having created (the world), he is merged (in it).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the perfect Guru in the mind.
From the Guru comes peace; (one) performs devotion day and night, and speaking (his) virtues, merges in the Lord of virtues.
Through the Guru (one sees that) in earth and water,
in air and fire, the Wondrous (Lord himself) is at play.
He is without a Guru who dies and dies and is born again; those without a Guru keep coming and going.
That Creator has staged a play;
within the frame of the body he has placed everything.
Piercing (the mind) with the Shabad, some (rare) one reaches (the Lord's) mansion; (the Lord) calls (him) into (his own) mansion.
The Banker is true, and the traders (who deal with him) are true,
(who) trade in Truth, in boundless love for the Guru.
They purchase Truth and practise Truth; Truth, and Truth alone, they practise.
Without capital, how can anyone obtain the goods?
All the manmukh people have gone astray.
Without capital all depart empty-handed; going empty-handed, they suffer pain.
Some, (abiding) in love through the Guru's Shabad, trade in Truth;
they themselves swim across and carry all their families across.
Their coming (into the world) is approved; meeting the Beloved, they find peace.
The treasure is within, (but) the fool searches outside;
the blind manmukhs wander about out of step (with life's true rhythm).
Where the treasure is, from there no (manmukh) obtains (it); the manmukhs stray in doubt.
(God) himself gives (this gift), calling (one to himself) through the Shabad;
in the mansion of the Master of the mansion, (such a one) finds the peace of Sahaj.
O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (God) himself hears (the Name) again and again and meditates (on it). ॥8॥
117.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The True Guru has imparted (this) true teaching:
remember the Lord; (he) is (your) companion at the end.
The Lord is beyond reach and beyond the senses, has no master over him, and is not born; (he) is found through love for the True Guru.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who rid themselves of self-conceit.
If one sheds self-conceit, then one finds the Lord, and in Sahaj merges with the Lord.
As was written from before, (one) has done that deed:
serving the True Guru, (he) has found lasting peace.
Without good fortune one does not find the Guru; through the Shabad (the Guru) unites (one) in union (with God).
The Gurmukh stays untouched in the world,
leaning on the Guru, with the Name as (his) support.
What force can anyone use on the Gurmukh? (The one who tries) wears himself out and suffers pain.
The blind manmukh has no understanding at all;
he is the slayer of his own soul and a butcher of the world.
Slandering again and again, he takes up a great load (of sin), and carries (others') load without wages.
This world is a garden, and my God (its) gardener;
he ever tends (it), and no (plant) is left out (of his care).
Whatever scent he places (within), that is what comes forth; the fragrant (flower) makes itself known by its fragrance.
The self-willed world is sick;
(it) has forgotten the Giver of peace, the Unreachable, the Infinite.
The wretched wander ever wailing; without the Guru (they) find no peace.
He who made (them) alone knows the way (to heal them);
if he himself acts (in grace), then (one) recognises (his) Hukam.
As (the nature) he places within (a being), so (that being) acts; and he himself casts (it) out.
Apart from that True One, I have no other;
the one he attaches (to himself) becomes pure.
O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (every) heart; the one to whom (God) gives (it) receives (it). ॥8॥
118.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(One who) enshrines the Amrit Name in the mind,
sheds Haumai, the sense of mine, and all pain;
through the Amrit Bani (he) ever praises (God), and through the Amrit (Bani) obtains the Amrit (Name).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Amrit Bani in the mind.
Enshrining the Amrit Bani in the mind, (they) meditate on the Amrit Name.
With (his) mouth, in (his) words, (he) ever speaks Amrit;
with (his) eyes (he) ever sees and discerns the Amrit (Lord).
Day and night (he) ever speaks the Amrit discourse, and recites it to others.
Dyed in the love of the Amrit (Lord), (he) holds (him) in loving attention;
by the Guru's grace (he) obtains the Amrit.
With (his) tongue (he) speaks Amrit day and night, and in mind and body drinks the Amrit.
(God) does what does not even enter (anyone's) thoughts;
no one can erase his Hukam.
By (his) Hukam alone the Amrit Bani prevails; by (his) Hukam alone (he) gives the Amrit to drink.
Wondrous are the works of the Creator Lord;
this mind, going astray, (he) turns back,
fixes (its) attention on the Amrit Bani, and through the Amrit Shabad makes (the Name) resound (within it).
The counterfeit and the genuine you yourself created;
you yourself assay all people.
Assaying the genuine, (you) put them in (your) treasury, and the counterfeit you lead astray in doubt.
(O God,) how can I see (you)? How can I praise (you)?
By the Guru's grace, through the Shabad, (I) praise (you).
In your will dwells the Amrit; by (your) will you give the Amrit to drink.
Amrit is the Shabad, Amrit the Lord's Bani;
when the True Guru is served, (it) settles in the heart.
O Nanak, the Amrit Name is ever the giver of peace; drinking the Amrit, all hunger departs. ॥8॥
119.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Amrit is raining down gently, of its own accord;
through the Guru, only some rare person obtains (it).
Drinking the Amrit, (they) are satisfied for ever; in (his) mercy (God) quenches (their) thirst.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who drink the Amrit through the Guru.
(Their) tongue, having tasted the savour (of the Name), stays ever dyed in (God's) love, (and) in Sahaj (they) sing the Lord's praises.
By the Guru's grace some (rare) one attains Sahaj;
(he) kills duality and holds the One in loving attention.
If (God) casts (his) glance of grace, then one sings the Lord's praises, (and) by (his) grace merges in the True One.
O God, your glance of grace is upon all;
on some it is little, on some it is much.
Nothing happens beyond you; through the Guru (this) understanding is won.
Through the Guru (this) essence has been reflected upon:
your storehouses are filled with Amrit;
without serving the True Guru, none obtains (it); by the Guru's grace (it) is received.
The person who serves the True Guru is made beautiful;
(his) inner mind is enraptured by the Amrit Name.
(His) mind and body are dyed with the Amrit, with the Bani; in Sahaj (he) recites the Amrit (to others).
The manmukh has gone astray; the love of another ruins (him);
(he) does not take the Naam, and dies eating poison.
Day and night, ever, (he) dwells in dung; without service (he) wastes (his) life.
He alone drinks the Amrit whom (God) himself gives it to drink;
by the Guru's grace, in Sahaj, (he) holds (God) in loving attention.
The Perfect (Lord) himself pervades all; through the Guru's teaching (he) comes into view.
He, the Immaculate, is himself all in all;
the One who created (the world) himself destroys (it).
O Nanak, cherish the Naam ever (in the mind); (so) in Sahaj you will merge in the True One. ॥8॥
119.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(O God,) those who please you are attached to the True One;
they ever serve the True One, in Sahaj and in love.
Through the true Shabad let (me too) praise the True One; the True One unites (those who praise him) in union (with himself).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who praise the True One.
All who meditate on the True One are dyed in the True One, and merge in the True One alone.
Wherever I look, the True One is in every place;
by the Guru's grace I enshrine (him) in the mind.
True is the body (of those) whose tongue is dyed in the True One; hearing the Truth, they speak it and tell of it.
(The mind) subdued, (one) whose desire has merged in the True One
has seen with this mind that all (the world) comes and goes.
Such a one serves the True Guru; (his) mind is ever steady, and he finds a dwelling in his own home (within).
The Guru's Shabad has shown (me the Lord) within the heart;
through the Shabad (I) have burnt away attachment to Maya.
Seeing only the True One (everywhere), I praise (him); through the Guru's Shabad (beings) find the True One.
Those who are dyed in the True One have their loving attention fixed on him for good;
those who keep the Lord's Name (in the heart) are fortunate.
Through the true Shabad (God) himself unites (with himself) those who sing the True One's praises in the Sat Sangat.
One could read (his) account, if he could be held in any account;
he is beyond reach, beyond the senses; understanding (of him) comes through the Shabad.
Day and night I praise (him) through the true Shabad; no one else can find his worth.
(People) have read and read until they were weary, but peace did not come;
burnt by craving, they have no understanding.
They buy poison, they thirst for attachment to poison, and speaking falsehood they eat poison.
By the Guru's grace I have known the One alone;
killing (the sense of) another, the mind has merged in the True One.
O Nanak, the one Name pervades within the mind; by the Guru's grace (it) is obtained. ॥8॥
120.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(O God,) all the colours and forms at play are yours;
(beings) die and are born again and again, and go through many rounds (of birth and death).
You alone are unshakable, beyond reach and without limit; through the Guru's teaching you give understanding (of yourself).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Name of Ram in the mind.
He has no form, no mark, no colour at all; through the Guru's teaching he himself gives understanding (of himself).
There is one Light in all, if anyone comes to know it;
serving the True Guru, it is made manifest.
Hidden and manifest, he pervades every place; he merges (the soul's) light in (his own) Light.
The world is burning in the fire of craving;
(in it is) greed, pride and much egotism.
Dying again and again it is born, loses its honour, and wastes its life in vain.
Some rare one understands the Guru's Shabad;
if one kills the self, then (the Lord, pervading) the three worlds is seen.
Then he does not die (again), death does not come to him; in Sahaj he merges in the True One.
He does not fix his mind on Maya again;
he remains ever merged in the Guru's Shabad.
He praises the True One, who is within every body; the True One alone shines (in all).
I praise the True One, ever present;
through the Guru's Shabad (he is seen) filling all.
By the Guru's grace the True One is seen; in the True One alone is peace found.
The True One is pervading within the mind;
the True One is ever unshakable; he does not come or go.
The mind that is attached to the True One is pure; through the Guru's teaching (such ones) merge in the True One.
I praise the True One; there is no other (like him),
serving whom there is lasting peace.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Name are discerning; Truth, and Truth alone, they practise. ॥8॥
121.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Pure is the Shabad (of his praise), pure is (his) Bani;
(his) pure Light is contained in all.
Through the pure Bani I praise the Lord; repeating (the Name of) the pure Lord, (beings) rid themselves of filth.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine in the mind the Giver of peace.
Through the Guru's Shabad I praise the pure Lord; hearing the Shabad alone, (they) quench their craving.
(One in whose) mind the pure Name has come to dwell
becomes pure in mind and body, and casts off attachment to Maya.
He ever sings the pure praises of the True One, and sounds the pure Naad (of praise).
(One who) has received the pure Amrit from the Guru
has died to self within; there is no attachment to Maya there.
Pure is (his) wisdom, his meditation utterly pure; (such ones) enshrine the pure Bani in the mind.
One who serves the Pure One becomes pure;
through the Guru's Shabad he washes off the filth of Haumai.
(Within him) the pure Bani sounds as the unstruck melody; (such ones) win glory at the True One's door.
From the Pure One all become pure;
pure is the mind of one who strings it on the Lord's Shabad.
Fortunate are those attached to the pure Name; through the Name they are pure and beautiful.
He alone is pure who is made beautiful by the Shabad;
the pure Name holds (his) mind and body enraptured.
In the True Name no filth ever clings; the True One makes (their) faces radiant.
The mind is filthy in the love of another;
filthy is (his) cooking square, filthy the place (he sits in).
Eating filth, he adds yet more filth; the manmukhs, through filth, suffer pain.
The filthy and the pure, all are in (his) Hukam, every one;
they alone are pure who please the True Lord.
O Nanak, (those within whose) mind the Naam dwells rid themselves of filth through the Guru. ॥8॥
121.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Govind is radiant, and radiant are (his) swans (his devotees);
(my) mind, (my) speech and my desire are made pure.
Radiant within, their faces ever shine; they meditate on the Naam, radiant beyond measure.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who sing the praises of Gobind.
(Such a one) says Gobind, Gobind, day and night, and through the Shabad lets (others) hear Gobind's praises.
(Those who) sing of Gobind in Sahaj and in love
become radiant in the fear of the Guru; the filth of Haumai departs.
They remain ever in bliss and perform devotion day and night; they hear Gobind's praises and sing them.
The mind dances (when one) holds devotion firm;
through the Guru's Shabad he joins the mind (to the Lord) within the mind.
Ending attachment to Maya is keeping the true beat; (such ones) dance in the Shabad alone.
(One who) cries out aloud and dashes his body (on the ground)
is (caught) in attachment to Maya; Jamkaal has him in sight.
Attachment to Maya makes this mind dance; with deceit within, (such ones) suffer pain.
When (the Lord) himself has devotion done through the Guru,
body and mind are dyed, in Sahaj and in love.
The Bani resounds (within), and he plays it through the Shabad; (the Lord) accepts devotion done through the Guru.
(One who) beats out many rhythms and plays instruments,
(by that) no one hears (the Name) or enshrines (it) in the mind.
For Maya's sake he marks out the ring and dances; in the love of another (such ones) suffer pain.
One within whom love (for the Lord) takes hold is liberated;
(his) senses are under control, and he holds to the self-discipline of Truth.
Through the Guru's Shabad he ever meditates on the Lord; this is the devotion that pleases the Lord.
Through the Guru alone has devotion been done in all four ages;
by any other way no one attains devotion.
O Nanak, the Name is obtained through devotion to the Guru, by fixing the mind on the Guru's feet. ॥8॥
122.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
I serve the True One, I praise the True One;
in the True Name there is never any pain.
Those who serve the Giver of peace find peace; through the Guru's teaching they enshrine (him) in the mind.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who rest in the Samadhi of peace, in Sahaj.
Those who serve the Lord ever look beautiful; they win glory, and their awareness is beautiful.
(O God,) everyone calls himself your devotee;
they alone are devotees who are pleasing to your mind.
Through the Bani they praise you, the True One; dyed in (your) love, they perform (your) devotion.
O True dear Lord, everyone is yours;
when one meets (you) through the Guru, the round (of birth and death) is ended.
When it pleases you, you absorb (beings) in the Name; you yourself have them repeat the Name.
(One who) through the Guru's teaching has enshrined the Lord in the mind
has cast off joy and sorrow and all attachment.
His loving attention is fixed on the One for ever; (such ones) enshrine the Lord's Name in the mind.
(O God, your) devotees are dyed in (your) love, ever in joyful eagerness for you;
the Naam, the nine treasures, has come to dwell in (their) minds.
By perfect fortune they have found the True Guru, (who) through the Shabad unites (them) in union (with the Lord).
(O God,) you are merciful, ever the giver of peace;
you yourself unite (beings with yourself); through the Guru (you) are known.
You yourself give the Naam and glory; those dyed in the Naam find peace.
O True One, ever, ever I praise you;
through the Guru (I) have known that there is no other.
The mind stays absorbed in the One; when the mind is won over, (such ones) are united (with the Lord) within the mind.
One who becomes Gurmukh praises
the True Master, the Carefree.
O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (his) mind; through the Guru's Shabad (such ones) are united with the Lord. ॥8॥
122.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(O God,) your devotees look beautiful at the true court;
through the Guru's Shabad they are adorned with the Name.
Day and night they remain ever in bliss; speaking (his) virtues, they merge in the Lord of virtues.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who hear the Naam and enshrine (it) in the mind.
The dear Lord is true, the highest of the high; killing Haumai, (beings) are united (with him).
The dear Lord is true, and true is (his) glory;
by the Guru's grace he unites some (rare one with himself).
Those who meet (him) through the Guru's Shabad are not parted (again); in Sahaj they merge in the True One.
(O God,) nothing happens outside you;
you create and create, and watch over (it); you alone know (it all).
The Creator himself does and has (all) done; through the Guru's teaching he himself unites (beings with himself).
The virtuous soul-bride finds the Lord;
she makes the fear (of God) and love her adornment.
Serving the True Guru, she is a happy wife for ever; through the true teaching she merges (in her Husband).
Those who forget the Shabad have no place and no rest;
lost in doubt, (they wander) like a crow in a deserted house.
They lose both this world and the next; (their lives) pass in pain upon pain.
Writing and writing, (they) have used up paper and ink;
(but) in the love of another no one finds peace.
They write falsehood and practise falsehood; with their minds fixed on falsehood, they burn away.
(Those who) through the Guru write Truth, and Truth alone, and reflection (on it),
those people are true; they find the door of liberation.
True are (their) paper, pen and inkpot; writing Truth, they merge in the True One.
My God sits within (all) and watches;
by the Guru's grace, the one who meets (him) is accepted.
O Nanak, (one who) receives the Naam receives glory; (the Naam) is obtained from the perfect Guru. ॥8॥
123.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Guru the light of the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) dawns (within);
through the Guru's Shabad one clears away the filth of Haumai that clings (to the mind).
The mind becomes pure and is dyed in devotion day and night; through devotion one finds the Lord.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who themselves practise devotion and lead others to devotion.
Let us ever bow to such devoted servants (of the Lord), who sing the Lord's praises day and night.
The Creator himself brings about the cause (of devotion);
he sets (each one) to the task that pleases him.
By perfect fortune the Guru is served; through serving the Guru, peace is found.
When one dies (to self) again and again and lives (anew), then one gains something;
by the Guru's grace one enshrines the Lord in the mind.
One who enshrines the Lord in the mind is ever free, and with natural ease merges in Sahaj.
(One who) performs many rituals does not find liberation;
he roams from land to land, and in the love of another goes astray.
The deceitful one has wasted his life in vain; without the Shabad he suffers pain.
One who guards the running (mind), checks it and keeps it still,
by the Guru's grace attains the highest state.
The True Guru himself brings (him) into union (with the Lord); meeting the Beloved, he finds peace.
Some are attached to falsehood, and gain false fruits;
in the love of another their lives are wasted in vain.
They drown themselves and drown all their kin as well; speaking falsehood, they eat poison.
Some rare Gurmukh sees the mind (held still) within this body,
when through loving devotion he dries up Haumai.
Siddhas, seekers and those under vows of silence have kept fixing their attention; they too have not seen the mind (held still) within the body.
That Creator himself causes (all) to be done;
what else can anyone do? What can come of what the created (being) does?
O Nanak, the one to whom he gives the Naam receives it, and enshrines the Naam alone in the mind. ॥8॥
124.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Within this cave (of the body) is a treasure that never runs out;
within it dwells the Lord, unseen and boundless.
He himself is hidden and himself manifest; through the Guru's Shabad (one) sheds the self.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Amrit Name in the mind.
The Amrit Name is of the highest savour, and sweet; through the Guru's teaching they drink this Amrit.
Killing Haumai, (one who) has had the hard (adamantine) doors opened
has found the priceless Naam by the Guru's grace.
Without the Shabad no one finds the Naam; by the Guru's grace (it) is enshrined in the mind.
One who has put the true collyrium (eye-salve) of the Guru's wisdom in the eyes
has light within, and has driven off the darkness of ignorance;
(his) light has merged in the Light, the mind is won over, and he wins glory at the Lord's door.
One who goes outside the body to search
does not find the Naam, and suffers great pain, (like one pressed into) forced labour.
The blind manmukh does not understand; when, after wandering about, he comes back, he finds the thing (the Name) through the Guru.
When by the Guru's grace one finds the True Lord,
one sees (him) in the mind and in the body, and the filth of Haumai goes.
Sitting in the sacred place (within), he ever sings the Lord's praises, and through the Shabad merges in the True One.
One who has barred the nine doors and held back the running (mind)
comes to dwell in the tenth (door), his own home.
There the unstruck melodies of the Shabad play day and night; through the Guru's teaching he lets (others) hear the Shabad.
Without the Shabad there is darkness within;
(one) neither finds the thing (the Name) nor does the round (of births) end.
The key is in the True Guru's hand; by no other means does the door open; the Guru is met by perfect fortune.
You are hidden and manifest in all places;
by the Guru's grace, meeting (you), this understanding is gained.
O Nanak, ever praise the Naam; through the Guru (it) is enshrined in the mind. ॥8॥
124.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukh meets (the Lord); (the Lord) himself unites (him with himself).
Death does not cast its eye on him, and pain does not torment (him).
Killing Haumai, he breaks all bonds; the Gurmukh is made beautiful through the Shabad.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who are made beautiful through the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The Gurmukh sings (his praises), the Gurmukh dances (in joy), and fixes his mind on the Lord.
The Gurmukh, living and dying, is approved (by the Lord);
his life does not waste away; the Shabad is his familiar companion.
The Gurmukh does not die, nor does death devour him; the Gurmukh merges in the True One.
The Gurmukh wins glory at the Lord's door;
the Gurmukh sheds the self from within.
He crosses over himself and carries all his kin across; the Gurmukh makes his life worthy.
Pain never touches the Gurmukh's body;
the Gurmukh's pain of Haumai is ended.
The Gurmukh's mind is pure, no filth clings to it again; the Gurmukh merges in Sahaj.
The Gurmukh receives the Name, and glory;
the Gurmukh sings (his) praises and wins honour.
He stays ever in bliss, day and night; the Gurmukh makes the Shabad (of praise) his work.
The Gurmukh is dyed in the Shabad day and night;
through all four ages the Gurmukh has known (the Lord).
The Gurmukh sings (his) praises and is ever pure; through the Shabad he performs devotion.
Without the Guru there is pitch darkness;
seized by Jamkaal, (people) cry out.
Day and night they are diseased; they are worms of filth, and in filth they suffer pain.
The Gurmukh (knows that the Lord) himself does and has (all) done;
in the Gurmukh's heart he himself comes and dwells.
O Nanak, through the Name honour is received; (it) is obtained from the perfect Guru. ॥8॥
125.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One Light is the light in (all) bodies;
the perfect True Guru shows (this) through the Shabad.
He himself has made the difference within the hearts; he himself has fashioned the whole design.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who sing the praises of the True Lord.
No one finds Sahaj without the Guru; through the Guru one merges in Sahaj.
You yourself are beautiful, and you yourself enchant the world;
you yourself, by your glance of grace, string the world (on your thread);
you yourself give pain and pleasure, O Creator; through the Guru the Lord is shown.
The Creator himself does and has (all) done;
he himself enshrines the Guru's Shabad in the mind.
From the Shabad springs the Amrit Bani; the Gurmukh speaks it and lets (others) hear it.
He himself is the Creator, himself the Enjoyer;
he breaks the bonds (of beings), and is ever free.
The True One himself is ever free; he himself, the Unseen, makes himself known.
He himself is Maya, and himself its shadow (its spell);
he himself is attachment; he has created the whole world.
He himself is the Giver of virtues and sings (his own) praises; he himself speaks (them) and lets (others) hear (them).
He himself does and has (all) done;
he himself sets up and himself pulls down;
nothing happens outside you; you yourself set (all) to their tasks.
He himself kills and himself gives life;
he himself brings (beings) together and unites (them) in union (with himself).
Through service, lasting peace has been found; through the Guru one merges in Sahaj.
He himself is the highest of the high;
only the rare one to whom he himself shows (himself) sees (him).
O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (his) heart; (the Lord) himself watches over (all) and reveals (himself). ॥8॥
126.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My God is fully pervading all places;
by the Guru's grace, within the home (of the heart) itself, I have found (him).
I serve (him) ever and meditate on (him) with a single mind; through the Guru (one) merges in the True One.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the Life of the World in the mind.
The Lord, the Life of the World, is fearless, the Giver; through the Guru's teaching (they) merge in Sahaj.
Within the home (of the heart) are the earth, the bull Dhaul (said to bear it) and the nether worlds;
within the home itself is the Beloved, ever young.
The Giver of peace is ever in bliss; through the Guru's teaching (one) merges in Sahaj.
(While) within the body there is Haumai and the sense of mine,
the round of birth and death does not end.
Whoever becomes Gurmukh kills Haumai, and meditates on the True One alone.
Within the body are two brothers, sin and virtue;
the two together have brought forth the world.
One who kills both and goes and enters the one home merges in Sahaj through the Guru's teaching.
In the home itself, through the love of another, there is darkness;
when one gives up Haumai and the sense of mine, there is light;
the Shabad, the Giver of peace, becomes manifest, and (one) meditates on the Naam day and night.
Within is the Light whose expanse is manifest (as the world);
through the Guru's teaching the darkness has gone;
the lotus (of the heart) has blossomed, lasting peace has been found, and (his) light is merged in the Light.
Within the mansion (of the body) are storehouses filled with jewels;
the Gurmukh obtains the boundless Naam.
The Gurmukh, the trader, ever deals (in it), and ever earns the profit of the Naam.
He himself keeps the merchandise (of the Name), and himself gives (it);
through the Guru, many a one trades (in it).
O Nanak, the one on whom he casts his glance of grace obtains (it); in his mercy he enshrines (it) in the mind. ॥8॥
126.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Lord himself unites (one with himself) and has (him) serve (him);
through the Guru's Shabad the love of duality goes.
The Lord is pure, ever the Giver of virtues; the Lord himself merges (his servants) in (his) virtues.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who enshrine the True One, ever true, in the heart.
The True Name is ever pure; through the Guru's Shabad (they) enshrine (it) in the mind.
He himself is the Guru and the Giver; he is the Maker (of beings) according to (their) deeds.
(His) servants serve (him); through the Guru they have known the Lord.
Through the Amrit Name (his) servants are ever beautiful; through the Guru's teaching they obtain the Lord's sweet essence.
Within this cave (of the body) one place is made beautiful,
(when) the perfect Guru has ended Haumai and doubt.
Day and night (such ones), dyed in (his) love, praise the Naam; by the Guru's grace they find (him).
Through the Guru's Shabad this (soul) reflects on the cave (of the body),
(and) the immaculate Name of Murari dwells within (him);
he sings the Lord's praises, is made beautiful by the Shabad, and meeting the Beloved, finds peace.
Jam, the toll-collector, levies his tax on those in the love of another;
he punishes those who have strayed from the Name.
He takes account of every ghari and muhat (every moment), and has (all) weighed out, ratti by ratti, masa by masa (to the smallest weight).
(The bride who) in her parents' home (this world) does not remember her Husband,
robbed by duality, weeps and wails aloud;
utterly of a bad home, unlovely and ill-natured, she does not find her Husband even in a dream.
(She who) in her parents' home has enshrined her Husband in her mind,
to her the perfect Guru has shown (him) ever present;
that bride keeps her Husband clasped to her bosom; through the Shabad she delights in her Husband, and her bed is beautiful.
He himself calls (beings) to himself and gives (this gift);
he enshrines his own Name in the mind.
O Nanak, (one who) receives the Naam receives glory, and ever, day and night, sings (his) praises. ॥8॥
127.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Exalted is the birth, and blessed the place of dwelling, of those
who serve the True Guru and, living at home, remain detached (from Maya).
They abide in the Lord's love, ever dyed in (that) love; their minds are sated with the Lord's sweet essence.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who read, understand and enshrine (the Name) in the mind.
Through the Guru they read and praise the Lord's Name, and win honour at the True One's door.
The Lord, unseen and unfathomable, is contained in all;
by no means at all can he be attained.
If he grants his grace, the True Guru is met, and with his glance of grace (the Lord) unites (one) in union (with himself).
One who reads in the love of another does not understand;
he frets and burns for the sake of Maya of the three qualities.
The bonds of the three qualities are broken through the Guru's Shabad; through the Guru's Shabad one is set free.
This fickle mind does not come under control;
caught in duality, it runs off in the ten directions.
It is a worm of poison, steeped in poison, and in poison itself it rots away.
(The manmukh) keeps saying I, I, and makes a show of himself;
he performs many rites, (but) none of them is accepted.
(O God,) nothing happens apart from you; those (you) forgive are made beautiful through the Shabad.
(One who) does not understand the Lord is born and wastes away;
day and night (such people) wander in the love of another.
The manmukh's life has gone in vain; in the end he departed repenting.
The Husband is in a far land, and (the wife) adorns herself:
such are the deeds the blind manmukh does.
He has no honour in this world and no shelter in the next; he wastes his life in vain.
Some rare one has known the Lord's Name,
recognising (it) through the perfect Guru's Shabad.
Every day, day and night, he performs devotion, and in Sahaj he finds peace.
The One, he alone, is at work in all;
only some rare one understands (this) through the Guru.
O Nanak, the servants imbued with the Name look beautiful; in his mercy (the Lord) himself unites (them with himself). ॥9॥
128.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukhs read (the scriptures) and have themselves called pandits,
(but) in the love of another they suffer great pain.
Drunk on the poison (of Maya), they perceive nothing; again and again they come into (new) births.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who kill Haumai and are united (with the Lord).
Through serving the Guru the Lord has come to dwell in (their) minds, and in Sahaj they drink the Lord's sweet essence.
(The pandits) read the Veda, (but) have not come to taste the Lord's sweet essence;
enticed by Maya, they only hold forth in dispute.
Those of ignorant mind are ever in darkness; those who understand through the Guru sing of the Lord.
When the Indescribable One is spoken of, through the Shabad (he) is found lovely;
through the Guru's teaching the True One becomes dear to the mind.
Day and night they dwell on the True One, the True One alone; this mind (of theirs) is dyed in the True One.
Those dyed in the True One love the True One alone;
(God) himself gives (this gift), and does not regret (the giving).
Through the Guru's Shabad they have ever known the True One; meeting the True One, they find peace.
The filth of falsehood and deceit does not cling to them;
by the Guru's grace (such a one) stays awake day and night.
The pure Name dwells within (his) heart, and (his) light merges in the Light.
(The manmukhs) read about the three qualities, (but) do not know the Lord, the essence (of all);
strayed from the Root, they do not recognise the Guru's Shabad.
Gripped by attachment, they perceive nothing; the Lord is found through the Guru's Shabad.
The Veda speaks aloud of Maya of the three qualities;
the manmukhs, in the love of another, do not understand.
They read about the three qualities, and do not know the One Lord; without understanding, they suffer pain.
When it pleases him, he himself unites (one with himself),
and through the Guru's Shabad takes away anxiety and pain.
O Nanak, true and lasting is the glory of the Name; by trusting in the Name alone (beings) find peace. ॥8॥
128.2: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
He himself is Nirgun, and he himself Sargun;
one who recognises (this) essence is the true pandit.
Enshrining the Lord's Name in the mind, he himself crosses over and carries all his kin across.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who taste the Lord's sweet essence and know its savour.
Those who taste the Lord's sweet essence, those servants, are pure, and meditate on the pure Name.
He alone is nihkarmi who reflects on the Shabad;
within (him) is the essence, and through wisdom he kills Haumai.
He obtains the treasure of the Name, the nine treasures, and, erasing the three qualities, merges (in the Lord).
One who acts in Haumai does not become nihkarmi;
by the Guru's grace (alone) does one shed Haumai.
Within (him) is discernment (between good and bad); he ever examines himself, and through the Guru's Shabad sings (the Lord's) praises.
The Lord (himself) is the lake, the ocean; he alone is pure.
The Sants, having become Gurmukh, ever peck (the pearls of the Name) from it.
They bathe (in it) ever, day and night, and wash away the filth of Haumai.
(One who dwells) in loving devotion is a pure swan;
having killed Haumai, he dwells in the Lord's lake.
Day and night in love with the true Shabad, he gains a dwelling in the Lord's lake.
The manmukh is ever a filthy crane, smeared with the filth of Haumai;
he bathes, but (his) filth does not go.
(One who) dies while living and reflects on the Guru's Shabad washes away the filth of Haumai.
(He) found the precious jewel (of the Name) within (his own) home (the heart),
(to whom) the perfect True Guru made the Shabad heard.
By the Guru's grace (his) darkness was dispelled; there was light in the heart, and (he) recognised his own self.
(God) himself creates, and himself watches over (all);
that person is accepted who serves the True Guru.
O Nanak, the Naam dwells within (his) heart; by the Guru's grace (he) attains (the Lord). ॥8॥
129.1: Raag Majh, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The whole world is (caught in) attachment to Maya;
(beings of) the three qualities are seen enticed by Maya.
By the Guru's grace some rare one understands (this), and fixes his attention in the fourth state.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who burn away attachment to Maya through the Shabad.
One who burns away attachment to Maya fixes the mind on the Lord, and wins honour at the Lord's door, in (his) mansion.
Maya is the root of the goddesses and gods,
(Maya,) which brought forth the Simritis and the Shastras.
Lust and anger have spread through the world; coming and going, (beings) suffer pain.
In it (this world) one jewel of divine wisdom has (also) been placed;
(the one who), by the Guru's grace, has enshrined (it) in the mind
practises continence, truthful living, self-restraint and truth, and through the perfect Guru meditates on the Naam.
In her parents' home (this world) the bride has strayed, lost in doubt;
clinging to another, she repents afterwards.
She loses both this world and the next, and finds no peace even in a dream.
The bride who, in her parents' home, cherishes her Husband (in her heart)
sees (him) by the Guru's grace right beside her;
in Sahaj she stays dyed in her Husband's love, and makes the Shabad her adornment.
Fruitful is the life of those who have found the True Guru;
through the Guru's Shabad they have burned away the love of another.
The One alone pervades within (their) hearts; joining the Sat Sangat, they sing the Lord's praises.
One who does not serve the True Guru: why did he come (into the world)?
Cursed is his life; he has wasted his birth in vain.
The Naam does not come into the manmukh's mind; without the Name he suffers great pain.
He who fashioned the world alone knows (its play);
he himself unites (with himself the one who) recognises (him) through the Shabad.
O Nanak, the Naam has come to those servants on whose foreheads this destiny was written by the Lord from the start. ॥8॥
129.2: Raag Majh, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
He himself is the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond;
he himself establishes (the world), and having established it, (himself) pulls it down.
The One, he alone, is at work in all; through the Guru (beings) win honour.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who meditate on the Name of the Formless One.
No form or feature is his, (yet) he is seen in each and every heart; through the Guru the Unseen is perceived.
(O God,) you are merciful and kind; you alone are that God.
Without you there is no other at all.
(On whom) the Guru bestows his grace, (to him) he gives the Naam; (such a one) stays merged in the Naam, in the Naam alone.
You yourself are the True Creator;
your storehouses are full of devotion.
One who receives the Name through the Guru has the mind drenched (in it), and enters Samadhi in Sahaj.
Day and night I sing your praises, O God;
I praise you, my Beloved.
I beg of no other than you; by the Guru's grace (alone) are you found.
(You are) inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses; no one has found your measure.
You show your mercy, and unite (one with yourself).
Through the perfect Guru's Shabad let (God) be meditated on; serving the Shabad, (people) find peace.
Virtuous is the tongue that sings (God's) praises;
(one who) praises the Naam is pleasing to the True One.
Through the Guru (that tongue) stays ever dyed in (his) love; meeting the True One, (such people) win honour.
The manmukh does his deeds in pride;
at the gamble he loses (his) life, the whole game.
Within (him) is greed, pitch darkness; again and again he comes and goes.
The Creator himself gives glory
to those for whom he himself set down this writ from the start.
O Nanak, (they) receive the Naam, the destroyer of fear, and through the Guru's Shabad find peace. ॥8॥
130.1: Raag Majh, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Unseen (Lord) is within (all), (yet) cannot be perceived;
(he) has taken the jewel of the Naam and kept it hidden (within).
Inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses, higher than all, (he) is perceived through the Guru's Shabad.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who make the Naam heard in Kalyug.
The True One upholds (his) beloved Sants; by great good fortune is the sight (of them) obtained.
He for whom seekers and Siddhas wander about,
(on whom) the Brahmas and Indras meditate in their hearts,
whom the thirty-three crore (gods) search for: (the fortunate,) meeting the Guru, sing of him in their hearts.
(O God,) at all hours the wind repeats (your Name);
the earth is (your) servant, a maid who waits at (your) feet.
You dwell in (beings of) all the sources of life and all tongues; you are pleasing to the minds of all.
The True Master becomes known through the Guru;
through the perfect Guru's Shabad (he) is recognised.
Those who have drunk (the nectar of the Name) are the ones satisfied; in the Truest of the True they are fulfilled.
In his home (the heart) is Sahaj; he alone is at ease;
he ever enjoys bliss, delight and joyful play.
He is the wealthy one, he the great banker, who fixes his mind on the Guru's feet.
(O God,) first you provided the sustenance,
and afterwards you created the being.
O Lord, there is no other giver as great as you; no one can be set beside you as your equal.
One with whom you are pleased meditates on you,
and lives by the mantra (teaching) of the holy.
He himself crosses over and carries all his kin across; at (your) court he meets no hindrance.
You are great, the highest of the high;
you are without end, the very greatest of the great.
I go as a sacrifice to you; Nanak is a slave of (your) slaves. ॥8॥
131.1: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Who is the one set free? Who is the one joined (to God)?
Who is the one who truly knows (God)? Who is the one who speaks (of him)?
Who is the householder, who the detached one? Who is the one who knows (the Lord's) worth?
In what way is one bound, and in what way set free?
In what way does the coming and going (of birth and death) end?
Who does (good) deeds, who is nihkarmi? Who is the one who speaks (God's praise) and has (others) speak it?
Who is the one at peace, who the one in pain?
Who is the one who faces (the Guru), who the one turned away?
In what way is (God) met, in what way is one parted (from him)? Who makes this way known?
What Word is it that holds the wandering (mind) still?
What is the teaching by which one bears pain and pleasure as one?
What way of life lets one meditate on the Supreme Lord? In what way may one sing (his) Kirtan?
The Gurmukh is the one set free; the Gurmukh is the one joined (to God).
The Gurmukh is the one who truly knows; the Gurmukh is the one who speaks (of God).
Blessed is the Gurmukh, householder or detached; the Gurmukh knows (the Lord's) worth.
Through Haumai one is bound; through the Guru one is set free.
Through the Guru the coming and going ends.
The Gurmukh does (good) deeds, the Gurmukh is nihkarmi; whatever the Gurmukh does, he does in (God's) love.
The Gurmukh is at peace, the manmukh in pain.
The Gurmukh faces (the Guru); the manmukh is turned away.
Through the Guru (God) is met; the manmukh is parted (from him); the Gurmukh makes the way known.
The Guru's Word is what holds the wandering (mind) still.
Through the Guru's teaching one bears pain and pleasure as one.
The way of life the Guru gives is what lets one meditate on the Supreme Lord; through the Guru one sings (his) Kirtan.
(God) himself has made this whole creation;
he himself does, has (all) done, and establishes (all).
From the One he has become countless (forms); O Nanak, (all) merges again in the One. ॥9॥
131.2: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
God is imperishable: then what is there (for his servant) to fret about?
The Lord is the Master of all good fortune: then his servant lives in great ease.
(O God,) you give peace to the soul, the breath of life and the mind; in what you do, (your servants) find peace.
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those to whose mind and body you are dear through the Guru.
You are my mountain, you are my shelter; no one can be set beside you as your equal.
The one to whom what you do seems sweet,
that servant has seen the Supreme Lord in each and every heart.
In every place and in the spaces between, it is you, you alone; you, the One and only, are at work (everywhere).
You are the giver of every wish;
(your) storehouses are full of devotion and love.
Those whom you have kept safe in your mercy, they alone, by your full grace, stay merged (in you).
(You) have drawn (them) up out of the blind well (of Maya) onto the bank;
in your mercy (you) have looked on (your) servants with a glance of grace.
They sing the praises of the Perfect, Imperishable (Lord); by telling and hearing, (his praises) never run short.
Here and in the world beyond, you alone are the protector;
in the mother's womb it was you who nourished (us).
The fire of Maya cannot touch those who, dyed in (your) love, sing (your) praises.
Which of your virtues can I tell and keep in mind?
Within my mind and body I see you, and you alone.
You are my friend, my companion, my Master; I know no other but you.
O God, the one whose helper you have become
is not touched by even a hot wind.
You are the Master, the shelter, the giver of peace; repeating (your Name) in the Sat Sangat, (your servants) make you manifest (within them).
You are lofty, fathomless, boundless, beyond price;
you are the True Master; (I am) your servant, your slave.
You are the sovereign Lord, and your rule stands for ever; Nanak goes as a sacrifice to you, again and again. ॥8॥
132.1: Raag Majh, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Day after day let the Beloved Lord be cherished (in the heart);
let him never at all be put out of the mind.
Let the company of the Sants be found,
through which one does not go on the path of Jam.
Take the Lord's Name as provisions (for the road), and no stain falls on your family.
Those who remember the Master
are not cast into hell.
Not even a hot wind touches those in whose mind (the Lord) has come to dwell.
They alone are fair and handsome
who sit in the Saadh Sangat.
Those who have gathered the Lord's wealth (the Name), they alone are deep and boundless (of heart).
Let the Lord's nectar, the home of all delights, be drunk;
seeing the face of (the Lord's) servant, one lives (in spirit).
Set all your affairs right: worship the Guru's feet each day.
One whom the Lord has made his own
is the one who will repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world.
He is the hero, he is the chief, on whose forehead (such) fortune is (written).
Diving deep within the mind, let God be sought out;
this is the enjoyment of (all) pleasures, this is sovereignty.
(In those who did so) nothing evil has ever arisen; attached to the true work, they have crossed over.
One who has enshrined the Creator in the mind
has obtained the fruit of (human) birth.
(O soul-bride,) the Lord, your Husband, pleases your mind: your wedded bliss has become lasting.
(He) has obtained the imperishable treasure (the Name),
(who has come) to the shelter of the Destroyer of fear.
O Nanak, attaching (him) to his hem, (the Lord) has carried (him) across; (he) has won (the game of) this priceless life. ॥8॥
132.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Majh, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Lord's Name again and again, the mind grows steady.
Remembering, remembering the divine Guru, (all) fears are erased and gone far away.
If one comes to the shelter of the Supreme Lord, why then should he pine in grief?
Serving the feet of the Sants and the holy, every wish is fulfilled.
In each and every heart the One is at work; he fills the water, the land and the sky.
One who has served the Destroyer of sins has been made pure by the dust of the Sants' feet.
The Master himself has set all (the world) free; repeating the Lord's Name, it has grown cool and calm.
The Creator has done justice: the wicked have died, become like stuffed calves (lifeless within).
Nanak is dyed in the True Name, and sees the Lord ever present (with him). ॥8॥
133.1: Barah Maha: Raag Majh, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Parted (from you) by the deeds we have done, O Lord (Ram), unite (us with you) in your mercy.
Having roamed the four quarters and the ten directions, worn out, we have come to God's shelter.
A cow that gives no milk is of no use at all;
without water the crop wilts and yields no money;
(so too,) if the Lord, the Husband, the Friend, is not met, where can rest be found?
Where the Lord, the Husband, is not made manifest in the home (of the heart), those towns and villages are a (blazing) furnace.
All adornments, betel and (other) pleasures, the body along with them, are all worthless;
for the bride bereft of God, her Master and Husband, all friends and companions are as Jam.
Nanak's prayer is this: in your mercy, grant (me your) Name.
O Lord, unite (me) with the Master, God, whose abode stands for ever. ॥1॥
133.2: In Chet, let Govind be worshipped in remembrance, and great bliss wells up.
Meeting the Sants, (this gift) is found: the tongue utters the Naam.
Only one who has found his God is to be counted as having truly come (into the world).
To live even a moment without him: know that life to be wasted.
(He) fills the water, the land and the sky, and pervades the forests too;
if such a God does not come to mind, how much of (that) pain can I count?
Those who have enjoyed (union with) that God: their fortune is beyond measure.
(My) mind longs for the sight of the Lord; in Nanak's mind is a thirst (for it).
Whoever unites (me) with that God in Chet, at his feet I would fall. ॥2॥
133.3: In Vaisakh, how can they keep heart, the brides cut off (from the Husband), who are parted from (his) love?
Forgetting the Lord, the Friend, the (all-pervading) Being, they are held fast by deceitful Maya.
Son, wife and wealth go along with no one; he, the Lord, alone is the imperishable (companion).
Tangled again and again in attachment to false pursuits, the whole (world) has perished.
Without the Name of the One Lord, (their deeds) are snatched away from them on the road ahead.
Forgetting the Beloved Lord, one comes to ruin; without God there is no other (to stand by one).
Those who hold to the feet of the Beloved: spotless is their good name.
O God, Nanak's prayer (to you) is this: come and meet (me), O God, that I may attain you.
Vaisakh seems lovely only when the Sant (the Guru) is met, and (through him) that Lord. ॥3॥
134.1: In Jeth one should be joined to the Lord, before whom all bow down.
Once one holds to the hem of the Lord, the Friend, he lets no one bind (that one).
The Name of God is rubies and pearls; no thief can tunnel through to them.
All the delights that please the mind are Narayan's.
Whatever the Lord wills, he does; and that alone his creatures do.
Those God has made his own are the ones hailed as blessed.
If (he) could be had by one's own taking, why would (people) weep in separation?
O Nanak, those who find the company of the holy (Guru) enjoy the delights (of union).
Jeth is full of joy for one who has the Lord as Master, on whose forehead (such) fortune is (written). ॥4॥
134.2: Asarh burns for those beside whom the Lord, the Husband, is not;
forsaking the Being who is the Life of the world, (they put their) hope in mortal men.
In the love of another one is ruined; the noose of Jam falls on (her) neck.
As one sows, so one reaps: (one meets) what is written on one's forehead.
The night (of life) passed; she repented, and rose and went, her hope broken.
Those who meet the holy one (the Guru) are released in the Lord's court.
O God, show your mercy, that thirst for the sight of you may stay (in me).
O God, I have no other but you; this is Nanak's supplication.
Asarh is pleasant to the one in whose mind the Lord's feet dwell. ॥5॥
134.3: In Sawan, the bride who loves (the Lord's) lotus feet is green and in bloom.
Body and mind dyed in the True One's love, she has the one Name as her support.
The false delights of Maya's poison all look (to her) like ashes.
Lovely is the drop of the Lord's nectar; meeting the holy (Guru), one is able to drink it.
Forest and grass have burst into bloom at the touch of God, the all-powerful, boundless Being.
(My) mind longs to meet the Lord; (he alone) unites (one with himself) by his grace.
The companions who have found God: I am ever a sacrifice to them.
Says Nanak, O dear Lord, show mercy; you are the one who adorns (the soul) through the Shabad.
Sawan belongs to those happy soul-brides on whose heart the Name of Ram is a necklace. ॥6॥
134.4: In Bhadon, (the soul-bride) whose love is fixed on another has strayed, lost in doubt.
She has put on a hundred thousand adornments, (but) they are of no use at all.
On the day the body perishes, at that hour (her own people) will call it a pret (the dead).
Jam's messengers seize (the soul) and drive it on, and tell no one their secret (where they take it).
Those she was bound to in love leave her in an instant and stand aside.
She wrings her hands, the body trembles, (its colour) turns from black to white.
As one sows, so one reaps: (the body) is the field of deeds.
O Nanak, to those who come to God's refuge, God gives the ship of his feet.
In Bhadon they are not cast into hell whose protector and loving friend is the Guru. ॥7॥
134.5: In Assu love wells up (within me): how may I go and meet the Lord?
In mind and body there is a great thirst for (his) sight; O mother, if only someone would bring (him) and unite (us).
The Sants are helpers (on the way) of love; I have fallen at their feet.
Without God, how can peace be found? There is no other place (for it).
Those who have tasted the delight of love stay satisfied and fulfilled.
Giving up self-conceit, they pray: O God, attach (us) to the hem of your robe.
She whom the Lord, the Husband, has united (with himself) does not part (from him) and go anywhere else.
Apart from God there is no other; Nanak has come to the Lord's refuge.
In Assu they dwell in peace on whom the Lord, the King, has mercy. ॥8॥
135.1: In Katak, (what one meets is) the deeds one has done; no one else can be blamed.
Strayed from the Supreme God, one is gripped by every disease.
Those who turn their faces away from the Lord suffer separation through births.
In a moment, all the pleasures of Maya, as many as they were, have turned bitter.
No one can stand between (as a go-between); before whom can they weep day after day?
Nothing comes of (one's own) doing; the lot written from the start (is what comes).
By great good fortune, if my God is met, then all the pains of separation are lifted.
O God, my Master, you who free (beings) from bondage, save Nanak.
In Katak, if the Saadh Sangat is found, all anxieties vanish. ॥9॥
135.2: In the month of Maghar they look lovely who sit beside the Lord, their Husband.
How can I count the glory of those whom the Master has united (with himself)?
With the Lord, in the company of their holy friends, their body and mind have blossomed.
Those cut off from the holy remain all alone.
Their pain never leaves them; they have fallen into Jam's power.
Those who have enjoyed (union with) their God are seen ever standing alert (in his service).
The Lord's jewels, gems and rubies (his Name and praises) are set at their throats.
Nanak longs for the dust (of the feet) of those who have fallen at God's door, in his refuge.
In Maghar God is to be worshipped: (those who do so) are not born again. ॥10॥
135.3: In Poh the frost does not trouble (the bride) whom the Lord, her Husband, has met in close embrace.
Her mind is pierced through by (his) lotus feet; her every breath clings to his sight.
(She has) the shelter of Govind, Gopal, the King; service of the Master is (her) gain.
The poison (of Maya) cannot touch her; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), she is immersed in (God's) virtues.
She has met the One from whom she sprang, and is absorbed in true love.
The Supreme Lord has taken her by the hand; she will not be parted again.
I am a sacrifice a hundred thousand times to the Lord, the Friend, inaccessible, unfathomable.
O Nanak, it falls to Narayan to keep the honour of those who have fallen at his door.
Poh is lovely, and every comfort is (hers), whom the Carefree (Lord) forgives. ॥11॥
135.4: In Magh, let your holy dip be in the company of the holy: bathe in the dust (of their feet).
Meditate on the Lord's Name and listen to it, and give it to all.
(Then) the filth of the deeds of (many) births is washed off, and pride leaves the mind.
One is not lured by lust or anger, and the dog of greed is destroyed.
As one walks on the true path, the whole world sings one's praise.
Compassion for (all) beings is accepted as (bathing at) the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage and (doing) every deed of merit.
The one to whom (God) gives (this) in his mercy is the one who is truly wise.
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who have met their God.
In Magh they alone are counted pure on whom the perfect Guru is merciful. ॥12॥
136.1: In Phagun bliss springs up (in those) to whom the Lord, the Friend, has come and been revealed.
The Sants, helpers (on the way) to the Lord, have in their mercy united (them with him).
The bed (of the heart) is lovely, all comforts are there; now there is no room for sorrows.
The desire of the fortunate bride is fulfilled: she has found the Lord, the King, as her Husband.
Gathering together, (her) companions sing songs of joy, raising the songs of Govind.
No other is seen like the Lord; no second can be set beside him as his equal.
He has set right this world and the next, and given (them) a place that does not shake.
He has kept (them) safe from the world-ocean; (such a one) does not run again into birth.
The tongue is one, (his) virtues countless; O Nanak, falling at (his) feet, (beings) cross over.
In Phagun let him be praised ever, who has not a grain of greed. ॥13॥
136.2: Each and every one who has meditated on the Naam has had (their) affairs fulfilled.
Those who have worshipped the Lord, the perfect Guru, are found genuine in the court of the True One.
The Lord's feet are a treasury of every comfort; (they) have crossed the terrifying world-ocean, hard (to cross).
They have obtained loving devotion; they do not burn in the poison (of Maya).
Their falsehoods are gone, duality has fled; they are filled to the full with the True One.
They serve the Supreme Lord God, keeping the One in their minds.
Every month, day and hour is good for the one on whom he casts his glance of grace.
Nanak begs for the gift of your sight: O Lord, show mercy. ॥14॥
136.3: Din Raini: Raag Majh, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Let me serve my own True Guru, and remember the Lord through all the days and nights.
Giving up self-conceit, let me fall into (his) refuge and speak sweet words with my mouth:
(I am) parted birth after birth; unite (me with) the Lord, (my) friend and beloved.
O sister, the beings who are parted from the Lord do not dwell in peace.
Without the Lord, the Husband, no rest is found; I have searched through all the skies and seen.
I am parted by what I myself have done; no one else is to be blamed.
O God, show mercy and save (me); there is no other who can do and cause (anything) to be done.
O Lord, without you (one must) roll in the dust; to whom shall (we) tell (our) laments?
This is Nanak's prayer: that I may see the Lord, the noble One, with my eyes.
He hears the anguish of the soul: the Lord, the all-powerful, infinite Being.
In death and in life he is to be worshipped, the support of all.
In her in-laws' home and in her parents' home (alike, the bride) belongs to that Husband, whose family is vast.
He is lofty, inaccessible, of fathomless wisdom; he has no end, no near shore and no far shore.
He is pleased by the service (in which one) becomes the dust of the Sants' feet.
He is the Master of the meek, the merciful Lord, the uplifter of the fallen.
From the beginning, through the ages, the Creator, whose Name is true, has kept (all).
No one knows his worth; there is no one who can weigh him.
He dwells within mind and body; O Nanak, there is no reckoning (of him).
To those who serve God day and night, I am ever a sacrifice.
The Sants worship him for ever and ever, the forgiver of all,
who fashioned soul and body, and in his mercy gave life.
Through the Guru's Shabad let him be worshipped; let his pure mantra be repeated.
His worth cannot be told; the Supreme God is without end.
The one in whose mind Narayan dwells is called fortunate.
The longing of the soul is fulfilled when the Master, the Husband, is met.
Nanak lives by repeating (the Name of) the Lord; all faults are destroyed.
The being who does not forget (him) day or night turns green (with life).
O God, you are full of every power; (you are) the refuge of me, the humble one.
O Lord, I have taken hold of your shelter in my mind; I live by repeating (your) Name again and again.
O God, show your mercy, that I may stay merged in the dust (of the feet) of your servants.
As you keep me, so I live; what you give, I wear and eat.
O God, have me make that effort (by which), meeting the Saadh (the Guru), I may sing (your) praises.
No other place comes to mind: where am I to go and cry out?
O destroyer of ignorance, dispeller of darkness, lofty, inaccessible, immeasurable (Lord),
unite with yourself, O Lord, the mind that is parted; this is Nanak's (one) aim.
All blessings come on that day, O Lord, when I touch the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
137.1: Vaar Majh ki: by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji), with saloks; to be sung to the tune of Malak Murid and Chandrahara Sohia.
There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, realised by the Guru's grace.
Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Guru is the Giver; the Guru is the home of snow (the source of coolness); the Guru is the lamp in the three worlds.
O Nanak, (from him comes) the imperishable treasure; when the mind trusts (him), there is peace. ॥1॥
137.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In the first (stage of life, the child) is lovingly drawn to the milk of the breast;
in the second, (it) comes to know its mother and father;
in the third, (it knows its) brother, brother's wife and sister;
in the fourth, the love of play springs up;
in the fifth, the running after food and drink;
in the sixth, lust, which does not ask about caste;
in the seventh, gathering (things), he makes his dwelling in a house;
in the eighth, anger (rises), and the body wears away;
in the ninth, (the hair turns) white and the breath comes in gasps;
in the tenth, he is burned and turns to ashes.
The companions who went (with him to the pyre) cried out in loud wails;
the swan (the soul) has flown, and asks the way.
He came and he went; even his name has died.
Afterwards, (they say:) call the crows to the leaf-plate.
O Nanak, the manmukh's love is blind;
without the Guru, the world has drowned. ॥2॥
138.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
At ten (one is) in childhood, at twenty in the age of desire; at thirty, one is called handsome;
at forty, one is in full bloom; at fifty, the foot starts to slip; at sixty, old age comes;
at seventy, one loses one's wits; at eighty, one cannot attend to one's affairs;
at ninety, one keeps to the bed, and knows no strength of one's own at all.
I have sought, I have searched, I have seen; says Nanak, the world is a white mansion made of smoke. ॥3॥
138.2: You are the Creator, the all-pervading Being, the Inaccessible; you yourself brought forth the creation.
You made it of colour upon colour, in many, many ways and kinds.
You know (it), you who made (it); the whole play is yours.
Some come, some rise up and go; without the Name (all) die and depart.
The Gurmukhs are dyed deep red, dyed in the colour of the Lord's love.
Serve him, the True One, the Stainless, the Lord, the all-pervading Being, the Maker.
