You yourself alone are all-wise, the great Being, great indeed.
O my True One, I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to those who meditate on you with mind and heart. ॥1॥
138.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Placing the soul (in it), (God) fashioned the body, and kept it, shaping its form.
With the eyes it sees, with the tongue it speaks; in the ears the power of hearing dwells.
With the feet it walks, with the hands it works; what is given (to it) it wears and eats.
Him who made and fashioned it, it does not know; the blind one does blind deeds.
When (the vessel) breaks, it becomes a potsherd; that shape cannot be fashioned again.
O Nanak, without the Guru there is no honour; without honour (God's grace) no one gets across. ॥1॥
138.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
To hold what is given dearer than the One who gives it: know the manmukh to be such.
His understanding, his wisdom, his cleverness: in what words can they be told?
What one does sitting hidden within becomes known in all four directions.
Whoever practises dharma gets the name of the righteous; by committing sin one is known as a sinner.
O Creator, you yourself play out all these plays; what other can we name and speak of?
As long as your light is (in the body), so long it is you who speak in that light; without the light, let anyone do anything at all, and I will see and acknowledge it.
O Nanak, through the Guru the one Lord, skilful and all-knowing, has come into sight. ॥2॥
138.5: You yourself created the world, and you yourself set it to its worldly business.
Giving it the drugging herb of attachment, you have led the world astray from yourself.
Within (it) is the fire of craving; hungry and thirsty, (the world) is never sated.
This world is nothing but anxiety; (in it, beings) die and are born, come and go.
Without the True Guru attachment does not break; all have grown weary performing (ritual) deeds.
Through the Guru's teaching the Naam is meditated on; when it pleased you, (the soul) was sated in peace.
(Such a one) saves his whole family line; blessed is the mother who bore him.
Lovely are the glory and the understanding of one who has joined his mind to the Lord. ॥2॥
139.1: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Seeing without eyes, hearing without ears,
walking without feet, working without hands,
speaking without a tongue: so one dies while living.
O Nanak, it is by recognising (the Lord's) Hukam that one then meets the Master. ॥1॥
139.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
(The Lord) is seen, is heard of, is known (in his creation), yet the taste (of meeting him) is not had.
How can one who is lame, handless and blind run and fall upon (his) neck?
If one makes the fear (of God) one's feet, love one's hands, and attention (held on him) one's eyes,
says Nanak: O wise (soul-bride), in this way union with the Husband comes about. ॥2॥
139.3: For ever and ever you are the One; you yourself have staged the play of duality.
Creating Haumai and pride, you placed greed within beings.
Keep (them) as it pleases you; all do only what you make them do.
Some you forgive and unite with yourself; it is you who have set them in the Guru's teaching.
Some stand ready, doing your service; without the Name nothing else pleases them.
To them any other work is worthless; some you have set to the true work.
Son, wife and family are there, yet some, who are pleasing to you, stay untouched (by them).
They are pure within and without, merged in the True Name. ॥3॥
139.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Should I make a cave in the mountain of gold, or (dwell) in the waters of the netherworld;
whether on the earth or in the sky, should I stay upside down, on my head;
should I cover my body wholly in clothes, and make washing my constant work;
should I cry aloud the Vedas, white, red, yellow and black;
should I live filthy and grimy: (all this is) the vice of an evil understanding.
Nanak, reflecting on the Shabad, asks only this: may there be no I-ness and no me-and-mine, and may I not be (a self apart) at all. ॥1॥
139.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Washing his clothes, he washes his body, and thinks himself (a man of) self-restraint.
The filth stuck within he does not know; he scrubs and scrubs, washing (himself) from outside.
The blind one has strayed and fallen into the net of Jam.
He takes what belongs to another for his own, and in Haumai he suffers pain.
O Nanak, when through the Guru Haumai is broken, then one meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
he repeats the Naam, worships the Naam alone, and through the Naam is merged in peace. ॥2॥
139.6: Ordaining their union, (the Lord) has joined the body and the swan (the soul).
The very One who created (them) has also ordained (their) parting.
The fool goes on enjoying pleasures, (the root of) every pain.
From pleasure diseases arise, through the sins committed.
From joy spring sorrow and parting; so (beings) are brought forth and wasted away.
Keeping the reckonings of fools, (man) has taken on a wrangle (of birth and death).
The settlement lies in the True Guru's hands; he has put an end to the wrangle.
What the Creator does, that alone will be; (no one's) driving can drive it otherwise. ॥4॥
139.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who tells lies and eats carrion (what is another's by right)
is robbed himself, and has his companions robbed as well.
O Nanak, such a leader is found out. ॥1॥
140.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The one within whom the True One dwells utters the True Name with his mouth, and speaks the truth.
He himself walks on the Lord's path, and puts others on the Lord's path.
If what lies ahead is a place of pilgrimage (of clean, open water), the filth comes off; bathing in a stagnant pond, one gathers still more filth.
The True Guru is the perfect place of pilgrimage, who meditates on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, night and day.
He is set free himself, with his family, and, giving the Name of the Lord, Har Har, he frees the whole world.
Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to the one who repeats (the Naam) himself and has others repeat the Naam. ॥2॥
140.2: Some gather roots and tubers to eat, and make their dwelling in some corner of the forest.
Some put on saffron robes and wander about as Yogis and Sannyasis.
(Yet) within them is great craving, the longing for clothes and food.
Wasting their life in vain, they are neither householders nor renunciants.
Jamkaal does not lift from their heads, (for in them is) desire of the three kinds.
Through the Guru's teaching death does not come near, when one becomes the servant of (the Lord's) servants.
With the true Shabad and the True One in the mind, one is detached while living at home.
O Nanak, those who serve their True Guru become free of (worldly) hopes. ॥5॥
140.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If blood stains the clothes, the garment becomes unclean;
those who drink the blood of men, how can their mind be pure?
Says Nanak: take the name of God on your lips with a clean heart;
all else is the world's show, and (by it) you do false deeds. ॥1॥
140.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When I am nothing (within), what can I tell (others)? With no virtue in me, what can I make myself out to be?
Through what I do and what I say, I am full (of filth); again and again I am soiled, and I wash.
I do not understand myself, yet I make the people understand: such is the leader I become.
O Nanak, one who, being blind himself, shows (others) the way has all his companions robbed.
Going on ahead (to the world beyond), he is struck again and again on the face: then such a leader is found out. ॥2॥
140.5: In all the months and seasons, in every ghari and muhurat, you are to be contemplated.
By calculations (of lucky days) no one has found you, O True One, unseen and infinite.
The learned man in whom are greed, avarice and pride is to be called a fool.
It is the Name that should be read, the Name that should be understood, reflecting through the Guru's teaching.
Those who through the Guru's teaching have earned the wealth of the Naam have their storehouses filled with devotion.
Those who have accepted the pure Naam are found true at the door of the True One.
The One whose are the soul and the breath of life: his infinite light is within (every being).
You alone are the true banker; the rest of the world are pedlars. ॥6॥
140.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Make compassion your mosque, faith your prayer mat, and honest, lawful earning your Quran;
modesty your circumcision, a gentle nature your fast: in this way become a Muslim.
(Make) good conduct your Kaaba, truth your Pir, and good deeds your kalma and namaz;
(let) what pleases him be your rosary: (then), O Nanak, he keeps your honour. ॥1॥
141.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, what is another's by right is (as) the pig to the one (the Muslim) and the cow to the other (the Hindu).
The Guru, the Pir, will vouch (for one) only if one does not eat carrion.
No one goes to paradise by talk; one is saved by practising truth.
Put spices into what is forbidden, and it still does not become lawful.
O Nanak, by false talk only falsehood is gained. ॥2॥
141.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The prayers are five, their times are five, and the five have five names.
(Let) the first be truth, the second lawful earning, the third (asking) God for the good of all;
the fourth a clean intention and mind, the fifth the praise and glory (of God).
Reciting the kalma of good conduct, one may then call oneself a Muslim.
O Nanak, as many as are false (to these), the honour of the false is false. ॥3॥
141.3: Some trade in jewels and precious things, some deal in glass.
When the True Guru is pleased, the stores of jewels within are found.
Without the Guru no one has found them; the blind, the false, have died barking (from door to door).
The manmukhs have rotted away in duality and died; they do not understand (true) reflection.
Apart from the One there is no other; before whom can they cry out?
Some, without wealth, are ever barking (from door to door); the coffers of some are full.
Without the Name there is no other wealth; all the rest is poison (of Maya), mere ashes.
O Nanak, (the Lord) himself causes (all) to be done and himself does (all); by his Hukam he sets (all) right. ॥7॥
141.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
To be called a Muslim is hard; if one truly is one, then let one be called a Muslim.
First of all, let him hold the faith dear, and, as a burnisher scrapes off rust, let his possessions go from him.
Becoming a Muslim under the guidance of the faith, let him put away the delusion of death and life.
Let him accept the Lord's will upon his head, hold the Creator (as the doer of all), and lose his self.
Then, O Nanak, if he is merciful to all beings, let him be called a Muslim. ॥1॥
141.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
If one forsakes lust, anger, falsehood and slander, gives up Maya and does away with pride;
if, giving up lust, he gives up attachment to woman, then amid the black stain (anjan) of Maya he finds the Immaculate (Lord);
if, giving up vanity and pride and the love of son and wife, giving up thirst and hope, he fixes his attention on the Lord (Ram),
(then,) O Nanak, the True One comes to dwell in the mind, and through the true Shabad he merges in the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
141.6: Kings, subjects, chiefs: none will remain.
Shops, cities and bazaars will fall by (his) Hukam.
The strong and handsome gateways the fool thinks his own.
Storehouses full of riches are emptied in an instant.
Arab horses, chariots, camels, elephants with their trappings,
gardens, lands, houses and homes: where are they, that (he thought) his own?
(Where are) the tents, the beds of woven tape, the screens of red satin?
O Nanak, the Giver alone is true, ever-abiding; he is recognised through his creation. ॥8॥
141.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Should the rivers become cows, and the springs turn to milk and ghee;
should the whole earth become sugar, and (my) soul rejoice every day;
should the mountain turn to gold and silver, set with diamonds and rubies:
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥1॥
142.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the eighteen loads (all plant life) became fruit, rich and melting in taste,
if the moon and the sun, both ever circling, were held still, and my seat became unshakeable,
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥2॥
142.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If pain were to strike my body, and the two ill-omened planets, Rahu (and Ketu, were set upon me),
if bloodthirsty kings were set over my head, and (your) love were shown (to me) in this form,
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥3॥
142.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If fire and frost were my clothing, and wind my food,
if the enchanting women of heaven were (mine) — O Nanak, all of it must pass away —
even then it is you I would praise, and my longing to speak (your praise) would never wane. ॥4॥
142.4: One who does evil in secret does not know the Master (to be present);
he is called mad, (for) he does not know his own self.
Strife is an evil thing in the world; in quarrelling one wastes away.
Without the Name, one is consumed in evil and in wandering doubt.
There are two paths; the one who knows the One will come through.
The speaker of kufr (falsehood) will burn, sunk in his kufr.
The whole world is glorious and wondrous if one is merged in the True One;
one comes through at (the Lord's) door, in (his) court, if one sheds the self. ॥9॥
142.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
He alone has lived in whose mind that (Lord) dwells;
O Nanak, no one else (truly) lives.
If (one empty of the Name) lives at all, he goes with his honour stripped from him;
all that he eats is forbidden.
His delight is in power, his delight in wealth;
steeped in that delight, he dances without shame.
O Nanak, he is cheated and plundered;
without the Name, he has lost his honour and gone. ॥1॥
142.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What comes of eating (rich food), what of wearing (fine clothes),
when that True One is not in the mind?
What are dried fruits, what is ghee and sweet gur, what fine flour, what meat?
What are clothes, what a soft bed, and the pleasures and delights enjoyed (on it)?
What are armies, what mace-bearers and attendants, and coming to dwell in palaces?
O Nanak, without the True Name, all this array is perishable. ॥2॥
142.7: What lies in the hands of caste? It is truth that is assayed.
If poison is in the hand, one dies on tasting it (whatever one's caste).
The rule of the True One is known (to be so) in every age.
One who obeys (his) Hukam is a chief at (his) door, in (his) court.
Obeying the command is the task for which the Master has sent (us into the world).
The drummer (the Guru) has sounded this thought through the Shabad.
Some have mounted, some have saddled (their horses);
some have tied up their loads, some have galloped away. ॥10॥
142.8: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When (the crop) ripened, it was cut; only the stubble and the hedge were left standing.
Bearded ears and all, it was threshed, and the grain was taken out by winnowing away the straw.
Setting together the two stones of the mill, (people) came and sat down to grind.
Those (grains) that stayed at the door (of the mill) were saved; O Nanak, a marvel has been seen. ॥1॥
142.9: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
See how the sweet (cane) is cut down; cut and stripped, it is bound with ropes into bundles.
Laying it between the press's wooden rollers, strong men deal out (as it were) its punishment.
The juice pressed out is poured into the cauldron; it heats and (as it were) wails.
Even the crushed pulp is gathered up and burnt in the fire (beneath the cauldron).
Says Nanak, for sweetness one is brought to ruin (like this); come, people, and see. ॥2॥
143.1: Some do not keep death in mind; their hopes are many.
Day after day they die and are born again, and belong to no one.
In their own mind and heart they call themselves good;
(but) the King of Death keeps those manmukhs in his sight, day after day.
The manmukhs are false to the salt they eat; they have not known what (the Lord has done for them).
They bow only under constraint, and so do not please the Master.
The one who meets the True One, with the Name on his lips, will please the Master;
(all) will salute him on his throne; he will receive what was written (for him). ॥11॥
143.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What harm can water too deep to stand in do a fish? What harm can the sky do a bird?
What harm can frost do a stone? What does married home life mean to a eunuch?
Smear a dog with sandalwood, and its nature is still a dog's.
If a deaf man is instructed, and the Simritis are recited (to him),
if a blind man is kept in the light, with fifty lamps burning,
if gold is laid before a grazing herd, it still picks out the grass and eats it,
if iron is put (in the fire) to be reduced to calx, it melts, but it does not turn into cotton:
O Nanak, such are the ways of a fool; whenever he speaks, it is ever to (someone's) harm. ॥1॥
143.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If bronze or gold or iron cracks,
the smith joins it again with fire.
If a husband breaks with his wife,
in the world the bond is formed again through sons.
The king makes his demand; when it is given, the bond is formed.
For the hungry, the bond (with life) is formed when they eat.
Famines are mended by rivers in spate and pouring rain.
The bond of love is formed by sweet words.
One is bound to the Vedas (the scriptures) when one speaks the truth.
The dead stay bound (to the world) by the good and the charity (they did).
By such bonds the world goes on.
For a fool, the bond is formed by blows to his face.
through praise (of the Lord), the bond is formed at his court. ॥2॥
143.4: God himself fashions the creation, and himself takes thought (for it).
Some are counterfeit, some genuine; he himself is the one who assays.
The genuine go into (his) treasury; the counterfeit are cast outside.
The counterfeit are flung out of the True Court; to whom can they cry out?
If they run and fall in behind the True Guru, that is the excellent course.
The True Guru makes the counterfeit genuine; through the Shabad he sets (them) right.
Through love and devotion for the Guru, (they) are accepted in the True Court.
What reckoning can anyone make of those whom the Creator himself has forgiven? ॥12॥
143.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The whole world, pirs, sheikhs and rajas, (all go) beneath the earth;
emperors pass away; God alone abides, ever greater.
143.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Neither gods nor demons nor men,
nor Siddhas nor seekers (stay) on the earth.
The One alone is; who else is there?
144.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
nor the seven (nether worlds) under the earth (endure).
The One alone is; who else is there?
144.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the sphere of the heavens,
nor the seven continents, nor the waters,
nor food nor wind: none of them is lasting.
144.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Sustenance lies in no one's hand (but yours);
for all, hope in the One is enough.
The One alone is; who else is there?
144.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Birds have no gold tied in a knot of cloth;
they look in hope to the trees and the water;
144.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, what is inscribed on the brow
He alone puts power (into beings), and he alone takes it away.
144.6: (O Lord,) your Hukam is true and abiding; it is known through the Guru.
By the Guru's teaching, shedding the self, the True One is recognised.
True is your court; the Shabad is the pass (that admits one there).
Reflecting on the true Shabad, (the Gurmukhs) merge in the True One.
The manmukhs ever deal in falsehood, gone astray in doubt.
Their dwelling is in filth; they have never known the relish (of the Name).
Without the Name, they come and go in pain.
O Nanak, the Assayer is (the Lord) himself, who has told the counterfeit from the genuine. ॥13॥
144.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Lions, hawks, falcons and kuhi hawks: these (God, if he wills,) feeds on grass;
those who eat grass he feeds on meat: such are the ways he sets going.
He brings sandbanks into view in the midst of rivers, and turns dry plains into bottomless waters.
He sets a worm upon a throne, and turns armies to ashes.
All the beings that live, live by drawing breath; (but if) he keeps (one) alive, what (need is there) of breath?
O Nanak, just as it pleases the True One, so he gives (each) its morsel. ॥1॥
144.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Some feed on flesh, some eat grass;
some receive the thirty-six (kinds of) nectar-sweet foods;
some, dwelling in the earth, eat earth;
some, the counters of breath (who practise pranayama), are bent on counting their breaths;
some, devoted to the Formless One, rest on the support of the Name.
The Giver lives on; no one dies (for want of food).
O Nanak, they are robbed in whose mind he does not dwell. ॥2॥
144.9: The work the Perfect Guru sets is done only through (God's) grace.
Through the Guru's teaching one sheds self-conceit and meditates on the Naam.
Taken up with any other work, one wastes one's life.
Without the Name, whatever one wears and eats is all poison.
Praising the True Shabad, one merges in the True One.
Without serving the True Guru there is no dwelling in peace; one comes (into birth) again and again.
The world is counterfeit capital; (trading with it) one earns falsehood alone.
O Nanak, praising the True One, the genuine, one departs with honour. ॥14॥
144.10: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) if it pleases you, (beings) play music and sing; if it pleases you, they bathe in (holy) waters.
When it pleases you, they smear (their bodies with) ashes and sound the call of the horn (singi).
When it pleases you, they read the Kateb and are called mullahs and sheikhs.
When it pleases you, they become kings and enjoy flavours of every kind in plenty.
When it pleases you, they wield the sword, and heads are severed from necks.
When it pleases you, they go to foreign lands, and hearing (their) news, come back home.
When it pleases you, they are absorbed in the Name; those who walk in your will are dear to you.
Nanak offers one prayer: all the others practise only falsehood. ॥1॥
145.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) since you are great, all greatness is (yours); from the good, only good comes.
Since you are true, everyone is true; no one at all is false.
Speaking, seeing, talking, walking, living and dying: (all this is the spread of) Maya.
Having fashioned his Hukam, he keeps (all) within the Hukam; O Nanak, (it is) the True One himself (who does so). ॥2॥
145.2: Serving the True Guru without reserve, one dispels doubt.
The work the True Guru bids is the work to be done.
When the True Guru is merciful, the Naam is meditated on.
The profit of devotion is the highest (profit), and it is found through the Guru.
As a manmukh, one lives in falsehood and darkness, and earns falsehood alone.
Going to the door of the True One, one utters the Truth (the True Name).
(Then,) through the Truth, one is called within the mansion of the True One.
O Nanak, one who ever holds fast to the Truth is truthful, and merges in the True One. ॥15॥
145.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Kalyug is a knife, kings are butchers; dharma has grown wings and flown away.
Falsehood is the dark night of the new moon; the moon of truth is not seen to have risen anywhere.
I have searched (for it) until I am bewildered;
in the darkness no path is (to be seen).
Caught in Haumai, (the world) weeps over its pain.
Says Nanak, by what means can (it) be set free? ॥1॥
145.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Kalyug, (the Lord's) praise is the light shining forth in the world.
(But) only some rare one crosses over (the darkness) through the Guru.
The one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace, to him he gives (this light);
O Nanak, through the Guru that one receives the jewel (of the Name). ॥2॥
145.5: Between the devotees and the worldly there has never been a match.
The Creator himself makes no mistake; no one can lead him into error.
The devotees he has himself united (with him), who have practised truth and truth alone.
The worldly he has himself led astray, who, speaking falsehood again and again, have eaten poison.
They do not grasp that they must depart; they have let the poison of lust and anger grow.
The devotees serve the Lord, who have meditated on the Naam night and day.
Those who, becoming the servants of (his) servants, have rid themselves of self from within,
at the Master's door their faces are bright; the True Shabad has made them beautiful. ॥16॥
145.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who in the early morning praised (the Lord) and meditated on (him) with a single mind:
they alone are the perfect shahs (the truly rich), who at the proper hour fought (their own mind) unto death.
In the second (watch) many paths (open), and the mind's thoughts are scattered.
Many fall into the fathomless (sea of the world); they go under and cannot get out.
In the third (watch) morsels go into mouths; hunger and thirst both bark (for more).
What is eaten turns to ash, yet the friendship with eating (remains).
In the fourth (watch) drowsiness comes; shutting his eyes, (man) passes as if into the other world (of deep sleep).
Rising again, he starts up the strife, (as though) he had marked out an arena for a hundred years (of life).
Every hour and every moment (is blessed), if through all eight watches there is the fear (of God).
O Nanak, (if) the Master dwells in the mind, (that) is the true bathing. ॥1॥
146.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
They alone are the perfect shahs who have found the Perfect One.
Through all eight watches they stay free of care, (dyed) in the love of the One.
Rare are those found (absorbed) in the sight and the form of the Unfathomable.
By perfect grace (one meets) the Perfect Guru, whose word is perfect.
O Nanak, if the Perfect One makes (someone) perfect, (that one's) weight does not fall short. ॥2॥
146.2: (O Lord,) when you are (mine), what need have I of anyone else? I tell the truth.
(But the soul-bride) robbed by the thief of worldly affairs does not find (the Lord's) mansion.
Because of this hard heart, (her) service is wasted.
The body in which the Truth is not found is broken and shaped (again and again).
How can (it) weigh true in the balance against the full weight?
No one calls (it) short, if Haumai is gone (from within).
The genuine, once assayed, are taken in at the door of the All-seeing One.
This merchandise is had at one shop alone: from the Perfect Guru. ॥17॥
146.3: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The eight watches are eight parts (of time); the ninth part is the body.
In it is the one Naam, the nine treasures; (the fortunate) seek (there) the Lord, deep in virtues.
The fortunate have praised (him), O Nanak, taking the Guru as their pir.
In the fourth watch, as morning nears, a longing wells up in those whose awareness is awake.
Their friendship is with the rivers (of the holy company), and the True Name is in their mind and on their lips.
There the Amrit (of the Name) is shared out; by (his) grace the gift is received.
The body, (like) gold, is tried on the touchstone, and takes on a fine lustre.
If the Assayer's glance of grace is on it, it is not put to the fire again.
In the (other) seven watches, truthful living is good, and one should sit with the learned.
There (in their company) sin and virtue are weighed, and the capital of falsehood runs down.
There the counterfeit are thrown out, and the genuine are praised.
To speak (of one's woes) is idle, O Nanak; pain and pleasure are in the Master's hands. ॥1॥
146.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Air is the Guru, water the father, and the earth the great mother.
Day and night are the two nurses, the female and the male; the whole world plays (in their care).
In (God's) presence, Dharam (Raj) reads out the good deeds and the bad.
By their own deeds, some are near (God) and some far.
Those who meditated on the Naam have gone, their toil accomplished.
O Nanak, their faces are bright, and many others have been set free along with them. ॥2॥
146.5: The True Guru has shown that love (for the Lord) is the true food.
(One who takes this food) is content in the True One alone, and blossoms in the True One.
In the true fortress, the true village, in his own home, he dwells.
Through the True Guru's favour (comes) the Name, and one rejoices in (the Lord's) love.
No one reaches the court of the True One by falsehood.
Uttering lie upon lie, one loses that mansion.
With the True Shabad as one's pass, no barrier is met (on the way).
Hearing, understanding and uttering the Truth, one is called into (the Lord's) mansion. ॥18॥
147.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If I were to wear fire, build my house in snow, and make iron my food;
if I drank down all sorrows like water, and moved the earth at my call;
if I set the sky on a balance and weighed it, with a tank (a tiny weight) on the other pan;
if I grew so vast that I could not be contained, and led everyone by a nose-string;
if there were such power in my mind that I could do (anything) myself and have it done at my word:
as great as the Master is, so great are his gifts; (were) the Lord of the Will to give and give (me all this, it would still be little).
O Nanak, the one on whom he casts his glance of grace has glory through the True Name. ॥1॥
147.2: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The mouth has never had its fill of speaking, nor the ears of hearing.
The eyes have never had their fill of seeing; (each sense) is a buyer of one kind of quality alone.
The hunger of the hungry does not leave them; hunger is not ended by talk.
O Nanak, the hungry one is sated only when, uttering (the Lord's) virtues, he merges in the Virtuous One. ॥2॥
147.3: Without the True One, all is false; only falsehood is earned.
Without the True One, the dealer in falsehood is tied up and led away.
Without the True One, the body is ash, and to ash it returns.
Without the True One, all that one wears and eats only (feeds) hunger.
Without the True One, through falsehood, (his) court is not reached.
Clinging to false greed, one loses (the Lord's) mansion.
The whole world has been cheated by the cheat (falsehood); (so) one comes and goes.
The fire of craving in the body is put out through the Shabad. ॥19॥
147.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Guru is the tree of contentment; dharma is its blossom, and divine knowledge its fruit.
Full of the sap (of love), it stays ever green; through (God's) grace and meditation (its fruit) ripens.
One who eats (it) tastes the delights of (union with) the Husband (Lord); (this) is the gift above all gifts. ॥1॥
147.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The Guru is) a golden tree: its leaves are coral, its flowers jewels and rubies;
on it grow fruits of gems, the words spoken by (his) mouth; in his heart of hearts he is in bliss.
O Nanak, (the one) on whom there is (God's) grace, and on whose face and forehead (such) destiny is written:
(for that one) the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are in the Guru's feet, and he worships them ever as the highest.
Cruelty, attachment, greed and anger: all four are streams of fire.
(Those who) fall in burn, O Nanak; by (God's) grace, clinging (to the Guru's feet), one crosses over. ॥2॥
147.6: Die while you are alive; killing (craving) so, one has no regrets (at the end).
False is this world; only a rare one has grasped (it).
(Man) does not set his love on the True One, and runs after worldly affairs.
(Yet) cruel death, death the destroyer, hangs over the head of the world.
By (the Lord's) Hukam, Jandar (the brute, Death's messenger) stands over (each) head, and strikes when his chance comes.
(God) himself gives (his) love, and (then) it is enshrined in the mind.
Not a moment, not an instant's delay (is allowed) when (life's) measure is full.
By the Guru's grace, understanding (this), one merges in the True One. ॥20॥
147.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The bitter gourd and the colocynth, poison, the swallow-wort, the thorn-apple and the neem fruit:
(O Lord,) these (bitter things) dwell in the mind and in the mouth of the one into whose thoughts you do not come.
O Nanak, to whom can (their state) be told? Bereft of (God's) grace, they wander about. ॥1॥
147.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The intellect is a bird; with its past deeds (kirat) beside it, it is now high, now low.
Now it perches on the sandalwood tree, now on a branch of the swallow-wort, and now (there is in it) a lofty love (for God).
O Nanak, (all) are made to move by (his) Hukam; this has been the Master's way (from the first). ॥2॥
148.1: Countless people give their accounts (of God), and having told and told, they depart.
The Vedas give their expositions, (yet) his limit cannot be found.
By reading, his secret is not found; it is found when understanding dawns.
Through the garb of the six orders (khat darshan), who has merged in the True One?
The True Being is beyond seeing; through the Shabad he becomes lovely (to the mind).
The one who has faith in the Name of the Countless One reaches (his) court.
He bows to the Creator, and as a minstrel he sings (his praise).
O Nanak, he enshrines in his mind the One who is in every age. ॥21॥
148.2: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
One who knows only the charm for scorpions, yet goes and lays hold of snakes,
sets a firebrand to himself with his own hands.
The Master's Hukam has gone forth from the very first: through overreaching, one is struck down.
The manmukh who sets himself against the Gurmukh drowns by (the Lord's) true justice.
Over both sides the Master himself (stands); he watches and judges between them.
O Nanak, know it so: everything is (done) in his Will. ॥1॥
148.3: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
O Nanak, if one assays oneself, then know (that one) to be an assayer.
One who knows both the illness and its remedy is a wise physician.
Such a one starts no quarrels on the road (of life), knowing himself a guest (here).
He speaks knowing the Root (of all), and brings harm upon what harms (him, the vices).
One who does not walk by greed and abides in the Truth: that go-between is accepted.
(If someone) aims an arrow at the sky, how can the shaft reach (it)?
It lies beyond, out of reach; know that (the arrow falls back on) the archer. ॥2॥
148.4: The soul-brides who love their Husband are adorned with love.
They worship day and night, and do not stop, though held back.
Made beautiful by the Shabad, they dwell in the (Lord's) mansion.
Thoughtful, they offer a true prayer.
Having come by his Hukam, they look beautiful beside the Master.
As his companions they make their prayer, loving (him) with all their heart.
Without the Name, cursed is the dwelling (in the world), and shame on such a life.
She whom he has adorned through the Shabad has drunk the Amrit (of the Name). ॥22॥
148.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The desert is never sated by rain, and the hunger of fire never leaves it.
No king was ever sated by his kingdom; and who has ever filled up the oceans?
O Nanak, what need to ask how great the longing for the True Name is? (It never ends.) ॥1॥
148.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Fruitless is the birth of that one, so long as he does not know Brahm (God).
By the Guru's grace many cross over the ocean of the world.
(God) is the Cause of creation, all-powerful: says Nanak, after reflection,
the cause (of all) is in the power of the Creator, who has established his power (in all creation). ॥2॥
148.7: The minstrel has come to dwell at the Master's court.
Praising the True Master, the lotus (of his heart) has blossomed.
Receiving the full (station) from the Master, he is glad at heart.
He has struck down and driven out his foes (the vices), and his friends rejoice.
Those who serve the True Guru: (he) has shown them the true path.
Reflecting on the true Shabad, they have destroyed (the fear of) death.
Made beautiful by the Shabad, the minstrel tells of the One beyond telling.
O Nanak, gathering the capital of virtues, he has met the beloved Lord. ॥23॥
149.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Born of wrongs, they commit wrongs, and so they sink (ever deeper) into wrongs.
These do not come off at all with washing, though they try a hundred washings.
O Nanak, if (God) pardons, they are pardoned; otherwise they are beaten with shoes. ॥1॥
149.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, it is idle prattle to ask for comforts and leave out pains.
Comfort and pain are both robes (given) at (the Lord's) door, which human beings come (into the world) and wear.
Where speaking only ends in defeat, there silence is best. ॥2॥
149.3: Having looked in all four directions, I searched my own self within,
(and saw that) the True Being, the Unseen, has created (the world) and watches over it.
To one lost in the wilderness, the Guru showed the way.
Wonderful is the True Guru, the true one, (through whom) the True One is cherished (in the heart).
The jewel (of the Name) was found within the house itself, (when the Guru) lit the lamp (of wisdom).
Those who hold to the Truth praise (God) through the true Shabad and are at peace.
Those without fear (of God) are seized by fear; they waste away in their pride.
Strayed from the Name, the world wanders about out of step. ॥24॥
149.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The world) is born in fear and dies in fear, and fear stays ever in its mind.
O Nanak, whoever dies in the fear (of God): that one's coming (into the world) is blessed. ॥1॥
149.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One may live long, very long, without the fear (of God), and enjoy pleasure upon pleasure;
(yet) O Nanak, if one dies without the fear (of God), one rises and departs with a blackened face. ॥2॥
149.6: When the True Guru is merciful, faith is made whole.
When the True Guru is merciful, one never grieves.
When the True Guru is merciful, pain is not known at all.
When the True Guru is merciful, the Lord's love is enjoyed.
When the True Guru is merciful, what fear of Jam can there be?
When the True Guru is merciful, the body is at peace for ever.
When the True Guru is merciful, one finds the nine treasures.
When the True Guru is merciful, one merges in the True One. ॥25॥
149.7: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
They have the hair of their heads plucked out, drink dirty water, and beg and eat others' leavings.
They stir their excrement and breathe its stench, and shrink at the sight of water.
Like sheep, they have their heads plucked, and the hands (that pluck them) are filled with ash.
They throw away the work of their mothers and fathers (earning a living), and their families wail aloud.
For them there is no pind, no pattal, no kiria, no lamp; once dead, who knows where they are cast?
The sixty-eight tiraths give them no shelter, and Brahmins do not eat their food.
Day and night they stay ever unclean, with no tikka on the brow.
They sit with heads ever bowed, as if mourning a death, and go to no gathering or assembly.
Bowls hang at their waists and whisks are in their hands, and they walk in single file.
They are neither yogis nor jangams, neither qazis nor mullas.
Ruined by God, they wander in disgrace, and the whole flock roams accursed.
He alone kills living beings and brings them to life; no one else can protect (them).
They are cut off from giving and from bathing; ashes fall on their plucked heads.
It was from water that the jewels came forth, when Meru was made the churning stick.
The gods set up the sixty-eight tiraths (by the waters), where the holy days draw crowds and the sacred word is recited.
Having bathed, one says the namaz; having bathed, one worships; the wise bathe always.
In death and in life, one is made clean when water is poured over the head.
O Nanak, these hair-plucked ones are perverse (shaitani); the matter (of bathing) does not please them.
When the rain falls there is gladness; the very life of all beings rests in it.
When the rain falls, grain, sugarcane and cotton (grow), and cotton covers everyone.
When the rain falls, the cows graze on grass every day, and the woman (of the house) churns the curd.
With that ghee the hom, the yagya and worship are ever performed; with it added, every rite is graced.
The Guru is the ocean, and his teaching all the rivers: bathing in it, one gains glory.
O Nanak, if the hair-plucked ones do not bathe (in it), then seven handfuls of ash (fall) on their heads. ॥1॥
150.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
What can cold do to fire? What can night do to the sun?
What can darkness do to the moon? What can caste do to air and water?
What can things do to the earth, in which everything comes to be?
O Nanak, honour is known (as true) only when he himself keeps (one's) honour. ॥2॥
150.2: O True One, I have ever praised you as Subhan (the Wondrous).
You are the true Ruler (Diwan); all others come and go.
Those who ask (of you) the gift of Truth become like you.
True is your command; through the Shabad it is beautiful (to them).
By obeying (your command), wisdom and meditation are received from you.
By (your) grace the mark (of approval) is set, which no one can remove.
You are the true Giver; you give every day, and ever more and more.
Nanak begs for the gift that pleases you. ॥26॥
150.3: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Those whom (the Guru) has given understanding by imparting his teaching, and merged in the True One through praise:
what (further) teaching can be given to those whose Guru is Nanak Dev? ॥1॥
150.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Only the one whom he himself gives understanding understands.
The one to whom he himself gives sight sees everything.
One who talks and talks in discourse only wrangles over Maya.
By his Hukam he makes all forms.
He himself knows what is in the thoughts of all.
O Nanak, the Word is his own utterance.
The doubt of the one who receives (this) gift is removed. ॥2॥
150.5: I was a minstrel with no work; (the Lord) set me to (his) work.
From the very first he commanded: Night or day, sing (my) vaar (of praise).
The Master called the minstrel into his true mansion.
He robed (me) in the robe of honour of his true praise.
The true, ambrosial Name came to (me) as food.
Whoever, by the Guru's teaching, has eaten (of it) to the full has found peace.
The minstrel shares (this) blessing (with all), and has made the Shabad resound.
Praising the True One, Nanak has found the Perfect (Lord).
